Section: MicroScenarios contract and shared host > Schema 2: complete apparatus presentation and existing-field inspection
**Current source:** schema 2 is opt-in. Schema-1 definitions, canonical hashes, legacy Tower/Water recipes and their controls remain unchanged. It adds exactly one required `presentation` record: `title`, `instructions`, `duration_ticks`, `baseline`, `profile`, `regions`. Text is bounded (128 characters for title and identity labels, 4096 instructions); duration is 1..3600 completed ticks. At most 12 unique named regions carry an in-world rectangle and a label of at most 96 characters. Presentation never changes native physics. The ancestral recipe hash is distinct from the complete definition hash and from the executing build. A schema-2 `cell_state` observation is exactly one cell. It returns copied stored material/state, raw temperature availability, body-mask identity and chunk/block coordinates through the [exclusive-owner native query](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#read-only-native-microscenario-inspection). It cannot be used as a scalar condition. Raw temperature is not a calibrated heat solver; masked temperature is unavailable, not falsely reported ambient. There is no entity census or per-cell awake flag. New capabilities require the rebuilt adapter: a stale runtime is rejected **before** replacing the previous world. No event type or capacity is added. In particular, a scheduled Water fill must have positive normalized mass; zero-mass fills are now rejected during pure validation because native already rejects them. Use an explicit erase for a sink. Initial partial-fill semantics and historical valid definitions are unchanged. The common workbench displays all declared probes (including pending ones), all retained results, complete identities, effective profiles, bounded native work statistics and instructions. Its A/B slots hold two independent validated complete definitions and at most one capture per slot. **Every load is a fresh reset** via the existing acknowledged desktop or synchronous Web owner. Invalid edits preserve the active world and slots; no parameter is written into a live worker. Matching runtime/tick/seed is necessary, not sufficient to claim matched organic brush input. Blind sessions disable these definition/capture routes exactly as before. **Run declared window** sends one existing single-step command at a time and waits for its owner acknowledgement, stopping at the declared completed tick. It is bounded by 3600; pause changes, any accepted reset (including the same definition), quarantine, opening the definition editor, or missing owner acknowledgement cancels it without retry/catch-up. At most one already-admitted step may complete while a modal opens. This is neither a recurring native event nor another physics loop. F8 hides labels, dialogs, help and optional telemetry across later status refreshes. Generic controls show only admitted tools. Material selection and the circle/square/rectangle brush geometry controls use the existing owner command boundary; brush shape, pixel size, rectangle ratio/orientation and effective secondary material are **exploratory UI/tool state, not fields

Section: MicroScenarios contract and shared host > Ownership, reset and failure
`CyberMicroScenarioHost` belongs to the **existing** mutable World owner: the GDScript simulation thread on desktop, the synchronous main-thread owner on Web, or the explicitly native-only headless runner. Native pool workers still call no Godot APIs. The host never owns live Rapier scene objects or mutable render storage. `install` validates and resolves the complete candidate before calling the existing native candidate-and-swap builder. On rejection the old World, scheduled cursor and retained observations remain intact. Accepted reset creates a fresh paused world, clears prior schedules/observations and retains only declared recipe, mode and selection state. Main-thread desktop acknowledgement waits for the new immutable summary before changing the active UI. Pending reset cannot be replaced by a new generic step/capture command. Explicitly choosing Tower/Water can cancel that pending selection through their existing reset path. Both controllers call the same `before_tick`/`after_tick` host around their existing physics order. Desktop character-before-cell and Web character-after-cell order are **not** silently unified. Headless `advance` has neither character nor Rapier. A missed event/observation or skipped completed-tick boundary latches a visible host fault instead of catching up. Native failure remains native quarantine; no partial native observation is exported as success, and no automatic retry occurs. Only a fresh admitted reset clears the fault. Definitions, summaries and captures are copied values. Desktop capture is requested at the owner boundary and frozen recursively once before publication; a retained record can be shared by successive snapshots without mutable nested dictionaries or a large per-frame definition copy. The consumer never reads the worker's World. This does not claim that the pre-existing general input queue is now bounded.

Each ornate construction uses the same prevalidated native install/reset boundary. Above/Below selects a fresh authored tile through that owner; viewpoint changes preserve its state. There are no scheduled events, observation conditions, native ABI changes or additional loops. The separate [Blacksite Nine](blacksite-nine-demo.md) consumer registers one `showcase/blacksite-nine` definition for the complete connected 3×3 map. Nine presentation regions describe its camera tiles; twelve reciprocal openings are ordinary Empty geometry in one native world. Its explicit reset reinstalls the entire complex through the existing owner boundary. A definition is JSON data, not executable code. `CyberMicroScenarioContract.base` provides a complete schema-1 template; `validate` checks in-memory data and `parse` checks bounded JSON. Unknown or missing fields, invalid types, fractional integer fields, non-finite numbers, out-of-world regions and capacity excess are rejected before native replacement. Integral JSON floats are normalized to integers, including validated transport settings, so canonical JSON round trips keep the same SHA-256. All root fields are required: | Fields | Meaning | |---|---| | `schema_version`, `id`, `recipe_version`, `seed`, `maturity` | Schema 1 or 2; stable ID; positive recipe version; 0..2147483647 seed; `exploratory` or existing `reference` baseline | | `rectangles` | Flat setup records `x,y,width,height,material`; current IDs 0..131 except reserved 10 | | `partial_water_fills` | Flat records `x,y,width,height,normalized_mass,coherence`; existing fractional Water setup, not a generalized fractional-liquid solver | | `transport_profile`, `water_semantics` | Existing validated transport profile and native Water packet `[1,mass_bits,coherence_ticks,0]`; mass3..8, coherence0..12 | | `player_start`, `camera_origin`, `player_enabled`, `body_enabled`, `tools` | Initial positions, existing character/body participation and admitted `paint`, `erase`, `player` tools; no new entity system | | `interest`, `execution` | Declared owner-controlled or fixed region and existing cadence/adhesion settings | | `events`, `observations`, `conditions` | Bounded ordered existing operations, read-only observations and objective/failure predicates | | `source_recipe`, `source_recipe_hash` | Ancestral recipe identity, distinct from the canonical full definition hash and actual runtime identity | | `presentation` (schema 2 only) | Required bounded title/instructions/duration/baseline/profile/region metadata; forbidden in schema 1 | Ordinary MicroScenario definitions use the finite 1024 by 1024 frame. Rectangles/fills must be wholly inside it, with positive dimensions. Limits are 4096 records per setup array; total rectangle write area at most eight world areas and partial-Water area at most one world area. Overlaps are intentional, ordered setup writes, not extra capacity. JSON is limited to 1 MiB. Seeds select the declared deterministic recipe; they do not introduce a new

Section: Simulation tick and threading > What happens when a tick fails or overloads?
**Current, chosen for issue #1:** a thrown tick latches `World::has_failed()`. There is no transactional rollback. Tick/epoch, accepted explosion edits, dirty metadata, chunk preparation and even earlier completed phases may already have changed. `tick_index()` identifies the attempted tick; `completed_tick_index()` advances only after successful execution and activity finalization. No partial `TickStats` is returned as success. See [ADR-010](../decisions/ADR-010-failed-tick-quarantine.md). Failure clears the in-progress guard after any dispatched phase has drained. Further ticks, gameplay writes, reservations and snapshot publication are rejected. Serialized reads remain diagnostic access to partial state, not a valid save or playable continuation. The last successful immutable lease remains usable. Accepted explosions apply in enqueue order at tick entry. A completed batch drains; if application itself throws, the retained batch may include applied or partial events. Neither batch is ever automatically replayed: the world cannot be retried. An explicit `clear()` discards cells, activity, pending events, masks and tick identity, retains construction options/latest requested region, and permits fresh setup. Destruction/reconstruction is the other native recovery path. No allocation failure, capacity change or camera move implicitly recovers a world. **Current desktop:** the exclusive GDScript owner checks native false, latches failure and publishes a fresh status wrapper around its previous valid publication. It withholds partial character, cell, terrain and body results, rejects new emissions and clears pending prototype emissions. The pacing thread stays alive to receive reset; main-thread Rapier stops when the failure status is observed. This is asynchronous notification, not rollback of Rapier or character work that preceded the fault. The fallback's void successful tick path is unchanged. **Current Web:** the synchronous owner pauses, opens the menu, reports restart/load recovery, and suppresses painting, ticks, terrain/render publication and further Rapier stepping while failed. Closing the menu or toggling pause cannot retry. Rapier's preceding step is not rolled back. Reset/restart or a validated saved-level replacement creates fresh activity and clears the fault; invalid import preserves it. The adapter returns `false` with first-error telemetry, zeroes unsuccessful tick statistics, exposes attempted/completed identity separately, and does not count rejected repeat calls as new failures. Its reset prepares a candidate before swap. Godot level export rejects failed state; CYSD1 replacement is level recovery, not exact replay. Region/configuration requests cannot wake or advance a failed World. Native region requests may be latched; the Waterwall adapter's stricter failed-setting admission is described below. **Rejected for this fix:** rollback, automatic retry, resuming partial state and silent event replay. **Planned separately:** state-preserving live capacity growth and complete replay. [Dated regression evidence](../audits/2026-09-08-issue-1-failed-ticks.md) separates source tests, Windows owners and browser coverage. Eligible native transport runs each tick;

Section: Materials Lab v1 > Manual evaluation checklist
- Open from the launcher and Shared Workbench; inspect Water, Sand, Slush, MoltenGlass and reserved 10. Confirm native/fallback/shadow distinctions and the origin of the copied solver policy. - Search for `23`, `powder`, `MoltenGlass` and a reaction partner; check physical and capability filters without implying semantic inheritance. - Create powder 132, change density/colour, validate and compile. Confirm no Runtime-active label and no production 132 in the browser. - Export/reimport the preset, then export a compiled bundle and import its `preset.json`. Tamper with a field/digest; require an actionable refusal and preservation of the current candidate. - Duplicate Salt, set threshold 0 and compare rolls 0/1 in the candidate and production resolver. Confirm explicit product-default effects. - Run Salt/Water for 120 ticks, read stored material/state, compare a clean reference, save/reopen the test and check one/four-worker agreement. - In **Try originals**, prepare a Water experiment with CellularYield and then PressureFlow. Inspect the applied settings, step the PressureFlow World, save it and reopen it to verify the selected model and native policy hash. - Duplicate Sand, set density500, compare both native Worlds against Water, inspect initial/final cells and export/reopen the World bundle. Edit settings while a compile runs and verify its older result cannot qualify the new recipe. - Cancel a compile and a reference replay; confirm the Lab stays usable and reports cancellation without a successful receipt. - Save/import a World recipe after changing placement, seed and workers; require exact restored controls, a validated state and a fresh compile before qualification. - Exercise Salt retention and a Metal state-B edit through **Run edited reaction**; check native registers/temperature and quantity evidence, not only the preview. - Select neighbouring native preview cells with left/right clicks, inspect a supplied roll, swap source/target and advance one step; the old contact report must retire and unobserved scheduling facts must remain labelled.

Section: Water design > How should I diagnose a shimmering pool?
**Current diagnostic:** compare exact Water mass, `World::content_hash()`, and dirty/activity observations before treating shimmer as a fluid bug. If authority is stable while the pool visibly changes, inspect its shader, presentation-time animation, and render-only dither. If a closed pure-Water fixture loses mass or continues changing cell content after its rest criterion, investigate simulation transfers, conversions, or waking. Appearance alone cannot decide which path failed. Water coverage dither derives from stable world coordinates and mass; it cannot mutate authoritative cells or wake the simulation. `transfer_water` conserves exact integer mass for each Water pair. A closed pure-Water fixture must preserve the exact total every tick, including sleep, wake, and boundary crossings. Current native quantity ledgers additionally book explicit Water sources/sinks from edits, generation, events, kernels and registered reactions, with overfill and in-flight terms where enabled. That bookkeeping does not claim universal physical mass conservation across all species or change legacy chemistry. For the original FreeMass fixture, use `World::content_hash()` to observe rest: it includes material/state/ temperature at meaningful coordinates and excludes tick/epoch/activity. `state_hash()` includes advancing tick and update epoch plus additional scheduler state, so it is expected to change during otherwise resting ticks. Compare state hashes at matching ticks/configurations for supported fixture parity; neither hash is a complete replay checkpoint. [Native tests](../../native/tests/test_world.cpp) provide explicit bounds: - `test_conserved_water_levels_and_sleeps`: four-worker phased fixture, 48×255 initial mass, at most 2,000 ticks to reach 40 unchanged content hashes, then 40 further mass/rest checks and zero active chunks. - `test_water_surface_column_mass_is_level`: settled column-mass difference at most 8/255 of a cell. - `test_water_conserves_across_storage_boundaries`: exact boundary conservation. These are fixture bounds, not universal settling-time guarantees. Additional mirrored, shifted, mixed-material, and every-direction edge cases remain needed.

Section: Scalable soliding representation lifecycle > What is implemented, and what is the approved direction?
**Approved requirement:** [issue #12](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/12) requires both cheaper representation of quiescent regions and useful coherent-body macro dynamics followed by fracture into coherent children and local loose material. These purposes are co-equal. The historical [PR #23](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/pull/23) and its ADR-012 are a one-slot Phase 0 proof, not production soliding or completion of this programme. They remain on their original source identity. **Current runtime:** World owns cellular material. Ordinary scheduler sleep, immutable copied snapshots, main-thread Rapier ownership, failed-world quarantine and interest-region pause/re-entry keep their existing contracts. Main has no production aggregate registry or representation handoff from this document. The Current ownership and collision contracts remain [ownership](data-ownership-and-lifetimes.md) and [coupling](rigid-body-and-cellular-coupling.md). Accepted source also contains disabled-by-default, read-only [settled-region discovery](../systems/settled-region-discovery.md), including World producer hooks, bounded tile observations and optional connectivity. `World::settled_discovery_tile` and `World::settled_region` return copied observations. This is implemented discovery, not a production connection of the representation-transfer model below. The unmerged ObjectShard programme has its own [current-state boundary](../reference/status-and-roadmap.md#active-candidates-and-integration-boundaries). **Current standalone contract model:** [`soliding_lifecycle.hpp`](../../native/include/cybersand/soliding_lifecycle.hpp) implements bounded slot identities, synthetic exact payload accounting, staged ownership transfers, refusal/cancel/quarantine and observation witnesses. It has no dependency on World, Godot, Rapier, adapters, runtime queues or save code. [`test_soliding_lifecycle.cpp`](../../native/tests/test_soliding_lifecycle.cpp) exercises that model. Passing these tests does not implement any runtime tier, prove thread safety, choose a stationary representation, or establish conservation of physical energy. Model arrays are copied synthetic membership records, not a second canonical copy of live World cells. **Planned runtime:** each state, reservation, material admission and fence below must be connected to its actual native/main-thread owner and revalidated before promotion becomes possible. Existing read-only discovery keeps cells as sole authority; it must not treat this model as runtime admission for acceleration or ownership transfer.

Section: Water hybrid, saturated-head and compartment-pressure extension programme > Core hypothesis: generic hybrid soliding may supply part of the missing bulk response > Precise sheet concept
The intended proof is **not**: - one monolithic solid Water core; - rigidifying an entire reservoir; - repeating lamination throughout the full depth; - one reservoir-spanning unbreakable plate; - a Water-specific second rigid-body engine. The intended candidate is approximately: - zero sheets for shallow Water; - at most roughly **3-5 tiers** for very deep Water; - tiers concentrated in the **upper volume**, while preserving a few cellular layers at the actual free surface; - each tier made of bounded/segmented local carriers rather than one unbounded slab; - tier count or eligibility derived conservatively from local depth/support; - promotion/demotion performed through the same generic hybrid ownership machinery used by other solided material; - aggressive split/desolid behavior around unsupported edges, rapidly changing surfaces, constrictions, excessive rotation, topology change or invalid support. The intended coarse mechanism is: `depth -> eligible tier count/load -> Rapier gravity/contact -> cellular displacement -> outward surge`. Three useful qualitative tiers may be enough; the ceiling exists to keep both cost and mechanical influence bounded.

Section: Rigid-body and cellular coupling > What are the current numerical bounds and units?
Body centres/sizes/corrections use cell/pixel coordinates; rotation is radians, linear velocity is pixels per second, angular velocity is radians per second. Mass and returned central impulses use the Godot physics adapter's quantities; there is no approved production SI calibration or generalized force/torque unit contract. Packed fields are documented in [interfaces](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md). | Operation | Current bound or response | |---|---| | Translation sweep | More than 32 pixels between samples is treated as a teleport: endpoint only | | Sweep sampling | Approximately one-cell spacing, capped at 24 intervals/25 samples; interpolates centre, shortest rotation and size | | Endpoint overlap | Search outward from nearest face and along its tangent, at most eight cells; the bounded half-cell path may not cross hard terrain or another body's transient mask | | Swept-only overlap | Prefer ejection in body-travel direction; rotational response remains approximate | | No valid destination | Retain the complete stored cell payload and report unresolved overlap plus reaction; no particle fallback or silent deletion | | Granular bearing | Exposed downward body cells query the version-1 granular support predicate against stored material; response is recomputed each accepted sample, capped at 20 impulse units and uses at most 0.5-cell low-speed correction | | Native impulse | Contact/displacement/density pressure terms retain the ordinary cap; the bounded bearing term shares the cellular coupling owner rather than becoming a second collider/solver | | Stale results | Reject age above eight body samples; suppress correction above one; scale impulse by `1/(1+0.25*age)` | Ejection transfers the compact cell state including Water mass. Pure closed Water conservation does not establish general body/cell energy conservation. Duplicate sample serials are not applied twice. Sample wrap and age constants are in [Rapier `apply_cellular_results`](../../godot/scripts/rapier_physics_bridge.gd). Packed rotation is `Transform2D.get_rotation()`, a float32 `atan2` from the platform libm, stored in `PackedFloat32Array`. Native rasterization then uses double `std::cos`/`std::sin`. On 2026-11-06, Windows and WSL Linux packed different last-ulp rotations from bit-identical Rapier transforms; see the [lockstep feasibility audit](../audits/2026-11-06-coupling-lockstep-feasibility.md). Same-host runs are unaffected. Cross-platform replay is not a Current claim. The internal [4LY free-flight chassis](../systems/physical-free-flight.md) reuses this same rectangle publication and cellular response. Its authored propulsion force cap is separate from the native impulse cap above. Raising a flight thrust limit does not repair or requalify body/material coupling. **Current opt-in native producer and journal:** [World](../../native/include/cybersand/world.hpp) owns a disabled-by-default [bounded coordinator](../../native/include/cybersand/settled_world_discovery.hpp), which feeds [SettledDiscovery](../../native/include/cybersand/settled_discovery.hpp) from serialized owner hooks and classifies complete registered tiles. Cells remain the only material owner; no scheduler skip, proxy, compaction, material rule or Rapier change is admitted. A uniform tile is not a face-connected region and not a cohesion certificate. Mixed states, holes and material boundaries must be explicit refusals of the uniform-summary classification, never silently filled or averaged. **Current opt-in connectivity:** when `settled_region_connectivity_enabled` is explicitly enabled, each completed journal publication is copied into the bounded [`SettledRegions`](../../native/include/cybersand/settled_regions.hpp) engine under the serialized World owner. Region publication remains read-only: it neither skips simulation work nor transfers cell/material ownership. Issue #64 replaces the earlier coarse facing-tile retirement with exact graph incidence. Each accepted tile revision owns bounded local components and revision-bound face runs; components own their incident cross-tile edges, while typed tile-revision and absence-face dependencies point back to the exact active build/publication subscribers that use them. A changed tile therefore retires its own dependency subscribers and only the absence certificates or neighboring publications that actually depend on newly resident/facing coverage. Blocked, refused and capacity-unavailable tiles remain unknown and therefore cannot be crossed by a complete publication. The Stage 2 lifecycle received an independent review and focused transition tests before this substrate was written. **Current:** #59 sizes journal and connectivity backing from the effective runtime tile capacity rather than the compiled maximum: journal/owner/key storage are `T`, region edge storage is `64T`, and frontier/seen/build-member scratch is `32T`; `C=1024`, `K=32`, `B=128` and publication `P=4096` remain frozen. #64 adds runtime-sized typed dependency storage `D=max(16T, frontier_capacity)` (therefore `32T` in the integrated configuration), plus `2P+2` bounded generation-bearing subscriber headers. The accepted #65 reconstruction path additionally reserves publication-member storage at twice frontier capacity (`64T`), reconstruction seeds and staged members at frontier capacity (`32T` each), and bounded ticket/child slots at `P`. These pools are explicit in `SettledRegions::storage_bytes()` and its capacity accessors; the older `32T` build scratch is not the complete publication memory budget. These are observer resources only: saturation refuses connectivity publication without changing authoritative World state. #60 adds construction-time bounded ordered key/spatial indexes without hot resizing or per-operation allocation. Registration rejects zero/oversized/overflowing bounds, duplicate/overlapping geometry where required, and full capacity. Handles contain an externally unique nonzero incarnation plus never-reused slot; there is no live reset. New registry construction requires a fresh incarnation. This is a block observation ID, not production region identity. Copy/move cloning is forbidden. **Current producer integration:** chunk creation registers canonical nonoverlapping subtiles through an array-backed height-bounded ordered index over canonical tile keys.

Section: Water hybrid, saturated-head and compartment-pressure extension programme > Parallel feasibility branch: lumped compartment gas pressure > Water coupling boundary
Compartment pressure does **not** by itself solve saturated Water transmission. It supplies a boundary condition at a free liquid surface. For a vented reservoir, surface pressure may be treated as atmospheric. For a sealed compartment, the Water surface sees that compartment's derived pressure. A sealed two-reservoir fixture therefore should not blindly require equal Water levels. Its equilibrium depends on both hydrostatic head and gas pressure. The explicit Water bulk mechanism and the gas-region model remain separate questions.

Section: Water hybrid, saturated-head and compartment-pressure extension programme > Core hypothesis: generic hybrid soliding may supply part of the missing bulk response > Precise sheet concept
The intended proof is **not**: - one monolithic solid Water core; - rigidifying an entire reservoir; - repeating lamination throughout the full depth; - one reservoir-spanning unbreakable plate; - a Water-specific second rigid-body engine. The intended candidate is approximately: - zero sheets for shallow Water; - at most roughly **3-5 tiers** for very deep Water; - tiers concentrated in the **upper volume**, while preserving a few cellular layers at the actual free surface; - each tier made of bounded/segmented local carriers rather than one unbounded slab; - tier count or eligibility derived conservatively from local depth/support; - promotion/demotion performed through the same generic hybrid ownership machinery used by other solided material; - aggressive split/desolid behavior around unsupported edges, rapidly changing surfaces, constrictions, excessive rotation, topology change or invalid support. The intended coarse mechanism is: `depth -> eligible tier count/load -> Rapier gravity/contact -> cellular displacement -> outward surge`. Three useful qualitative tiers may be enough; the ceiling exists to keep both cost and mechanical influence bounded.

**Historical FreeMass comparator:** #26 did not change its original law. Section: Water hybrid, saturated-head and compartment-pressure extension programme > Conditional space/decompression extension
Space/vacuum scenes make the compartment model potentially useful beyond Water, but this remains conditional research. Do not model "negative absolute pressure". Vacuum approaches zero absolute pressure; negative **gauge** pressure is only relative to a chosen reference. If a pressurized compartment opens toward a much lower-pressure region, a cheap game-engine approximation may create a bounded decompression event at the opening instead of simulating cellular air. A candidate event may carry: - opening identity, location, effective area and direction; - source/destination region and pressure differential; - bounded mass/impulse budget; - duration/decay; - local spatial horizon; - explicit generation/revision so stale openings cannot continue applying force. A bounded local flow/distance/occlusion field may then apply impulses to loose cellular material, debris and generic Rapier bodies. The research question is whether this can look and behave plausibly without becoming full gas CFD or a magical radial "suction" force. This branch is optional and executes only after the lumped-region feasibility issue records a positive admission.

Section: WEX-004 bounded decompression impulse-event preregistration > Frozen pressure-to-budget mapping
This proof uses a unitless **work proxy**, not joules and not a calibrated gas model. For all valid openings, define an area-weighted effective destination pressure: `P_dest_eff = sum(area_i * min(P_dest_i, P_source)) / sum(area_i)`. At fixed source volume, the isothermal amount proxy that could be discharged before that conservative effective equilibrium is: `A_extractable = A_source * clamp(1 - P_dest_eff / P_source, 0, 1)`. The finite shared source work budget is: `B_source = min(12.0, A_extractable * 1.0)`. If every opening has less than **250 Pa** positive differential, registration is valid but creates no effective work. The threshold is frozen to prevent tiny near-equal differences from becoming persistent jitter. Initial opening weights are: `w_i = area_i * max(P_source - P_dest_i, 0)`. Each event receives once, at registration: `B_i = B_source * w_i / sum(w)`. Thus event budgets sum to the one source budget: adding openings cannot multiply available work. After actual work `W` is consumed, source amount decreases by `W / 1.0`, clamped at zero. Current source pressure is always derived from the original snapshot by the fixed-volume ratio: `P_current = P_source_initial * A_remaining / A_source_initial`. An event stops producing work whenever `P_current - P_dest_i < 250 Pa`, its budget reaches zero, topology/generation becomes stale, or its lifetime expires. No coefficient may be tuned after observing D0-D8 without registering a new experimental arm.

This may run independently of WEX-002. **Research disposition, 2026-09-20:** [WEX-003 feasibility research](../research/lumped-gas-region-pressure-bookkeeping.md) finds lumped connected-gas bookkeeping technically promising for a bounded optional/research feature, without selecting production integration. The preferred candidate combines exact dirty-local gas connectivity, a sparse macro-component graph, explicit narrow portals and invalidatable authored seeds. Authoritative gas amount plus free volume derive pressure; stale or over-budget split topology returns unavailable rather than silently retaining pressure authority. Worst-case closure still scales with the affected region, so a later production proof would need explicit work/capacity budgets and real churn measurements. Do not integrate a production atmosphere system by default. Minimum proof cases: 1. sealed static room; 2. volume compression/decompression with constant gas amount; 3. door/window opening that merges/vents regions; 4. closing that requires split detection; 5. two reservoirs with both headspaces vented; 6. same geometry with sealed headspaces; 7. exterior/vacuum boundary; 8. topology churn and conservative failure/refusal. Section: Smoke, heat, and pressure roadmap > Current native Smoke
[MaterialRules](../../native/include/cybersand/material.hpp) names material ID 4 `Smoke`, with `Gas` as an alias. In [World::update_rule_kernel, RuleKernel::Gas](../../native/src/world.cpp), Smoke attempts up, both up-diagonals, then lateral movement. An Empty target permits a move; a denser movable target permits an exchange only when its descriptor accepts density exchange. Wall and the Mite/Rocket agents opt out. Numeric density alone does not imply permeability. Smoke starts with `state_a = 240`. On its coordinate-staggered eight-tick lane, it loses one lifetime unit, or two when at least five of the eight neighbors are Smoke. At the final decay sample it becomes Empty. Movement changes the coordinate-dependent phase, so this is not a universal lifetime in seconds. Trapped Smoke uses `keep_cell_active` between samples. The ignition helper excludes Smoke: ordinary heat-contact/Fire ignition does not turn it into Fire. The owner-approved visual intent is a lingering cloud with slow internal collapse, substantially slower than Foam, without an extra full-world age scan. Further artistic tuning is **Planned**.

Section: Repository development and release > Reconciliation and design choices
**Current owner policy (2026-11-06):** agents reconcile long-running or stacked branches with main as needed, without stopping for owner approval. Integration must not silently decide a design question, though. When a conflict or merge has to choose between competing systems, laws or designs, or changes default behavior or feel, the agent: - chooses the best-supported option and continues; - records it under **Design choices** in the PR: what was chosen, the alternative, why, and what reversing it would take, written in plain language for a non-programmer owner; - keeps the evidence and qualification needed for that choice. Protected-source transitions, provider policy and release gates still apply. Purely mechanical conflicts (text, docs, routing) need no entry. The owner reviews these notes asynchronously and may redirect later. This adds no gate: merging to main, Ready, deleting finished work and default promotion remain owner actions as before. To limit drift, prefer refreshing long-running branches from main after significant main merges, and land a base before stacking more than one dependent layer on it.

Section: CI execution watchdogs and advisory performance > Timing records and comparable history
[Execution telemetry](../../tools/ci/execution_telemetry.py) writes `execution-performance-v1` JSONL alongside original evidence. Records identify commit/tree, tracked delta, fixture and source definition, policy, runner and CPU characteristics, OS, material inventory, solver/world definition and result. Existing structured Godot/native markers retain construction, stepping, worker, Rapier, input, snapshot, pause/reset/recovery and shutdown metrics where those fixtures expose them. Whole-process elapsed time is distinct from nested phase fields. Completed hosted-job wall times come from GitHub job timestamps and are bound to original observations by a hashed runner identity. Queue delay is excluded; unfinished collector jobs have no invented final duration. CPU seconds and peak RSS are explicitly direct-process observations; unavailable process counters remain unavailable. No direct GPU or physical presentation timing is inferred from elapsed time. Renderer, driver, selected shader and cache state are retained when actually reported. Missing compiler/cache details remain `unknown`; headless/native work uses explicit `not-applicable` renderer fields. Shader-specific cold/warm runs must supply their actual provenance before any comparable shader baseline exists. Raw logs remain the complete record, including information a compact reduction does not expose. [The history collector](../../tools/ci/performance_history.py) reads current JSONL and up to ten eligible completed default-branch artifact bundles. Each workflow publishes one consolidated `execution-performance-*` artifact for 90 days and a compact Actions summary. Authenticated run/source/attempt custody, bounded archive reads and safe signed redirects protect history attribution. Unavailable or expired history is recorded, not replaced with invented values. A baseline requires at least three distinct comparable successful runs. Failed, watchdog and incomplete rows remain in the retained current dataset but are not successful baseline samples. Like-for-like cohorts include platform, hosted runner/CPU, fixture/configuration, renderer/compiler and cache state. Historical Avrea measurements remain a separate hardware cohort. Missing required identity makes a row incomparable. The rolling median produces advisory warnings at 1.5 times baseline, prominent warnings at 2 times, and cumulative-drift advice after five successive increases reaching 1.2 times the starting value. These ratios never fail correctness. Source, fixture and shader changes are reported separately; a possible introducing commit is named only when direct-parent evidence supports that inference. A small artifact window may contain fewer than three distinct runs, so the first qualified runs intentionally report insufficient history.

Use the repository-pinned Godot/Rapier and matching native extension. The accepted runtime includes the multi-part response-owner capacity. Rebuild when its source inputs differ; never relabel an older DLL/SO as a matching runtime. Follow [local build and validation](local-build-and-validation.md) and retain source, runtime hashes, exact commands, logs and the platform alongside results. From the repository root, with `GODOT` naming the pinned executable: ```sh "$GODOT" --headless --path godot --script tests/test_workbench_actor_catalog.gd -- --save actor-compose-schema "$GODOT" --headless --path godot --script tests/test_workbench_actor_catalog.gd -- --reopen actor-compose-schema "$GODOT" --headless --path godot --script tests/test_workbench_actor_composition_session.gd "$GODOT" --headless --path godot --script tests/test_workbench_actor_composition_native.gd "$GODOT" --headless --path godot --script tests/test_workbench_actor_equipment_extent.gd CYBERSAND_ACTOR_COMPOSITION_REPORT=/absolute/path/author.json "$GODOT" --headless --path godot --script tests/test_workbench_actor_composition.gd CYBERSAND_ACTOR_COMPOSITION_REOPEN=1 CYBERSAND_ACTOR_COMPOSITION_REPORT=/absolute/path/reopen.json "$GODOT" --headless --path godot --script tests/test_workbench_actor_composition.gd ``` The integration writer uses named start `actor-compose-589-evaluation`; set `CYBERSAND_ACTOR_COMPOSITION_NAME` in both processes to isolate another run. The second invocation is a new process with a fresh native World and physical owner. Its completion marker is `WB_ACTOR_COMPOSE` followed by JSON checks, failures, per-actor movement/support, equipment receipts, native/Rapier progression and elapsed/cost observations. A nonzero exit or any failure means it did not pass. Retain failed logs, not only the final result. For actual framebuffer evidence, remove `--headless` in an available graphical display and set `CYBERSAND_ACTOR_COMPOSITION_CAPTURE` to an absolute output directory. PNGs come from the real application framebuffer after presentation; the capture refuses the headless driver. Captions in the JSON identify human, scripted, policy and passive roles, phase and tick. A software-rendered Linux capture proves the displayed application state, not Windows playfeel or hardware frame pacing. Select further Workbench input, combined-authoring, generated-start, Flatten and equipment regressions according to the changed behavior and the dedicated qualification runner. Documentation-only edits do not require an expensive full runtime matrix. The commands above are reproduction procedures, not a claim that this documentation mission reran them. Catalogue, controller and gameplay results are separate from performance: compare no NPC, one script, heterogeneous scripts, mixed producers and equipment on both small and 2048 × 1024 canvases, retaining actual tick progression, decision cost, frame/publication timing and memory. Do not infer performance from slot limits. Windows graphical execution and owner acceptance remain explicit requirements when the build environment cannot run a Windows desktop. A portable package must contain the source-matched native/Rapier runtimes, pinned Godot, project resources and this example; its launcher must open interactive Shared Workbench.

Section: Local build and validation > First launch from a source checkout
Use this repository's launcher and retained runtime for a first exploration. A native rebuild is a separate development task. The [player getting-started guide](getting-started.md) walks through opening the Workbench; this page owns the build, identity and validation procedure. From a new checkout with Git and Git LFS installed: ```sh git clone https://github.com/techrote/cybersand.git cd cybersand git lfs install --local git lfs pull git rev-parse HEAD git status --short python3 tools/ci/check_repository.py --require-materialized ``` On Windows, use `python` instead of `python3` when that is the installed command. `git lfs pull` obtains the committed runtime payloads. A small text pointer is not a usable DLL or shared library. `check_repository.py` checks the runtime bytes and recorded source inputs; it also checks documentation and dependencies, so read the actual failure rather than assuming every failure means a broken DLL. **Windows:** install the [exact Godot pin](#which-build-inputs-are-required), then run from this repository root in PowerShell: ```powershell .\launch-desktop.cmd -Godot C:\path\to\Godot_v4.7-stable_win64.exe -PrintIdentityOnly .\launch-desktop.cmd -Godot C:\path\to\Godot_v4.7-stable_win64.exe ``` The path is an example: use the actual executable location. The launcher also accepts `CYBERSAND_GODOT`, or searches `C:\Godot47`. It validates the pinned Godot version, materialized Windows runtimes and CyberSand DLL hash; it prints the checkout/runtime identity and performs no build or replacement. The default project scene is [Feature Launcher](../../godot/project.godot), which routes to the ordinary **Shared Workbench** and standalone scenes. `-Editor` opens the same project in the editor. `dev.cmd` is not required for a source-only checkout. **Linux x86_64:** with the pinned Godot executable and materialized Linux runtimes, use an explicit executable path: ```sh CYBERSAND_GODOT=/absolute/path/to/Godot_v4.7-stable_linux.x86_64 "$CYBERSAND_GODOT" --version "$CYBERSAND_GODOT" --headless --editor --path godot --import "$CYBERSAND_GODOT" --path godot ``` The version output must match the table below. The last command requires a graphical session. Import and launch are separate steps; successful project import is not proof that native gameplay or every feature ran. A software display is useful for reproducible graphical tests, but does not establish the owner's Windows/NVIDIA playfeel.

results.query: Why can Ice freezing or Lava and Water reactions stop after settling, and does unrelated nearby activity change the result?
facts: MAT-001 preserves the next existing opportunity for persistent compact-pair and Ice contacts through the existing earliest block deadline.
Pair contact keeps its four-tick phase; Ice melting uses four ticks and freezing sixteen. Products, probabilities, neighbor order and random streams are unchanged.

The source epoch check includes neighbor-only successful writes, while contact eligibility respects body masks. Other specialized lifecycle kernels retain their existing waiting behavior. Workers publish keepalive and earliest-deadline requests through geometry-bounded job grids; only the serial phase barrier changes shared block/chunk metadata, independently of optional discovery overflow. Fixed disjoint job spans borrow two contiguous ParallelState buffers, with checked setup products and no tick-time resize.

Section: Materials and rule kernels > Kernel execution and cadence > How do persistent reactions survive sleep?
**Current, MAT-001 / #158:** after ordinary source admission and kernel execution, World checks an unchanged source for a possible compact-pair reaction, or Ice for hot/Water neighbors. A registered pair schedules its next four-tick contact lane. Ice schedules its next four-tick melting lane when heat is present, otherwise its sixteen-tick freezing sample when Water is present. All use the original stable coordinate phases. Products, probabilities, neighbor order and random streams are unchanged; the repair preserves opportunities that quiet-block sleep used to lose. A failed probability roll or an Ice sample that misses the eligible neighbor retains another opportunity. A successful neighbor-only write also rechecks the unchanged source, which matters when another contact remains across a block/core boundary. Eligibility respects body masks. Removing a mask wakes the affected resident block so its newly visible contacts can be reconsidered. This does not force a reaction on every contact or prescribe a universal completion time. The [activity contract](activity-dirty-regions-and-waking.md) owns bounded deadline, pause/re-entry and render-dirty semantics. The [MAT-001 evidence](../audits/2026-10-18-mat001-material-reaction-progress.md) records the reproduced starvation, retained controls and platform limits.

**Physical placement:** primary releases the existing equipment body. After supported low-speed settling, the owner fixes that same body at its current pose and submits a deployment request. Only worker admission enables processing. The copied object pose belongs to its actor, instance, equipment epoch and stable body ID. Dropping a chassis alone does not automatically start a processor. Physical ports follow the body's rotation and lie outside its collider. Their local x distance is `ceil(half_extents.x + 2)` on the intake/output sides, with local y offsets `-1` and `+1`; transformed locations round to cell coordinates. Body occupancy and material conditions are checked under cellular ownership. The retained sampled route instead requires an empty 5×5 workspace and uses logical ports `(-2,-1)`, `(-2,+1)`, `(+2,-1)`, `(+2,+1)`. | Ref / ID | Object | Recipe / response | |---|---|---| | U23 `stone_grinder` | Stone Grinder | Stone → Sand | | U24 `glass_reclaimer` | Glass Reclaimer | base Glass → Sand | | U25 `brine_splitter` | Brine Splitter | two Brine slots → Water + Salt | | U26 `glass_kiln` | Glass Kiln | Sand → Molten Glass while Fire or Lava is nearby | | U27 `steam_condenser` | Steam Condenser | Steam → Water while Ice is nearby | | U28 `cement_finisher` | Cement Finisher | Cement → Concrete while Water is nearby | | U29 `sludge_scrubber` | Sludge Scrubber | Toxic Sludge + Water → Water + Dust | | U30 `metal_reclaimer` | Metal Reclaimer | Rust + Coal → Metal + Smoke | | U31 `seed_incubator` | Seed Incubator | Seed + Water → Plant | | U32 `firewarden` | Firewarden | nearby Fire → emit Water; twelve successful pulses | Ordinary processors have 16 successful batches, a 45-second lifetime and a 0.35-second cadence; deployment costs 18 actor equipment charge. Firewarden has 12 successful pulses. Catalysts are sensed within a 7×7 square and are not consumed. A complete batch checks every required input, catalyst, output and owner-side work budget before consuming the recipe. Blocked output leaves inputs untouched. Physical **U** pickup requires the owning mount to be close enough with a clear attachment path. It reuses the existing body and retires that deployment's active processing authority. A bounded per-actor/per-processor history retains stock, age, cycles and cooldown across pickup, redeployment and selection changes; recovering a used device cannot refill it. Exhausted or expired devices remain inert and visible until physical retirement. Remote right-click retrieval applies only to the sampled compatibility route. Neither path refunds spent charge. results.query: Why can removing a body mask leave settled sand or material reactions asleep, and how is that wake repaired without a false render write?
facts: The ordinary neighbor wake helper skips the center block because material writes already wake it. Mask changes need their own explicit center-block activity wake.
Insertion and removal wake the resident mask block plus ordinary boundary neighbors without changing stored cell bytes or marking rendering dirty.
The current coupling rebuilds masks, so this can wake touched interior body blocks on each rebuild; the repair does not add a global wake or change body forces.

Section: Activity, dirty regions, and waking > What wakes a region?
Direct `set`/`write_cell` operations mark their cells dirty and active. `wake_cell_neighborhood` wakes resident nonempty neighbors when the changed coordinate lies at an activity-block edge or corner. Movement marks both source and destination. The phased `merge_job_effects` path additionally wakes through the corners of touched block bounds, so its wake can be broader than one direct cell write. Explosion edits and transient-obstacle changes use explicit wake paths. A mask insertion or removal explicitly wakes its own resident block without a render write, then applies the ordinary boundary-neighbor wake. The neighbor helper alone excludes the center block because ordinary material writes already wake it. Mask changes must not depend on a neighboring material write to resume contact. The current body-coupling path rebuilds masks, so it can wake touched interior body blocks even for stationary bodies; this is confined to that existing footprint. Settled Water can become inactive; render dithering does not wake it. **Current:** a denied slow Mercury pair records the earliest due tick in its source block. The existing `begin_tick` metadata pass wakes due included blocks and clears their deadline. Sleeping blocks therefore progress without a periodic cell scan. Excluded deadlines remain pending; re-entry evaluates only the current modulo lane, with no missed-move catch-up. Clear/replacement discards these deadlines and failed-world quarantine prevents their processing. The [versioned pair policy](granular-interaction-policy.md) owns rate and endpoint rules. **Current, MAT-001 / #158:** `World::schedule_pending_reaction_wake` uses that same earliest block deadline for an eligible compact-pair contact or an Ice thermal contact. It runs after an admitted kernel when the source itself was not written in the current epoch, including successful neighbor-only work. Eligibility uses the existing pair resolver and mask-aware neighbors, independent of the current probability roll. The deadline is strictly in the future, so a missed sample can receive another scheduled opportunity. Waiting does not alter cell content, movement counts or render dirtiness; an inert contact acquires no new deadline. The deadline is shared by all work in a block. Removing one partner does not cancel a deadline that may belong to another source or a transport lane; one already scheduled wake can retire normally after re-evaluation. Interest exclusion, re-entry, clear and failed-world handling use the existing lifecycle above. The [dated regression record](../audits/2026-10-18-mat001-material-reaction-progress.md) scopes the executed evidence. Other specialized kernels retain their own waiting behavior; this is not a guarantee for every future material rule. **Current:** newly included cores wake their resident blocks once, including sleeping blocks. Existing overlap and unchanged/equivalent regions stay asleep. Render dirty consumption explicitly has no discovery-acknowledgement meaning. 23. Epoch wrap/epoch-byte clearing is scheduling metadata and does not dirty discovery payload by itself. 24. Any new source mutation/event path introduced while this stage is active must be added to this matrix before Stage 3 can pass.

Section: Materials and rule kernels > Kernel execution and cadence > How do persistent reactions survive sleep?
**Current, MAT-001 / #158:** after ordinary source admission and kernel execution, World checks an unchanged source for a possible compact-pair reaction, or Ice for hot/Water neighbors. A registered pair schedules its next four-tick contact lane. Ice schedules its next four-tick melting lane when heat is present, otherwise its sixteen-tick freezing sample when Water is present. All use the original stable coordinate phases. Products, probabilities, neighbor order and random streams are unchanged; the repair preserves opportunities that quiet-block sleep used to lose. A failed probability roll or an Ice sample that misses the eligible neighbor retains another opportunity. A successful neighbor-only write also rechecks the unchanged source, which matters when another contact remains across a block/core boundary. Eligibility respects body masks. Removing a mask wakes the affected resident block so its newly visible contacts can be reconsidered. This does not force a reaction on every contact or prescribe a universal completion time. The [activity contract](activity-dirty-regions-and-waking.md) owns bounded deadline, pause/re-entry and render-dirty semantics. The [MAT-001 evidence](../audits/2026-10-18-mat001-material-reaction-progress.md) records the reproduced starvation, retained controls and platform limits.

Section: Issue 12 Stage 3 execution freeze > Stage 3 exit checklist
Stage 3 is complete only when all items below have passing evidence or an explicit evidence-backed refusal that keeps affected coverage nonconsumable: - [ ] PR #43 foundation/reconciliation state is incorporated without rewriting evidence. - [ ] Complete World producer matrix is implemented or affected tiles stay witness-incomplete. - [ ] No worker mutates the shared discovery manager. - [ ] Direct tuple/state/temperature ABA invalidates independently of render dirty state. - [ ] Worker writes invalidate after deterministic barriers with workers1/4 parity. - [ ] No-write activity and interaction deadlines prevent false settled evidence. - [ ] Mask add/remove/reconfigure ABA has local revisions; far masks do not cause global reset. - [ ] Accepted pending events invalidate/block before execution. - [ ] Requested/applied inclusion, exclusion/re-entry and fresh-observation semantics pass. - [ ] Chunk creation/reservation and tracking-capacity refusal never alter simulation. - [ ] Clear/replacement/move identity and failed-world quarantine are explicit and tested. - [ ] Epoch-wrap bookkeeping does not masquerade as discovery mutation. - [ ] Canonical bounded subtiles handle default and declared custom geometry/refusal cases. - [ ] Exact stored tuple sampling includes temperature beneath occupancy. - [ ] Local component extraction preserves holes/seams/state boundaries and rejects truncation. - [ ] Cross-tile face connectivity works across activity/chunk seams and negative coordinates. - [ ] Diagonal contact does not merge; narrow face necks connect only as discovery, never cohesion. - [ ] Tile invalidation retires both old connected regions and facing-neighbor completeness. - [ ] Region traversal is bounded/resumable and publishes only complete revision-matched results. - [ ] Region identity/generation, split/merge invalidation and capacity refusal are deterministic. - [ ] Untracked/blocked/capacity boundaries prevent false globally-complete regions. - [ ] Feature-disabled authoritative behavior and work counters remain equivalent. - [ ] 1/4-worker deterministic state plus discovery summaries/digests match where required. - [ ] ASan/UBSan and feasible TSan/failure tests pass. - [ ] Whole-system producer+journal+connectivity CPU/memory/latency costs are measured. - [ ] Large-world region count/area, churn, invalidation fanout and wake/rebuild amplification are retained. - [ ] No stationary acceleration, ownership transfer or Rapier behavior is claimed by Stage 3. - [ ] Canonical docs, evidence, retrieval routes and exact source/artifact identities are synchronized.

Section: Neon Reliquary and the city below > Presentation and ownership
[`CyberShowcasePresentation`](../../godot/scripts/showcase_presentation.gd) creates district/viewpoint controls and one backdrop for the accepted tile. It reads the existing accepted current/previous render textures and the existing player rectangle. It adds no native queries, mutable world image, simulation thread or cell fields. The normal material palette, emission and glow shaders remain the foreground renderer. The [backdrop shader](../../godot/shaders/neon_reliquary_backdrop.gdshader) draws a restrained distant skyline, coloured haze, shafts and sparse dust only in empty cells. Current material occupancy, unfinished previous-material transitions and the sampled player are excluded. Material paint/erase therefore updates its mask through the ordinary render publication. The atmosphere does not show through occupied glass, gas or partial Water cells; those continue using the existing material renderer. These lights and skyline silhouettes are decorative scenery, with no collision, heat or illumination authority. The backdrop is disabled for an edited definition that enables rigid bodies; the authored scene has none. The top tile keeps its original cyan atmosphere. Middle Cyberberbia adds warm rose/amber haze around the inhabited bridge; Sewertech Alley shifts toward utility teal; Industrial Underswamp uses muted green and rust-coloured haze. The selected palette derives from the accepted district identity, with the same material/player/transition mask for all four. New scene installation uses the established desktop worker acknowledgement or synchronous Web host. A pending reset or open experiment/definition modal blocks the showcase shortcut. On desktop, this also includes an open actor selector or an actor installation awaiting acknowledgement. Viewpoint popups block paint underneath them and require mouse release before paint resumes. F8 also hides the player/environment and actor launchers and dismisses their tuning panels, preserving the promised clean view. Accepted showcase installation clears ordinary sandbox actor prototypes through the existing MicroScenario transition.

Section: SetA actor controls and legacy policy compatibility > How can a neural policy control the same actor?
**Current interface, future policy consumer:** the movement model consumes a small value command and exposes a bounded observation. Keyboard adaptation and a future neural-network controller must use that same command contract. Their responsibility is to select actions; the actor model remains responsible for admission, acceleration, action timing, energy and collision. The owner-local core methods are `configure_model(StringName) -> bool`, `reset(Vector2)`, `simulate_action(delta, movement, primary, secondary, world)`, `capabilities() -> Dictionary` and `observation() -> PackedFloat32Array`. `movement` is a finite `Vector2` with each component clamped to -1..1. Runner and Crawler ignore y without slowing x; Skimmer additionally limits the vector's magnitude to one so diagonals gain no extra thrust speed. `primary` and `secondary` are held button states interpreted by the selected rule set, with edges retained by the session. These methods are called by the serialized simulation owner; a main-thread or inference worker must use the copied session bridge rather than directly invoking the live actor or passing itself World. Version 1 observations have a fixed 16-float order: | Index | Value | |---:|---| | 0–1 | Position x, y in world cells | | 2–3 | Velocity x, y in cells/second | | 4 | Grounded flag | | 5 | Runtime-enclosed flag | | 6 | Energy fraction | | 7–8 | Primary-ready, secondary-ready flags | | 9 | Remaining action cooldown in seconds | | 10–11 | Primary-active, secondary-active flags | | 12 | Horizontal facing direction | | 13 | Model index: 0 Runner, 1 Skimmer, 2 Crawler | | 14 | Occupancy query count for the last actor update | | 15 | Movement-limited flag | Flag values use 0/1. The entire vector is **not normalized**: absolute position, velocity, timing and query-count fields retain the units above. A training adapter must version its own feature scaling. The session publication pairs each observation row with epoch, simulation tick, model, producer and accepted sequence. The zero-based row index is its actor ID; the vector alone is insufficient to identify a response target. `sequences` reports the latest **admitted** command, which may arrive after the motor last stepped; it is not an applied-action or exact-replay receipt. ACT-002 additionally publishes consumed actions, sequences and edge flags through the [v2 observation contract](actor-rigs.md#identity-freshness-and-consumed-edges); these additive fields do not change the original observation order.

Section: SetA actor controls and legacy policy compatibility > How can a neural policy control the same actor? > Command admission and expiry
`CyberActorPrototypeSession.configure(definitions, world)` admits at most eight actors. Each definition provides `model`, `position` and one producer identity: `human`, `policy` or `demo`. Session state stays with the same simulation owner. The session submission contract is below. Producers reach it through the thread-safe `CyberSimulationWorker.submit_actor_action` forwarding method with the same fields; they do not obtain the owner-local session or motor itself. ```gdscript submit_action(actor_id: int, epoch: int, sequence: int, observed_tick: int, movement: Vector2, primary: bool, secondary: bool, lease_ticks: int = 12, producer: StringName = &"policy") -> bool ``` Admission checks actor/producer identity, the current epoch, strictly increasing sequence, finite movement and the observation tick. Future observations are rejected. A lease is at most 18 simulation ticks; its deadline is calculated from the **observation tick**, so a delayed inference result cannot gain a fresh full lease merely by arriving late. At the 60 Hz desktop actor cadence the default lease is 200 ms and the maximum is 300 ms of simulation time. Each actor slot has one replaceable held-state command and latched rising edges. Several submissions before a tick replace continuous movement with the latest accepted value while preserving a brief press/release; multiple rises of the same button before consumption coalesce to one edge. There is no action FIFO to drain later. Rejection returns `false` and does not create a command for another actor or bypass the active producer's authority. Pause invalidates command identity and clears held inputs/edges while preserving actor cooldown state. Reset or scenario replacement also invalidates the old epoch. An input producer must read the current published epoch and observation tick after those transitions; late output for the previous actor incarnation is rejected. The complete controller state is not serialized for replay.

Section: Shared Workbench actor composition > Producer and policy interface
Authored sources are `human`, `scripted`, `policy` and `passive`. `scripted` maps to the existing session's `demo` producer. The UI calls it **Scripted NPC**, not AI. A policy source additionally chooses `fixture` or `external`. The fixture is a deterministic local test producer that obtains actual issued observations and submits the same leased command envelope as an external caller. Selecting External Policy does not start an HTTP service, neural model, SLM or LLM. | Workbench API | Meaning | |---|---| | `select_instance(instance_id)` | Inspect without changing producer | | `pilot_id()` / `pilot_instance(instance_id)` | Inspect or explicitly change the human pilot; takeover is live | | `hand_back_pilot()` | Restore the previous compatible source, or the model's scripted default | | `set_actor_control(instance_id, control)` | Validate and switch source/enabled state/cadence/policy adapter; rejects starting-equipment changes | | `actor_observation(instance_id, false)` | Copy current diagnostic observation; does not issue new command authority | | `actor_observation(instance_id, true)` | Issue a fresh physical policy observation for an enabled, running policy actor | | `submit_actor_policy(instance_id, command)` | Resolve stable authored identity to its current slot, then submit through session producer/freshness checks | | `physical_actor_session.workbench_control(instance_id)` | Copy source, run/epoch/slot/generation/tick, lease, sequence, per-actor accepted/refused counts, decision costs and diagnostics | An in-process integration uses the same adapter available in the panel: ```gdscript var view := workbench.actor_observation(instance_id, true) if not view.is_empty(): var action := {"move": Vector2(0.5, 0.0)} var command := CyberPhysicalActorSession.make_command( view, int(view.last_sequence) + 1, action, 12) workbench.submit_actor_policy(instance_id, command) ``` `make_command()` copies the run, epoch, physical actor slot, issued observation identity/tick and applicable equipment identity. The caller maintains monotonic sequences and must use a fresh observation after cancellation, takeover, expiry or replacement. A policy command uses version 2 and `kind: physical_wire_action`; its bounded lease is 1–18 physical ticks. Local decision intervals are 1–12 ticks. The script scheduler collects copied views before submitting the independent decisions, at the existing physical tick boundary. Decision time is recorded separately from native and Rapier progress. Wrong actor, producer, run, epoch, generation-bound observation, repeated sequence, expired lease, unissued observation and sampled command kinds refuse. Knowing a reused physical slot is insufficient: a replaced actor has a new authored identity and retired run/observation authority. No diagnostic view exposes mutable native cell storage or PhysicsServer objects. The panel's **Issue observation** prepares an editable JSON envelope. **Submit command** keeps that envelope's original identity and therefore demonstrates stale-output refusal when editing takes too long. **Send fresh test action** is explicitly a local test producer: it issues a new observation and binds the edited action values immediately. It does not relabel a delayed external reply

results.query: What bounds the cost of the actor prototypes, and does that prove they are ready for a large neural NPC population?
facts: The session admits at most eight actors. Original SetA controllers reuse an 8 by 14 sampled body, clamp each step to 1/30 second and cap speed at 120 cells/second, bounding ordinary movement to four increments per axis; additional ACT-002 rigs have their own separately bounded motor.
Crawler ledge search is bounded to four cells with intervening clearance; runtime enclosure immobilizes the prototype rather than initiating repeated terrain relocation.

SetA observations retain 16 floats plus session identity; ACT-002 adds versioned rig fields without requiring full-world scans. Bounded local work is not proof of zero allocations, target-PC performance, inference latency or production many-NPC scaling.

Section: SetA actor controls and legacy policy compatibility > What bounds the cost and response time?
The [fixed limits](../reference/configuration-reference.md#actor-control-prototype-values) admit at most eight actors, each with the same 8 by 14 sampled body. Updates accept at most 1/30 second and limit speed to 120 cells/second, bounding ordinary movement to four increments per axis. A Crawler tries at most one ledge search per update and at most four cells of rise with intervening clearance. Runtime burial immobilizes the prototype, so it does not repeat a relocation search. Local observations contain 16 floats plus bounded session metadata and do not scan the world. One replaceable held command and coalesced rising edges per actor bound retained input work. The general desktop gameplay/emission queues retain their separately documented limitations; this actor session does not claim to replace every command path in the engine. Holding an action does not authorize an unbounded action queue. Transient actions must be consumed by the actor's timing rules, and stale policy outputs must not silently become input for a replacement actor after reset. Ordinary presentation can remain independently paced while the worker services admitted actor state. **Not yet established:** production many-NPC throughput, target-PC frame-time acceptance, maximum acceptable inference latency or zero-allocation simulation. The implementation uses GDScript value containers and copied publications; bounded actor counts and local queries are not a claim that every operation is allocation-free. Any timing report must name the source, runtime, actor count, world/fixture, platform and worker configuration actually tested.

Section: SetA actor controls and legacy policy compatibility > How can a neural policy control the same actor?
**Current interface, future policy consumer:** the movement model consumes a small value command and exposes a bounded observation. Keyboard adaptation and a future neural-network controller must use that same command contract. Their responsibility is to select actions; the actor model remains responsible for admission, acceleration, action timing, energy and collision. The owner-local core methods are `configure_model(StringName) -> bool`, `reset(Vector2)`, `simulate_action(delta, movement, primary, secondary, world)`, `capabilities() -> Dictionary` and `observation() -> PackedFloat32Array`. `movement` is a finite `Vector2` with each component clamped to -1..1. Runner and Crawler ignore y without slowing x; Skimmer additionally limits the vector's magnitude to one so diagonals gain no extra thrust speed. `primary` and `secondary` are held button states interpreted by the selected rule set, with edges retained by the session. These methods are called by the serialized simulation owner; a main-thread or inference worker must use the copied session bridge rather than directly invoking the live actor or passing itself World. Version 1 observations have a fixed 16-float order: | Index | Value | |---:|---| | 0–1 | Position x, y in world cells | | 2–3 | Velocity x, y in cells/second | | 4 | Grounded flag | | 5 | Runtime-enclosed flag | | 6 | Energy fraction | | 7–8 | Primary-ready, secondary-ready flags | | 9 | Remaining action cooldown in seconds | | 10–11 | Primary-active, secondary-active flags | | 12 | Horizontal facing direction | | 13 | Model index: 0 Runner, 1 Skimmer, 2 Crawler | | 14 | Occupancy query count for the last actor update | | 15 | Movement-limited flag | Flag values use 0/1. The entire vector is **not normalized**: absolute position, velocity, timing and query-count fields retain the units above. A training adapter must version its own feature scaling. The session publication pairs each observation row with epoch, simulation tick, model, producer and accepted sequence. The zero-based row index is its actor ID; the vector alone is insufficient to identify a response target. `sequences` reports the latest **admitted** command, which may arrive after the motor last stepped; it is not an applied-action or exact-replay receipt. ACT-002 additionally publishes consumed actions, sequences and edge flags through the [v2 observation contract](actor-rigs.md#identity-freshness-and-consumed-edges); these additive fields do not change the original observation order.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > Where could neural cellular automata fit?
Growing Neural Cellular Automata uses shared learned local updates and recurrent cell state on a grid. Its demonstrations concern pattern growth, persistence and regeneration. These results motivate a local recurrent design experiment; they do not show that an NCA is an effective actor pilot, battle policy or population controller. [Mordvintsev et al. 2020](https://distill.pub/2020/growing-ca/). The executable candidate and a future lattice experiment retain different names and contracts: | Form | State and neighborhood | Claim boundary | |---|---|---| | NCA-inspired actor graph | A small recurrent vector per actor; shared update using permitted neighboring actor state | A bounded graph-controller candidate; untrained weights provide no learned-control evidence | | Proposed terrain-lattice NCA | A separate coarse spatial lattice with recurrent channels and local cell updates | A training/interface proposal until its encoder, update, action readout and evaluation actually exist | Current [`nca.gd`](../../godot/examples/thunderbowl/nca.gd) uses a shared 12→8→4 residual MLP with four private recurrent values per actor. Inputs are own recurrent values, the mean of delivered `latent_state` messages, visible-enemy displacement, own horizontal velocity and energy. One update uses old delivered state; output is bounded to −1–1 and controls movement, effort and primary action. Episode or actor identity changes reset recurrence. The supplied weight artifact is explicitly `untrained`; loading `trained_external` metadata alone proves no training quality. For a proposed version-1 lattice experiment, start with an explicit spacing, 16 latent channels, a radius-one Moore neighborhood, one synchronous update round and a declared stochastic update probability. Freeze boundary handling, reset, sensor injection and local action readout before training. Keep the neural grid separate from authoritative material cells. A full-arena truth encoder creates a distributed sensor field with more coverage than an actor's local view and needs its own perception tag. Neither variant may hide global pooling, full-roster attention or in-place unbounded propagation behind a local label. Account for recurrent state, communication and update cost separately from the actor's collision queries. The existing world is not a differentiable training graph. Learning an update rule for this arena therefore needs an explicit route such as imitation, black-box policy optimization or a separately validated differentiable surrogate.

Section: Provisional actor rigs and shared control interface > Which actor rigs are available?
**Current, experimental (ACT-002 / #168):** the desktop sandbox and exploratory showcase maps have six sets containing 29 movement rigs. Every rig can be assigned to keyboard input, an external policy producer or the built-in scripted demonstration. Producer identity changes who may submit an action; it does not grant different movement, collision or tool authority. SetA preserves the original Runner, Skimmer and Crawler motors. Its [version-1 contract](actor-control-prototypes.md) remains the compatibility route. The additional sets share a sampled motor with authored rotation, surface attachment, ropes, resource limits and selected local tools. These are provisional gameplay rules for comparison, not a selection of the final player representation. | Set ID | Theme | Stable rig IDs, in catalog order | |---|---|---| | `setA` | Reference controls | `runner`, `skimmer`, `crawler` | | `setB` | Ground and near-ground machines | `scout`, `scrabbler`, `ripper`, `groundeffect`, `digger` | | `setF` | Unusual flight and descent | `copter`, `pouncer`, `dropbot`, `lineshank` | | `setY` | Contact, rope and impulse traversal | `walljumper`, `clamberer`, `swinger`, `rocketjumper` | | `setU` | Self-propelled salvage tools | `springjack`, `gyrocrate`, `bellows`, `winchbug`, `magpie`, `skatesail` | | `setV` | Speculative interface personas | `astra`, `claude`, `luna`, `qwen`, `bonsai`, `jev`, `gemini` | `groundeffect` has no underscore; its display name is **GroundEffect**. The first three global rig indices remain 0 Runner, 1 Skimmer and 2 Crawler. A catalog entry is copied metadata, not a live controller. Its `parameters` extension dictionary is currently empty; movement tuning belongs to the motor, while effort is an input action rather than a replacement PENV profile. Source: [`actor_rig_catalog.gd`](../../godot/scripts/actor_rig_catalog.gd) (`RIG_IDS`, `entry`, `controls_text`), [`actor_rig_motor.gd`](../../godot/scripts/actor_rig_motor.gd) (`simulate_rig_action`, `_advance_rig`) and [`actor_prototype_session.gd`](../../godot/scripts/actor_prototype_session.gd). USABLE-001 adds an independent [actor equipment layer](actor-usables.md) for the sampled rig session. Equipment has its own epoch/sequence/lease stream and does not reuse movement buttons or grant policies direct World-edit authority. The [physical ACT-005 equipment](physical-actor-rigs.md#which-usable-examples-exist) uses articulated body/mount authority and the physical issued-observation envelope.

results.query: How can a controller drive a tracked Ripper while tilting it, steer Digger downward, and independently aim and reel a Lineshank?
facts: The extended input contains movement and independent aim vectors, effort from zero to one, trim and reel from minus one to one, and primary/secondary/auxiliary buttons; each rig uses its declared subset.

Ripper separates track direction from tilt/torque; Digger deliberately limits drill steering to a downward cone; Lineshank has an aimed bungee harpoon, reel control, blade lift and a release that spends stored tension on a bounded horizontal kick.
WASD, pointer aim, Space/Shift/C, Q/E trim, Z/X reel and brackets/power are the desktop adapters for human-controlled new rigs; the worker never reads raw Input for a policy.
