Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How should a smart model link run at several rates?
```mermaid flowchart TD owner["Arena owner"] --> view["Permitted observation"] view --> reflex["Fresh local reflex"] view --> slow["Slow decision adapter"] slow --> admission["Identity and age checks"] admission --> reflex reflex --> command["Wire command"] command --> owner owner --> judge["Separate evaluator record"] ``` A large decision or vision/language model can propose a goal while a smaller local controller handles fresh observations. The current driver samples humans at 60 Hz, runs scripted/local-reflex/NCA decisions at 10 Hz, and steps motors and materials at 60 Hz. No external service latency is assumed. Current [`smart_link.gd`](../../godot/examples/thunderbowl/smart_link.gd) permits one outstanding request, no more often than every 30 simulation ticks, expiring 120 ticks after its source observation. The request includes `request_id`, run/actor/epoch/observation identity, `observed_tick`, `expires_tick` and the copied permitted observation. A response echoes those identities and supplies `valid_for_ticks` in 1–120 and `intent: {"mode": "pursue_visible", "goal": [0, 0], "speed": 0.65, "engage": true}`. Modes are `hold`, `move_to` and `pursue_visible`; goal components are world-cell coordinates 0–1024. `speed` is normalized drive demand, not guaranteed velocity. Plan expiry stays anchored to the request observation; admitting a late reply does not renew it. A fresh local reflex converts an admitted goal into a new 12-tick motor command and only aims tags at currently visible enemies. Zero drive, `hold`, missing/expired plans or an absent pursuit target cancel armed actions and coast under passive physics. There is no implicit hover, brake or path solver. No owner waits for model inference or a reply. The sample adapter synchronously polls bounded files between arena ticks, so filesystem latency can still delay the next step; this is not asynchronous I/O or a hard real-time guarantee. Log the sensor sample tick, material/render sample age when images are involved, request time, response time, plan admission, local action production and actual command consumption. Measure service latency separately from simulated-time age. A model trained or tested with paused decision time belongs to a different evaluation class from a real-time pilot. The sample file adapter only exercises the decision contract; it does not establish a live LLM, vision encoder, reward trainer or neural service integration.

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > How do the scripted examples behave?
Every physical entry has a deterministic local feedback producer in [`physical_actor_script.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_script.gd). It consumes the same copied pose, velocity, contact, local-ray, resource and attachment observations available to a policy. It cannot read native World, teleport a body, replenish resources or bypass command admission. The scripts patrol relative to their starting location, reverse before a target becomes an asymptotic stopping point, and use actual contact and progress towards the route to decide when to vault or recover. Vertical bouncing against a wall and backward shoves do not disguise a stall; intended climbing, winching and drilling retain their relevant progress directions. A stalled actor gets a debounced escape attempt. Flyers use altitude, velocity, ceiling and attitude feedback; Duet pulse-width modulates its two buttons with collective off periods and an inverted-thrust cutoff. Heavylift reads its connected payload's pose and velocity, reduces acceleration while it swings, and applies a bounded correction beneath an outward-moving load. Rope pilots take up slack from a floor start, pump the observed swing and release during a useful ascent, while Winchbug favours hauling and damping. Charge actions have explicit hold/release phases. A resource hysteresis band suppresses expensive bursts while the reserve recovers. These are energetic demonstration controllers and useful baselines. They are not global route planners. A difficult enclosure can still defeat a local controller; reported obstruction and recovery state allow later policies to make a different decision. No neural training or live LLM inference is supplied by ACT-004.

hits.text: Document: Simulation tick and threading Path: architecture/simulation-tick-and-threading.md authority: current-documentation document-kind: contract status: Current scope: Desktop, Web and native stage ordering, fixed quanta, failure behavior and permitted thread access canonical-for: [simulation-step-order-and-threading] last-reviewed: 2026-11-24 Section: Simulation tick and threading > Physical actor scheduling receipts authorize bounded recoil on the main thread at most once; admission alone does not spend equipment charge or apply recoil. Reset, suspension, cancellation and lease expiry revoke pending control. The session cancellation signal also retires worker effect generations, including requests already copied out of its queue but not yet admitted. For physical usables, the mutex serializes cancellation with material consumption, and extracted work remains in the admission capacity until resolved. Cancellation leaves already committed projectiles and deployed physical devices in the current world; reset/replacement retires that world-owned state. An old epoch cannot actuate new bodies. Desktop still has independently paced physical and cellular timelines, so this is not a claim of lockstep cells/body integration. **Current physical Thunderbowl v2:** [`CyberPhysicalActorArena.step`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_arena.gd) owns one native world and an isolated Rapier space synchronously at 60 Hz: 1. Prepare the occupancy mask from the current actual part poses. 2. Admit policy packets and advance the common actor session without integrating bodies yet; source/muzzle positions still correspond to that mask. 3. Consume bounded effects and physical usable requests against those copied poses, complete one native material tick and apply its cellular responses. 4. Synchronize hard terrain, step Rapier, and publish the next actor observation. Its schedule identifier is `synchronous-mask-actuation-effects-material-feedback-terrain-rapier/v1`. The ACT-005 usable course uses the same synchronous schedule and isolated owners. Its material targets and processor Feed/Jam/Clear actions are explicit bounded fixture authoring; they do not grant actor controllers an additional world-write path. The lab completes all pending bounded terrain chunks before its Rapier step; this makes no desktop frame-time claim. Local material patches disclose both their sample tick and preceding body-mask pose tick. Native failure stops the environment and publishes the failure disposition without another physics step. This separate manoeuvre/usable lab does not change sampled Thunderbowl v1's schedule, rewards or observation privileges, and does not migrate Web control.

Section: Shared Workbench actor composition > Physical equipment and material authority
Compatible physical rigs retain the existing ACT-005 32-item catalogue, mount, hit/mask validation, cooldown, charge, release/attach and native material accounting. The Workbench bridge maps each equipment part to its actual native proxy ID, including offsets after a compound flyer. Main publishes the copied body sample and equipment frame together through the existing worker boundary; native receipts return to the matching session. Physical ACT-004 effects and the ACT-005 engine receive the committed Workbench canvas extent, so valid tools on a 2048 × 1024 landscape are not clipped to a historical 1024-cell laboratory width. Coordinates outside the committed extent still refuse. Sampled actor/usable contracts keep their own bounds. The worker uses the existing cancellation mutex across the bounded physical effect apply, so cancellation cannot overtake validation and leave a late material write. The example gives Runner a Brick Stamper, Crawler a Powder Vacuum and Skimmer a Water Lance. These demonstrate deposition, excavation and liquid emission with native `physical_usables` receipts and `changed_cells`; they do not acquire human paint permissions. Model/tool behavior remains local and resource-bounded. Crawler starts at `(300, 350)` on the solid approach to the granular patch. These ground mechanisms obtain traction from real Rapier hard-terrain or body support. Native granular support alone does not become a grounded contact: placing a rig on a thick loose-powder bed can strand it until legitimate equipment clears enough material. The example preserves that boundary instead of granting a controller artificial traction or material-edit privileges. Autonomous tools never use or capture the human PAINT pointer. Human tools use explicit tool keys/gamepad controls and the observed equipment identity. Workbench also disables the legacy slot-zero mouse equipment adapter: an equipped scripted actor in the first physical slot cannot consume pointer input or have its generation cancelled by the old single-player path. Live source switching preserves the current item. **Apply equipment / restart** is a separate authored prepare operation that changes the starting loadout, retains live material cells/body poses where supported, and explicitly restarts controller/resource state. No item is silently attached to a model without a mount. Native refusal retains the old applied arrangement.

results.query: How do articulated actors wield, aim, recoil, drop and pick up tools, and are all 32 requested usable illustrations functional items?
facts: ACT-005 carries all 32 U01-U32 usables onto real articulated equipment parts, reusing an existing held part or adding one within the eight-part limit. M or left mouse uses, right mouse alternates, N releases and U picks up a nearby part.

Independent equipment aim steers a bounded physical mount; effects use the actual copied muzzle and per-part native source/target masks. Held, released, fixed, deployed and picked-up equipment retains one body ID; pickup checks bounded proximity and clearance without teleporting or resetting velocity.

Run, actor, generation, equipment epoch, instance, body and request identity fence remote work and receipts. Only a matching accepted consumed receipt permits bounded physical recoil once. Cancellation retires pending intent without deleting committed projectile/device state.

Section: Actor usables — 32-item catalogue and physical equipment > Action and readback contract > Physical actions and copied feedback
The physical version-2 `physical_wire_action` envelope carries an optional `equipment` dictionary. The enclosing run, actor epoch, producer, issued observation and lease remain authoritative; there is no second physical policy mailbox with weaker freshness checks. ```gdscript var command = CyberPhysicalActorSession.make_command(view, sequence, { "move": Vector2.RIGHT, "equipment": { "usable_index": view.equipment.usable_index, "instance_id": view.equipment.instance_id, "equipment_epoch": view.equipment.equipment_epoch, "aim": Vector2(1, -0.2), "power": 0.7, "trigger": true, "alternate": false, "drop": false, "attach": false } }, 12) ``` Only the physical owner supplies source positions, mount/body IDs, material effect requests and lifecycle changes. The helper fills missing equipment identity from the copied view; raw external packets must carry it. The worker validates the copied physical frame and request together. At most eight requests are admitted globally, with one unconsumed request per actor, including a request already extracted for the owner to process. Queue admission and the later effect result are distinct; repeated receipt consumption cannot apply recoil twice. Selection/lifecycle transitions advance equipment epochs; cancellation advances the actor control generation. Old observations cannot restore a retired state. Cancellation and finite material-effect consumption share the worker mutex. After cancellation returns, an old pending request cannot commit a later cell edit. This does not roll back already committed projectiles or deployed devices. The exact owners are [`simulation_worker.gd::_set_physical_usable_state_locked/_consume_physical_usables`](../../godot/scripts/simulation_worker.gd), [`physical_usable_runtime.gd::request_error`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_runtime.gd) and [`physical_actor_session.gd::submit`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_session.gd). Copied `observation.equipment` includes identity/usable, owning part and held-body pose, actual and requested aim, joint limits, clearance, release/pickup readiness, charge/cooldown, pending/result/refusal state, recoil and bounded processor or projectile readback. Exact fields and handoff timing belong to [physical equipment interfaces](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-equipment-actions-and-results).

**Current experimental source, USABLE-002 / ACT-005 / #182:** the **32 usables** from USABLE-001 retain their identities and authored semantics: 12 material deposition/destruction tools, 10 ballistic payloads and 10 processors. Physical equipment uses the articulated actor session's command authority. Its aim and power can differ from locomotion aim and effort, so firing a nozzle does not silently retarget a thruster, rope or charged leap. The [dated ACT-005 checkpoint](../audits/2026-10-19-act005-physical-usables.md) owns implementation progress, actual validation and merge status. The catalogue is present in accepted main. Accepted Shared Workbench actor composition (#683) also exposes equipment for actor definitions with a usable mount; its passive barrel and 4LY drones do not gain a mount through the picker. The later Equipment and Actor Compose repair candidates (#724 and #762) remain separate from this accepted behavior. The [current-state register](../reference/status-and-roadmap.md) owns their live status. The executable catalogue is [`usable_catalog.gd`](../../godot/scripts/usable_catalog.gd), bounded gameplay is owned by [`usable_runtime.gd`](../../godot/scripts/usable_runtime.gd). The physical owner in [`physical_usable_equipment.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_equipment.gd) manages a real held part, joint aiming, lifecycle and recoil. The worker-owned [`physical_usable_runtime.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_runtime.gd) reuses the authored effects while resolving source clearance and hits against actual part occupancy. The simulation worker alone queries or mutates its cellular World; policies receive copied observations. The retained sampled actor route still uses [`usable_session.gd`](../../godot/scripts/usable_session.gd) and its separate epoch/sequence/lease stream. Its old axis-aligned actor hull and logical device placement are compatibility behavior; physical equipment does not borrow those spatial or ownership assumptions. Neither route exposes a Rapier RID or live body reference to a producer.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > Physical Thunderbowl v2 > Physical usable course
The launcher entry **Physical usable course — 32 tools, payloads and processors** opens the same physical scene in its **Usable integration course** mode. The scene's **Manoeuvre lab / Usable integration course** selector resets the environment into the selected authored layout. All 46 rigs retain their catalogue loadout and the same human/demo/policy admission path; the course does not provide a separate actor controller with direct material access. ```text godot --headless --path godot --script res://examples/thunderbowl/run_physical_thunderbowl.gd -- --course=usables-v1 --rig=digger --actors=8 --ticks=600 --seed=0 --output=physical-usable-result.json ``` [`CyberPhysicalUsableCourse`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_course.gd) defines bounded native material fixtures and a varied default roster. The eight sections expose different interactions: | Section | Observable interaction | |---|---| | Bore / Cut | Editable packed-earth seams for advancing excavation rigs | | Sort / Drain | Powder, glass and liquid targets for selective material work | | Penetrate | Separate editable leaves for swept projectile penetration | | Ricochet | Protected hard faces for damped bounce and physical firing recoil | | Stage / Burst | Flight space for fuse, airburst and staged ignition behavior | | Drop / Deposit | Receiving bins for downward payloads and native deposits | | Release / Grip | Same-body release, retained momentum and nearby physical reattachment | | Place / Jam | A service pad for dropping, settling, fixing and operating processors | For a deployed processor belonging to the selected follow actor, **Feed processor**, **Jam output** and **Clear output** perform explicit bounded fixture edits at the current physical ports. Feed uses that device's real material recipe; Jam/Clear expose the existing rule that blocked outputs prevent input consumption. These are visible authoring controls, separate from the actor's copied local observation and equipment actions. They do not imply autonomous material creation or a general inventory economy. Course configuration adds `"course": "usables-v1"` to the physical version-2 environment schema. Equipment observations, requests, receipts and native processor state follow the [physical equipment interface](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-equipment-actions-and-results). Body pose, joint aim, charged resources and native changes remain separate observable facts; the course has no virtual combat score or automatic assertion that every scripted actor completed every section. Acceptance is recorded in the [ACT-005 audit](../audits/2026-10-19-act005-physical-usables.md), with [focused validation commands](../operations/local-build-and-validation.md#physical-usable-validation).

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > Which usable examples exist?
**Current experimental ACT-005 source:** the entire [U01-U32 catalogue](actor-usables.md) is selectable on physical equipment. Every rig has a defined default loadout in [`physical_usable_loadouts.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_loadouts.gd). Each loadout names its usable, power, strategy and purpose; no physical actor is left with an unspecified equipment policy. SetP explicitly starts with an empty mount and human movement strategy; F5 can still select ordinary equipment. Mount definitions bind a specific host/held part, grip, joint, aiming limits and clearance. The equipment owner aims the actual configured joint when it supports aiming. The shot direction comes from the current held body's pose; a limited joint cannot acquire an unlimited virtual muzzle. The suspended payload, hammer and blade preserve their authored mechanical roles. A selection change retools the existing held chassis without allocating another body. Release clears the held connection and retains the same object, pose, velocity and body ID. A short collision grace ages with physical time even after input cancellation. Pickup checks the owning grip's proximity and terrain clearance; it does not teleport the object or reset its velocity. An already held, remote, occluded or ambiguously owned item is refused. A released chassis must return before it can select another usable. Processors are deployed by dropping that real body, waiting for supported settling, and fixing it at its current pose. A worker receipt admits processing; blocked output leaves recipe inputs and stock unchanged. The body and its rotated intake/output ports remain visible while it works, jams or exhausts. Physical pickup retires processing authority. See the [processor contract](actor-usables.md#u23u32-fixed-functional-objects). The main-thread owner applies recoil once for the matching admitted use. Native material effects use copied physical source/part information under worker ownership. Protected cells, foreign part occupancy, bounds and source clearance remain checked. The physical command, worker admission and changed-cell receipt are separate results; a valid command does not guarantee an unobstructed effect. Late receipts are fenced by run, actor, control generation, equipment epoch and request identity. The older ACT-004 direct mount/effect fixtures retain their bounded deposit/cut/rocket-charge substrate for regression; it is not a second unleased policy API for the full catalogue.

The physical lab has no competitive tag rewards, damage, metal, oracle, NCA or live model service; sampled v1 examples retain their original independent contracts.

**Current experimental ACT-004/ACT-005:** the separate physical lab uses all 46 [articulated Rapier actors](physical-actor-rigs.md), their actual jointed parts, native materials and the same human/demo/policy session as F5. It owns a native world and an isolated Rapier space. Its purpose is manoeuvre, recovery and usable testing. It has no virtual tag score, damage/reward system, metal lane, oracle team, NCA controller or live model service. Those sampled v1 examples remain independently runnable below. The five SetP entries are human movement presets with explicitly empty starting mounts; the original ACT-005 41-rig tool loadouts remain defined. Their separate [seven-preset playground](player-control-playground.md) also includes Sand/Water fields that are not physical Thunderbowl actors. Earlier dated lab results retain their original roster and source scope. Run the physical scene from the launcher or directly. In these examples, `godot` means the [repository-pinned executable](../operations/getting-started.md), with the matching native and Rapier libraries: ```text godot --path godot res://examples/thunderbowl/physical_thunderbowl.tscn godot --headless --path godot --script res://examples/thunderbowl/run_physical_thunderbowl.gd -- --rig=ripper --actors=4 --ticks=600 --seed=0 --output=physical-result.json ``` The UI picker selects the 46 `RIG_IDS` and one through eight actors. Its retained small header still says 41; the catalogue and picker include the five SetP rigs. This picker is distinct from F5's additional 4LY group and Workbench's mixed catalogue. Actor zero may be human, demo or policy; companion actors use the local scripted examples. Whole arena/follow cameras and collider outlines show the actual parts. Click the arena to arm human control. WASD, mouse, Space/Shift/C, Q/E, Z/X and brackets match F5; M uses the tool, N releases a held object, U reattaches a nearby one. ACT-005 gives actor zero the full equipment picker and independent equipment power. Left mouse or M triggers primary use; right mouse requests the usable's alternate action. Selection and use enter the same physical session as demo and policy actions. Pause, cancel, focus changes and reset revoke pending control through the owner. The whole-arena camera is evaluator information, so human play is not an equal-perception policy benchmark. [`CyberPhysicalActorArena`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_arena.gd) exposes `configure`, `reset`, `observation`, `submit`, `cancel`, `set_paused`, `step`, `snapshot` and `close`. Configuration has this shape: ```json { "version": 2, "seed": 0, "max_ticks": 600, "local_patch_radius": 6, "actors": [ {"model": "ripper", "producer": "policy"}, {"model": "copter", "producer": "demo"} ] } ``` Actor positions may optionally be explicit finite `[x,y]` coordinates in the authored arena. Unknown fields and invalid capacities are refused before replacing a live environment. `submit(command, producer)` and `step(policy_commands)` consume the same version-2 issued-observation envelope as the desktop [physical command interface](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-actor-control-and-effects). Model names alone never invoke model APIs. `observation(actor_id)` contains the copied local rig view plus a bounded square native material/body-ID

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > How should the control modes be classified?
Human fly-by-wire, a central oracle, an NCA and an emergent swarm describe different properties. Classify them on independent axes before comparing presets. | Axis | Meaning | Examples | |---|---|---| | Actuation lane | What commands reach the motor, with which assists and limits? | High-level wire intent; direct metal actuator channels | | Decision placement | Where are decisions made and which actors share a decision process? | Human pilot; one independent controller per actor; central team controller | | Perception privilege | What information may that decision process receive? | Own state; filtered nearby observations; camera image; full present-state oracle | | Coordination | What agent-to-agent or environment-mediated information changes decisions? | None; shared altered terrain; designed neighbor steering; bounded messages | | Controller family | What computes a decision from its permitted inputs? | Hand-authored reflex; search; recurrent neural policy; NCA-inspired graph; vision/language planner | | Training privilege | What information was used to produce the deployed controller? | No training; local rollouts; global critic; full-state teacher | A central process can aggregate only permitted local views and still lack oracle knowledge. Independent actor processes can each receive full state and therefore be privileged. Shared neural weights do not mean shared runtime memory. Human input can feed either actuation lane if that rig exposes the lane. The same local controller can be compared with and without communication while preserving its motor and sensory capabilities. Keep the actuation lane fixed for an actor's configured lifetime. Wire inputs request rig behavior: movement, aim, effort, trim, reel and the three action buttons. Metal inputs address the supported rig's direct actuators and bypass the high-level behavior dispatch. A force or torque expressed in game units is only meaningful with the published mass, inertia, channel map and integration law. It must not be described as a physical SI quantity or a Rapier force when the motor is an authored sampled approximation.

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > What does the arena publish and resolve?
[`CyberThunderbowlArena`](../../godot/scripts/thunderbowl_arena.gd) exposes `configure(config)`, `observation(actor_id)`, `snapshot()`, `step(commands)` and `close()`. A successful configuration installs an exclusive native world and actor session; a refused configuration preserves the existing instance. Each `step` advances one 1/60-second motor/material tick, with at most eight commands. An oversized batch is refused as a whole. Failed material ticks quarantine the owner and retain the last completed actor/reward publication. | Published view | Contents and permission | |---|---| | Every policy observation | Run/actor/epoch/tick/observation identity; assigned model, lane, team and view mode; own alive/HP/tag readiness; own 40-value rig state and 32-value actuation state/profile | | Own terrain stencil | 9×9 material samples spaced four cells, with explicit origin; this is a sampled 32-cell span, not every intervening cell | | `self` | Empty neighbor and message arrays | | `local` | Up to seven alive neighbors within 64 cells and clear terrain LOS; visible ID/team, relative center, velocity, body size and rotation; no neighbor HP, energy, actions or hidden state | | `oracle` addition | All actors' current 40-value states, HP and alive status, plus a 32×18 terrain grid sampled every eight cells; not every native cell or future state | | Evaluator `snapshot()` | Full copied actor/session state, HP, rewards, tags, bounded events, admission/work counters, layout and material hashes; never the ordinary local-policy input | Neighbor order is actor-ID order. LOS uses bounded supercover rays and treats any non-Empty material as blocking. At most 8,192 sensor and 10,752 tag cell reads are available per completed tick; exhaustion refuses visibility/hits. Optional full-arena presentation samples are separately bounded and excluded from those policy-sensing budgets. Virtual tags require a rising edge, nonzero aim, range ≤56 cells, aim dot product ≥0.94, clear LOS and a 30-tick cooldown. The nearest eligible opponent center is selected; a shot attempt consumes cooldown even on a miss. Each actor starts with three HP. Simultaneous hits resolve before eliminations: each hit gives +1/−1 reward, and an elimination's +2 bonus is shared among that tick's attackers; the victim loses two more. Ring-out costs two and eliminates the actor. Elimination cancels input and marks virtual status; it does not remove a native body or slot.

Section: Level saves and exact replay > What does import validate, and what stays intact on failure?
The codec checks lengths, header/version fields, checksum, decompression and bounded metadata types/ranges. Native validation checks exact payload length and legal material IDs (`0…131` except reserved `10`). Selected-material metadata accepts paintable IDs through `CyberCellWorld.LAST_MATERIAL`; Empty remains an invalid selection. Constructor IDs are range-checked before narrowing, so a wide integer cannot wrap into a valid material. Validation does not implement a complete semantic schema for every material's two state bytes. The MAT-002 catalogue extension changes the accepted IDs, not the CYSD1 header or five-byte cell encoding. Existing levels remain readable. Older runtimes whose catalogue ends at 80 reject levels containing the new materials; they do not gain support from the unchanged format version alone. `CyberDemoBridge::import_level` validates and builds a replacement World and render exchange before no-throw ownership swaps. CYSD1 stores no liquid solver policy: this original API reconstructs every liquid's default family (LCB NC-10), whatever the live World's policy. Invalid codec/native payloads leave the active World intact. The Web controller rejects a Physics Pit save when Rapier is unavailable before native import. This guarantee concerns the checked import paths; it is not a general transaction guarantee for simulation ticks or arbitrary later scene allocation failures. **Current bounded unmerged #202 source:** the normal synchronous application's liquid panel can explicitly arm the next ordinary body-free import with a copied policy, normalization opt-in and geometry in Exploratory mode. The separate `prepare_liquid_level` API preserves thermal tuples and stages native World, sampled player, metadata-derived execution and qualified host observation before the final commit. Refusal retains the prior World/player/receipt/record. The [prepared import contract](../architecture/liquid-prepared-setup-and-receipts.md#explicit-ordinary-level-import-and-retained-restart) owns those bounds and unsupported body/Tower/showcase routes. Restart retains the accepted in-memory payload and selection; CYSD1 serialization is unchanged and unarmed import still uses Current defaults. No full replay or browser/release qualification follows from this opt-in reconstruction. The follow-up preflight explicitly refuses unsupported inherited interaction, diagnostic-law or independent transport settings rather than replacing them with preparation defaults. The accepted private Baseline may restart only with matching native component/generation/receipt identity. Unarmed legacy import continues to preserve its inherited configuration. Optional enabled preparation telemetry is observational and remains qualified separately. Section: Owner authoring and world intent — 14 November 2026 > Paint, play and the Workbench
**Confirmed:** CyberSand is a paint-and-play engine as an authoring system. Workbench is the creative workshop, control centre and monitoring outpost, with creative-mode and development/cheat-level control in an ergonomic interface. Make valuable capabilities compatible with and accessible through Workbench. Provide easy-to-learn, multiple levels of access to dials, modifiers and controls, while allowing deeper manipulation. Painting should develop toward the range between classic MSPaint and GIMP/Krita. The engine should remain flexible across a passive plasma chamber, a forest drone game, a digging game and other experiments. The owner wants continued integration, testing, tuning and incremental improvements while personally evaluating authored scenes. **Game-facing scoring and consequential player/actor combat damage wait until the arrangements, materials and actors feel fun.** This is not a prohibition on internal diagnostic or training metrics. **Confirmed near-term interest:** revisit NPC controllers, Rapier actors and drone training. Envisaged authoring roles include conversational autofill, automated feature/flavour/item generation, and tiny/local models for detailing, texture and randomisation. Model roles may evolve; these are not permanent capability claims about any model or instructions to start training.

Section: Reproducible physics characterisation > Which checks guard the measurement path?
The standalone native CLI accepts current catalogue IDs `0..131` except reserved ID `10`. It validates signed wide arguments before narrowing, and its sampled `counts` and `sum_y` arrays each contain 132 entries. This current output extent does not revise historical 81-slot records or the intentionally 81-entry transport profile. The named issue #9/#10 reducers remain scoped to their original fixture series; arbitrary building-material experiments require a matching consumer. Run `make physics-characterisation-test` and `make physics-characterisation-sanitize` to compile and exercise the actual CLI. The [executable-level oracle](../../tools/physics/test_characterisation_cli.py) checks all 51 building IDs in both fixture layers, old-ID controls and invalid wide, reserved and malformed inputs. It parses the JSON rows and independently checks rectangle counts, sum-Y/centroid accounting, complete observation totals and rejection before any fixture output. The sanitized target uses ASan/UBSan; set `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:strict_string_checks=1` in a supported execution environment to include LeakSanitizer. Each oracle child uses the shared `operation_seconds` watchdog (300 seconds at this source), as recorded in its result. Read the actual value with `python3 tools/ci/execution_policy.py seconds operation_seconds`; the old ten-second description is obsolete. Results, commands, executable hash and individual stdout/stderr are retained under `build/physics-cli-validation/`; Native CI uploads this evidence. The [MAT-002 review record](../audits/2026-10-19-mat002-review-and-validation.md) preserves the pre-fix overflow and separately identifies successful reruns. Use the [source-native and Godot validation entry points](testing-validation-and-replay.md) with a source-matched runtime; rebuild when relevant inputs changed. Companion `dev.cmd` aliases are optional. Existing coverage includes exact native cell/state and histogram parity, diagnostics enabled/disabled comparisons, Mercury confined vertical controls, explicit histogram overflow, masked-source characterization, stored Water under masks, invalid-reset preservation, exact coupled trajectories with one/four workers, duplicate suppression and hard-floor control. Existing failed-tick quarantine, region re-entry, conservation and render ownership fixtures remain required. Use the [dated report](../audits/2026-09-09-physics-characterisation.md) for actual passes and remaining platform/fixture gaps; do not reuse earlier test totals. [platforms.py](../../tools/physics/platforms.py) reduces the actual browser/async JSON and copies their captured runtime identities into the curated output. It expects `runtime-checkpoint/manifest.json`, `desktop-async-final/provenance/manifest.json` and the named raw platform result folders. The [Water accounting JSON](../../tools/physics/water-accounting.json) is directly accepted by `test_physics_characterisation.gd`; construct its output directory, capture a fresh manifest and pass those two paths after Godot's `--` separator. Run [verify.py](../../tools/physics/verify.py) against the complete named raw series before publishing reduced results. [capture.py](../../tools/physics/capture.py) retains source deltas, new fixture files, dependencies and artifact hashes before standalone/async/browser runs. The async CLI and trace allocator reject horizons outside 1..7,200 ticks and the CLI rejects seed counts outside 1..20. Construct the output directory before invoking Godot directly. Generator/default budgets remain distinct from production worker, terrain and gameplay queue capacities.

The shared apply seam publishes current frame settings before preparation captures its revision, fixing first-render construction retirement reproduced in Xvfb. Section: Testing, validation, and replay > CI execution sharding
The accepted [GDExtension workflow](../../.github/workflows/gdextension.yml) uses source-derived Linux and Windows matrices from [godot_job_plan.py](../../tools/ci/godot_job_plan.py). Sharding changes execution schedule; it does not weaken assertions, omit unknown tests or turn a missing readback into a pass. Each shard has its own import. Every assigned original case must appear exactly once in the complete source/run/attempt evidence. [Linux](../../tools/ci/verify_linux_godot_shards.py) and [Windows](../../tools/ci/verify_windows_godot_shards.py) independent readers check original logs, complete assignments, runtime identity and natural completion. `max-parallel` caps simultaneous jobs, while the planner determines the actual number of shards and parent budgets. The old fixed four-shard examples are historical migration evidence. [CI execution policy](ci-execution-and-performance.md) owns current budget arithmetic and scheduling; open optimization experiments are not adopted policy. Linux rendered cases use a display and the OpenGL compatibility renderer. Missing display, explicit skip, timeout, nonzero exit, engine/script error, incomplete readback and cleanup failure retain their failure meaning. Software-rendered pixels are evidence for that backend, not target-GPU performance or playfeel. `--keep-going` preserves later outcomes after ordinary case failure; failed import stops the shard because the test project was not prepared. The Windows helper receives a source-built candidate in accepted CI and can also validate a retained runtime through its explicit alternative path. Windows headless execution, cross-build validation and graphical qualification remain separate claims. Source/runtime mismatch fails admission before a runtime pass can be claimed. The [build guide](local-build-and-validation.md#windows-retained-runtime-execution) owns invocation and artifact details.

results.query: Which actor tools, projectile payloads and functional processors exist, and who owns their material edits, triggers and bounded work?
facts: The catalogue contains 12 material tools, 10 swept ballistic payloads and 10 fixed processors/responders with stable U01-U32 identities. ACT-005 binds the complete catalogue to physical equipment while retaining the sampled USABLE-001 route.

Physical equipment actions use the shared physical issued-observation envelope with explicit equipment identity, independent aim and power. The retained sampled session has its own actor epoch/sequence/lease stream. Only the serialized cellular owner performs material queries and writes.

Committed projectiles/devices survive input release, freeze on pause and clear with their World/reset lifetime. Real processors drop, settle and fix before worker admission; complete batch preflight and blocked outputs prevent partial consumption.

The launcher entry **Physical usable course — 32 tools, payloads and processors** opens the same physical scene in its **Usable integration course** mode. The scene's **Manoeuvre lab / Usable integration course** selector resets the environment into the selected authored layout. All 46 rigs retain their catalogue loadout and the same human/demo/policy admission path; the course does not provide a separate actor controller with direct material access. ```text godot --headless --path godot --script res://examples/thunderbowl/run_physical_thunderbowl.gd -- --course=usables-v1 --rig=digger --actors=8 --ticks=600 --seed=0 --output=physical-usable-result.json ``` [`CyberPhysicalUsableCourse`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_course.gd) defines bounded native material fixtures and a varied default roster. The eight sections expose different interactions: | Section | Observable interaction | |---|---| | Bore / Cut | Editable packed-earth seams for advancing excavation rigs | | Sort / Drain | Powder, glass and liquid targets for selective material work | | Penetrate | Separate editable leaves for swept projectile penetration | | Ricochet | Protected hard faces for damped bounce and physical firing recoil | | Stage / Burst | Flight space for fuse, airburst and staged ignition behavior | | Drop / Deposit | Receiving bins for downward payloads and native deposits | | Release / Grip | Same-body release, retained momentum and nearby physical reattachment | | Place / Jam | A service pad for dropping, settling, fixing and operating processors | For a deployed processor belonging to the selected follow actor, **Feed processor**, **Jam output** and **Clear output** perform explicit bounded fixture edits at the current physical ports. Feed uses that device's real material recipe; Jam/Clear expose the existing rule that blocked outputs prevent input consumption. These are visible authoring controls, separate from the actor's copied local observation and equipment actions. They do not imply autonomous material creation or a general inventory economy. Course configuration adds `"course": "usables-v1"` to the physical version-2 environment schema. Equipment observations, requests, receipts and native processor state follow the [physical equipment interface](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-equipment-actions-and-results). Body pose, joint aim, charged resources and native changes remain separate observable facts; the course has no virtual combat score or automatic assertion that every scripted actor completed every section. Acceptance is recorded in the [ACT-005 audit](../audits/2026-10-19-act005-physical-usables.md), with [focused validation commands](../operations/local-build-and-validation.md#physical-usable-validation).

Units are gameplay cells, seconds and authored charge; recipe accounting is authored cell slots. | Boundary | Current value and consequence | |---|---| | Equipment actor slots | 8; follows the actor-session count | | Committed projectiles | 64 globally | | Fixed processors | 16 globally; at most 4 owned by one actor | | Visual effects / hit receipts | 64 / 64 | | Material work | At most 2,048 reads and 128 writes per equipment owner step | | Swept projectile trace | At most 96 samples per movement segment | | Accepted delta | At most 1/15 second | | Shared equipment charge | 100 maximum; Section: Actor usables — 32-item catalogue and physical equipment > U13–U22: ballistic payloads
Projectiles are sparse bounded records with swept cell-space contact, gravity, lifetime and explicit state transitions. They are separate from the native pixel-material `Rocket`. | Ref / ID | Usable | Activation | |---|---|---| | U13 `impact_slug` | Impact Slug | First editable contact chips a small footprint. | | U14 `borer_round` | Borer Round | Up to three editable penetrations, losing speed after each. | | U15 `ricochet_pellet` | Ricochet Pellet | Up to two damped terrain bounces. | | U16 `sticky_delay_charge` | Sticky Delay Charge | First contact sticks; 0.55 s simulation-time fuse excavates locally. Alternate activation fires the oldest eligible owned charge early. | | U17 `timer_airburst` | Timer Airburst | 0.45 s flight fuse splits into five bounded child chip shots. Alternate activation bursts the oldest live owned canister early. | | U18 `water_capsule` | Water Capsule | Contact releases Water into nearby available cells. | | U19 `oil_igniter` | Oil Igniter | Contact deposits Oil; 0.35 s later it attempts one Fire pulse. Alternate activation fires the oldest primed owned payload early. | | U20 `seed_pod` | Seed Pod | Contact disperses Seed locally. | | U21 `cement_blob` | Cement Blob | Heavy short-range Cement payload. | | U22 `water_contact_charge` | Water Contact Charge | Contact arms the carrier; nearby Water or Brine triggers one Fire pulse. | A swept non-owner actor contact publishes a bounded hit receipt containing tick, owner, target, projectile and usable identity. Physical hits also identify the target body part. Accepted physical use applies bounded recoil through the main-thread equipment owner. The catalogue does **not** add health, damage numbers or a general damage/impact impulse system. Fuse time is simulation time and still advances if the movement read budget is exhausted; position remains at the last verified point. Collision sweep examines the valid in-bounds segment before discarding an out-of-world endpoint. Early activation of an eligible committed U16/U17/U19 payload is independent of new-launch charge, cooldown, power and muzzle clearance. It still requires the current held equipment identity and an active command lease, and adds no launch recoil. A zero-power primary use is refused; processor placement rejects it before releasing the physical chassis.

results.query: Can a delayed physical equipment request or receipt fire a replaced, dropped or cancelled tool, and how is the worker queue bounded?
facts: Physical actions share issued-observation identity and additionally carry usable_index, instance_id and equipment_epoch; copied requests and receipts are scoped to run, actor, generation, equipment/body identity and request ID.
Worker admission is atomic for at most eight requests globally and one pending request per actor, counting extracted in-flight work. Explicit refusals do not replace already admitted queued work.

Cancellation is serialized with material consumption; old generations, expired leases, reset epochs and duplicate receipts cannot apply a new transaction or repeat recoil. Already committed projectiles and devices remain until their normal or World lifetime ends.

The following F5 and pointer controls belong to the ordinary sandbox and standalone scenes that use its actor picker. Open **F5**, select the actor rig as usual, then choose equipment. **Equip only** changes the current human actor through its admitted equipment action. A physical item can be changed only while its chassis is held; a dropped or deployed object must be recovered first. The same chassis and existing shared equipment charge remain in use when its selected usable changes. - pointer position supplies equipment aim; - left mouse is primary activation; - right mouse is a tool precision pulse or supported early payload activation; - **N** drops the physical held item and **U** requests nearby pickup; processor primary starts physical placement, while sampled processors retain right-click logical retrieval; - equipment power is independent from movement effort; - tools repeat while held; projectiles and deployments consume a press edge; - choosing **None** returns the pointer to painting only after the owner publishes the unequipped selection and all pointer buttons have been released. While equipment is selected, ordinary world painting is suppressed. Focus loss, blocking UI, pause, reset or stale input cancels held equipment input. Already launched projectiles and deployed devices are owner state, not held input: they continue after release/cancellation, freeze while simulation is paused and clear on a fresh actor/World reset. Cancelled physical input retires pending requests and late receipts without teleporting a released body or erasing actor momentum. Changing equipment while a trigger is held requires release before rearming.

The physical version-2 `physical_wire_action` envelope carries an optional `equipment` dictionary. The enclosing run, actor epoch, producer, issued observation and lease remain authoritative; there is no second physical policy mailbox with weaker freshness checks. ```gdscript var command = CyberPhysicalActorSession.make_command(view, sequence, { "move": Vector2.RIGHT, "equipment": { "usable_index": view.equipment.usable_index, "instance_id": view.equipment.instance_id, "equipment_epoch": view.equipment.equipment_epoch, "aim": Vector2(1, -0.2), "power": 0.7, "trigger": true, "alternate": false, "drop": false, "attach": false } }, 12) ``` Only the physical owner supplies source positions, mount/body IDs, material effect requests and lifecycle changes. The helper fills missing equipment identity from the copied view; raw external packets must carry it. The worker validates the copied physical frame and request together. At most eight requests are admitted globally, with one unconsumed request per actor, including a request already extracted for the owner to process. Queue admission and the later effect result are distinct; repeated receipt consumption cannot apply recoil twice. Selection/lifecycle transitions advance equipment epochs; cancellation advances the actor control generation. Old observations cannot restore a retired state. Cancellation and finite material-effect consumption share the worker mutex. After cancellation returns, an old pending request cannot commit a later cell edit. This does not roll back already committed projectiles or deployed devices. The exact owners are [`simulation_worker.gd::_set_physical_usable_state_locked/_consume_physical_usables`](../../godot/scripts/simulation_worker.gd), [`physical_usable_runtime.gd::request_error`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_runtime.gd) and [`physical_actor_session.gd::submit`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_session.gd). Copied `observation.equipment` includes identity/usable, owning part and held-body pose, actual and requested aim, joint limits, clearance, release/pickup readiness, charge/cooldown, pending/result/refusal state, recoil and bounded processor or projectile readback. Section: Shared Workbench actor composition > Physical equipment and material authority
Compatible physical rigs retain the existing ACT-005 32-item catalogue, mount, hit/mask validation, cooldown, charge, release/attach and native material accounting. The Workbench bridge maps each equipment part to its actual native proxy ID, including offsets after a compound flyer. Main publishes the copied body sample and equipment frame together through the existing worker boundary; native receipts return to the matching session. Physical ACT-004 effects and the ACT-005 engine receive the committed Workbench canvas extent, so valid tools on a 2048 × 1024 landscape are not clipped to a historical 1024-cell laboratory width. Coordinates outside the committed extent still refuse. Sampled actor/usable contracts keep their own bounds. The worker uses the existing cancellation mutex across the bounded physical effect apply, so cancellation cannot overtake validation and leave a late material write. The example gives Runner a Brick Stamper, Crawler a Powder Vacuum and Skimmer a Water Lance. These demonstrate deposition, excavation and liquid emission with native `physical_usables` receipts and `changed_cells`; they do not acquire human paint permissions. Model/tool behavior remains local and resource-bounded. Crawler starts at `(300, 350)` on the solid approach to the granular patch. These ground mechanisms obtain traction from real Rapier hard-terrain or body support. Native granular support alone does not become a grounded contact: placing a rig on a thick loose-powder bed can strand it until legitimate equipment clears enough material. The example preserves that boundary instead of granting a controller artificial traction or material-edit privileges. Autonomous tools never use or capture the human PAINT pointer. Human tools use explicit tool keys/gamepad controls and the observed equipment identity. Workbench also disables the legacy slot-zero mouse equipment adapter: an equipped scripted actor in the first physical slot cannot consume pointer input or have its generation cancelled by the old single-player path. Live source switching preserves the current item. **Apply equipment / restart** is a separate authored prepare operation that changes the starting loadout, retains live material cells/body poses where supported, and explicitly restarts controller/resource state. No item is silently attached to a model without a mount. Native refusal retains the old applied arrangement.

results.query: Does picking up a real deployed processor refill its stock, and how do rotated ports, settling and output jams affect material consumption?
facts: A processor is the same coupled body across held, released, fixed, deployed and nearby pickup states. It must remain supported within bounded linear/angular speed for eight consecutive ticks before fixing; distant or obstructed pickup is refused.
Worker admission checks the fixed physical source and four distinct exterior ports rotated from the actual body pose. It preflights every input/output cell; a blocked output consumes no inputs.

Bounded per-actor/per-processor history retains stock, age, cycles and cooldown across pickup, redeployment and selection. Same/older equipment epochs and exhausted deployment are refused; exhausted physical objects remain observable and inert until their physical owner retires them.

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > Which usable examples exist?
**Current experimental ACT-005 source:** the entire [U01-U32 catalogue](actor-usables.md) is selectable on physical equipment. Every rig has a defined default loadout in [`physical_usable_loadouts.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_loadouts.gd). Each loadout names its usable, power, strategy and purpose; no physical actor is left with an unspecified equipment policy. SetP explicitly starts with an empty mount and human movement strategy; F5 can still select ordinary equipment. Mount definitions bind a specific host/held part, grip, joint, aiming limits and clearance. The equipment owner aims the actual configured joint when it supports aiming. The shot direction comes from the current held body's pose; a limited joint cannot acquire an unlimited virtual muzzle. The suspended payload, hammer and blade preserve their authored mechanical roles. A selection change retools the existing held chassis without allocating another body. Release clears the held connection and retains the same object, pose, velocity and body ID. A short collision grace ages with physical time even after input cancellation. Pickup checks the owning grip's proximity and terrain clearance; it does not teleport the object or reset its velocity. An already held, remote, occluded or ambiguously owned item is refused. A released chassis must return before it can select another usable. Processors are deployed by dropping that real body, waiting for supported settling, and fixing it at its current pose. A worker receipt admits processing; blocked output leaves recipe inputs and stock unchanged. The body and its rotated intake/output ports remain visible while it works, jams or exhausts. Physical pickup retires processing authority. See the [processor contract](actor-usables.md#u23u32-fixed-functional-objects). The main-thread owner applies recoil once for the matching admitted use. Native material effects use copied physical source/part information under worker ownership. Protected cells, foreign part occupancy, bounds and source clearance remain checked. The physical command, worker admission and changed-cell receipt are separate results; a valid command does not guarantee an unobstructed effect. Late receipts are fenced by run, actor, control generation, equipment epoch and request identity. The older ACT-004 direct mount/effect fixtures retain their bounded deposit/cut/rocket-charge substrate for regression; it is not a second unleased policy API for the full catalogue.

The launcher entry **Physical usable course — 32 tools, payloads and processors** opens the same physical scene in its **Usable integration course** mode. The scene's **Manoeuvre lab / Usable integration course** selector resets the environment into the selected authored layout. All 46 rigs retain their catalogue loadout and the same human/demo/policy admission path; the course does not provide a separate actor controller with direct material access. ```text godot --headless --path godot --script res://examples/thunderbowl/run_physical_thunderbowl.gd -- --course=usables-v1 --rig=digger --actors=8 --ticks=600 --seed=0 --output=physical-usable-result.json ``` [`CyberPhysicalUsableCourse`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_course.gd) defines bounded native material fixtures and a varied default roster. The eight sections expose different interactions: | Section | Observable interaction | |---|---| | Bore / Cut | Editable packed-earth seams for advancing excavation rigs | | Sort / Drain | Powder, glass and liquid targets for selective material work | | Penetrate | Separate editable leaves for swept projectile penetration | | Ricochet | Protected hard faces for damped bounce and physical firing recoil | | Stage / Burst | Flight space for fuse, airburst and staged ignition behavior | | Drop / Deposit | Receiving bins for downward payloads and native deposits | | Release / Grip | Same-body release, retained momentum and nearby physical reattachment | | Place / Jam | A service pad for dropping, settling, fixing and operating processors | For a deployed processor belonging to the selected follow actor, **Feed processor**, **Jam output** and **Clear output** perform explicit bounded fixture edits at the current physical ports. Feed uses that device's real material recipe; Jam/Clear expose the existing rule that blocked outputs prevent input consumption. These are visible authoring controls, separate from the actor's copied local observation and equipment actions. They do not imply autonomous material creation or a general inventory economy. Course configuration adds `"course": "usables-v1"` to the physical version-2 environment schema. Equipment observations, requests, receipts and native processor state follow the [physical equipment interface](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-equipment-actions-and-results). Body pose, joint aim, charged resources and native changes remain separate observable facts; the course has no virtual combat score or automatic assertion that every scripted actor completed every section. Acceptance is recorded in the [ACT-005 audit](../audits/2026-10-19-act005-physical-usables.md), with [focused validation commands](../operations/local-build-and-validation.md#physical-usable-validation).

Section: Thunderbowl actor arena and control reference > Physical Thunderbowl v2
**Current experimental ACT-004/ACT-005:** the separate physical lab uses all 46 [articulated Rapier actors](physical-actor-rigs.md), their actual jointed parts, native materials and the same human/demo/policy session as F5. It owns a native world and an isolated Rapier space. Its purpose is manoeuvre, recovery and usable testing. It has no virtual tag score, damage/reward system, metal lane, oracle team, NCA controller or live model service. Those sampled v1 examples remain independently runnable below. The five SetP entries are human movement presets with explicitly empty starting mounts; the original ACT-005 41-rig tool loadouts remain defined. Their separate [seven-preset playground](player-control-playground.md) also includes Sand/Water fields that are not physical Thunderbowl actors. Earlier dated lab results retain their original roster and source scope. Run the physical scene from the launcher or directly. In these examples, `godot` means the [repository-pinned executable](../operations/getting-started.md), with the matching native and Rapier libraries: ```text godot --path godot res://examples/thunderbowl/physical_thunderbowl.tscn godot --headless --path godot --script res://examples/thunderbowl/run_physical_thunderbowl.gd -- --rig=ripper --actors=4 --ticks=600 --seed=0 --output=physical-result.json ``` The UI picker selects the 46 `RIG_IDS` and one through eight actors. Its retained small header still says 41; the catalogue and picker include the five SetP rigs. This picker is distinct from F5's additional 4LY group and Workbench's mixed catalogue. Actor zero may be human, demo or policy; companion actors use the local scripted examples. Whole arena/follow cameras and collider outlines show the actual parts. Click the arena to arm human control. WASD, mouse, Space/Shift/C, Q/E, Z/X and brackets match F5; M uses the tool, N releases a held object, U reattaches a nearby one. ACT-005 gives actor zero the full equipment picker and independent equipment power. Left mouse or M triggers primary use; right mouse requests the usable's alternate action. Selection and use enter the same physical session as demo and policy actions. Pause, cancel, focus changes and reset revoke pending control through the owner. The whole-arena camera is evaluator information, so human play is not an equal-perception policy benchmark. [`CyberPhysicalActorArena`](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_arena.gd) exposes `configure`, `reset`, `observation`, `submit`, `cancel`, `set_paused`, `step`, `snapshot` and `close`. Configuration has this shape: ```json { "version": 2, "seed": 0, "max_ticks": 600, "local_patch_radius": 6, "actors": [ {"model": "ripper", "producer": "policy"}, {"model": "copter", "producer": "demo"} ] } ``` Actor positions may optionally be explicit finite `[x,y]` coordinates in the authored arena. Unknown fields and invalid capacities are refused before replacing a live environment. `submit(command, producer)` and `step(policy_commands)` consume the same version-2 issued-observation envelope as the desktop [physical command interface](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#physical-actor-control-and-effects). Model names alone never invoke model APIs. `observation(actor_id)` contains the copied local rig view plus a bounded square native material/body-ID

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > Which usable examples exist?
**Current experimental ACT-005 source:** the entire [U01-U32 catalogue](actor-usables.md) is selectable on physical equipment. Every rig has a defined default loadout in [`physical_usable_loadouts.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_loadouts.gd). Each loadout names its usable, power, strategy and purpose; no physical actor is left with an unspecified equipment policy. SetP explicitly starts with an empty mount and human movement strategy; F5 can still select ordinary equipment. Mount definitions bind a specific host/held part, grip, joint, aiming limits and clearance. The equipment owner aims the actual configured joint when it supports aiming. The shot direction comes from the current held body's pose; a limited joint cannot acquire an unlimited virtual muzzle. The suspended payload, hammer and blade preserve their authored mechanical roles. A selection change retools the existing held chassis without allocating another body. Release clears the held connection and retains the same object, pose, velocity and body ID. A short collision grace ages with physical time even after input cancellation. Pickup checks the owning grip's proximity and terrain clearance; it does not teleport the object or reset its velocity. An already held, remote, occluded or ambiguously owned item is refused. A released chassis must return before it can select another usable. Processors are deployed by dropping that real body, waiting for supported settling, and fixing it at its current pose. A worker receipt admits processing; blocked output leaves recipe inputs and stock unchanged. The body and its rotated intake/output ports remain visible while it works, jams or exhausts. Physical pickup retires processing authority. See the [processor contract](actor-usables.md#u23u32-fixed-functional-objects). The main-thread owner applies recoil once for the matching admitted use. Native material effects use copied physical source/part information under worker ownership. Protected cells, foreign part occupancy, bounds and source clearance remain checked. The physical command, worker admission and changed-cell receipt are separate results; a valid command does not guarantee an unobstructed effect. Late receipts are fenced by run, actor, control generation, equipment epoch and request identity. The older ACT-004 direct mount/effect fixtures retain their bounded deposit/cut/rocket-charge substrate for regression; it is not a second unleased policy API for the full catalogue.

results.query: Does current CI actually execute the retained Windows DLL, and how does it reject stale native source or incomplete headless coverage?
facts: The GitHub-hosted Windows execution job is separate from Windows cross-build inspection and runs the retained DLL after exact checkout, committed LFS, provenance and complete current native source/header input-set checks.

The helper verifies pinned official Godot 4.7 and Rapier, imports the project and dynamically executes every applicable headless case exactly once with the shared runner timeouts and strict diagnostic/skip rejection.

All dynamically discovered rendered cases are explicitly outside the Windows lane and are executed by the Linux rendered shards; headless execution does not establish Windows rendered-output or browser acceptance.
The Windows execution artifact retains commands, source/runtime/tool identities, per-case logs and hashes, source drift and completion; actual pass claims require the dated exact workflow run.

Only the four declared Rapier texture import-descriptor text files normalize CRLF to LF for comparison; descriptor content changes still fail, and DLLs, images and all other tracked inputs retain byte-exact SHA-256 checks.

The focused native regressions extend `make worldgen-test`; the separate [`tools/architecture/`](../../tools/architecture) harness exercises actual native materials, legacy identities, compiler validation, three seeded 1024² outcomes, toggle deltas, independent component counting, geometry-only comparisons, negative coordinates, cancellation, stale state and separate-process authoring reconstruction. Routine coverage survives the feature branch: the broad [GDExtension workflow](../../.github/workflows/gdextension.yml) discovers the architectural native-material, project-contract and UI test scripts on Linux and Windows, while [Native CI](../../.github/workflows/native.yml) runs the native generation suites. The architectural workflow also runs its bounded publisher-guard tests on pull requests and `main` pushes. The expensive full graphical/package campaign remains restricted to feature-branch pushes or an explicit workflow dispatch. Headless regression coverage and publisher unit tests do not replace the full graphical publication campaign.

It passes the built candidate with `--native-candidate`; the helper also supports its retained-runtime path when no candidate is supplied. These are explicit artifact sources, not interchangeable provenance claims. The helper verifies exact source identity, runtime inputs, pinned official Godot archive/version and Rapier before import. It discovers the applicable headless cases, profile probes and scene startup. Rendered cases are outside this headless Windows lane and require their own graphical evidence. Section: Testing, validation, and replay > CI execution sharding
The accepted [GDExtension workflow](../../.github/workflows/gdextension.yml) uses source-derived Linux and Windows matrices from [godot_job_plan.py](../../tools/ci/godot_job_plan.py). Sharding changes execution schedule; it does not weaken assertions, omit unknown tests or turn a missing readback into a pass. Each shard has its own import. Every assigned original case must appear exactly once in the complete source/run/attempt evidence. [Linux](../../tools/ci/verify_linux_godot_shards.py) and [Windows](../../tools/ci/verify_windows_godot_shards.py) independent readers check original logs, complete assignments, runtime identity and natural completion. `max-parallel` caps simultaneous jobs, while the planner determines the actual number of shards and parent budgets. The old fixed four-shard examples are historical migration evidence. [CI execution policy](ci-execution-and-performance.md) owns current budget arithmetic and scheduling; open optimization experiments are not adopted policy. Linux rendered cases use a display and the OpenGL compatibility renderer. Missing display, explicit skip, timeout, nonzero exit, engine/script error, incomplete readback and cleanup failure retain their failure meaning. Software-rendered pixels are evidence for that backend, not target-GPU performance or playfeel. `--keep-going` preserves later outcomes after ordinary case failure; failed import stops the shard because the test project was not prepared. The Windows helper receives a source-built candidate in accepted CI and can also validate a retained runtime through its explicit alternative path. Windows headless execution, cross-build validation and graphical qualification remain separate claims. Source/runtime mismatch fails admission before a runtime pass can be claimed. The [build guide](local-build-and-validation.md#windows-retained-runtime-execution) owns invocation and artifact details.

results.query: Where can I open the full Deepworks map, watch its foreground and background chemistry exhibits, and replay a room after the guided tour has passed it?
facts: The desktop launcher, --deepworks user argument or res://deepworks.tscn opens one total 1024 by 1024 map with sixteen 256 by 256 districts and 32 paired native exhibits. It is a free-camera material viewer with foreground/rear painting, not the ordinary actor sandbox.

Four independent full-size native worlds run at target rates play 30 Hz, scripted rear 20 Hz, effects 15 Hz and frozen background zero. The live rear supplies the interacting background sets; the fourth distant architecture plane is never ticked. Source events supply reactants while native rules own the products.

The serpentine camera tour changes district every 14 running seconds, or 224 seconds per nominal circuit, while every district continues simulating. Finite reaction feeds can finish before a late visit. Whole-map R reset restores all four worlds and sources, pauses and preserves the camera; P then replays the selected view. Camera selection and layer hiding alone do not reset or pause worlds.

Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > How do the scripted drops and reactions work?
The current recipe contains **77 bounded source events**. Each record names a unique ID, district, target plane, rectangle, material, first native tick, period and repetition limit. Immediately before that plane's due native tick, the owner applies its due source rectangles, then calls the ordinary native step. The scheduler supplies reagents and environmental edits; native rules produce and subsequently move or consume the reaction products. Apparatus descriptions and expected-product metadata do not paint results into the world. Reaction feeds have finite repetition limits so completed specimens and their products can be inspected. Repeating environmental sources and drains are confined to the effects plane. Switching **Automatic material sources** off prevents future scheduled writes while existing material continues to simulate. Switching it back on admits future due ticks; missed opportunities are not replayed in a catch-up burst. Pause stops the three dynamic clocks and freezes material animation. **N** advances each active dynamic plane once; this manual step is not one frame of the normal 30/20/15 Hz pacing. The **guided tour** starts simulation and follows a serpentine district route, changing view every 14 running seconds. A nominal circuit takes 224 seconds. It is camera automation: it neither resets districts on arrival nor delays their native clocks until visited. A late visit can therefore show an already completed reaction. Stop the tour and use **R**, then **P**, to replay a room from its original state while retaining its camera view. The complete candidate programme and all four authoring layers are validated before replacement. Invalid dimensions, rectangles, material IDs, schedules or capacity requests preserve the current exhibition. Successful reset advances the generation and clears earlier queued commands and event counters. The [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#depth-host-and-deepworks-configuration) owns event and authoring limits. This dedicated programme does not change the shared MicroScenario schema or implement general serialized replay. Source: [`CyberDeepworksRuntime.install()`, `_validate_programme()` and `_step_layer()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_runtime.gd), [`CyberDeepworks._process()` and `toggle_tour()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks.gd) and [`CyberDeepworksMap.recipe_hash()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_map.gd). The recipe hash includes all four layer definitions and explicit event fields; it identifies authored content, not a saved running state.

Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > Controls
| Input or control | Result | |---|---| | **P / Space** | Run or pause all three dynamic planes and their material animation. | | **N / Step** | Pause and advance each active dynamic plane by one native tick. | | **R / Reset** | Restore all worlds, specimens and sources; pause while preserving the current camera. | | **District grid**, **[ / ]** | Select a 256 × 256 district view without changing material state. | | **Inspect foreground / rear setup** | Centre a 200 × 200 view on that district's selected apparatus. | | **O / Home / Whole map** | Show the full 1024 × 1024 composition. | | **WASD / arrows**, **middle-drag** | Pan the camera. | | **Mouse wheel** | Zoom around the pointer; supported view widths run from 128 to 1024 cells. | | **T / Guided tour** | Start or stop the camera tour; starting it also resumes a paused exhibition. | | **1–5** | Foreground only, quantized relief, four material layers, Hybrid depth, Diorama cutaway. | | **Layer visibility checkboxes** | Show or hide foreground, rear apparatus, atmosphere or distant architecture. | | **Automatic material sources** | Enable or disable scheduled material writes; existing native reactions continue. | | **Paint foreground / Paint rear apparatus** | Choose the independently editable native world. | | **Left mouse / right mouse** | Add the chosen material / erase, using the selected brush radius of 1–8 cells. | | **F8 / Tab** | Hide or show the controls for a clean view. | | **F2 / Escape** | Close the exhibition and return to the feature launcher. | The painting palette includes Water, Sand, Acid, Spark, Fire, Lava, Salt, Steam, Brine, Oil, Packed Snow, Thermite Brick, Magnesium Plate, Quicklime Block and Wall. Pointer coordinates use the selected plane's inverse parallax transform, so rear painting and the foreground brush target their own visible native cells. UI interaction, modal menus and focus loss release painting/panning input; a fresh press is required after those boundaries. Arrow keys continue adjusting a focused brush slider without moving the camera. Click the map to return keyboard focus to it, then release and freshly press any movement key held while using a control. Source: [`deepworks.gd` input, UI and focus handling](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks.gd) and [`CyberDepthCompositor.screen_to_layer()`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_compositor.gd).

Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > Open, inspect and replay a setup
Choose **Deepworks** in the desktop feature launcher, pass the user argument `--deepworks`, or open [`res://deepworks.tscn`](../../godot/deepworks.tscn) directly: ```sh godot --path godot -- --deepworks godot --path godot res://deepworks.tscn ``` Use the pinned Godot and materialized native libraries from the [build guide](local-build-and-validation.md). Deepworks starts paused in the whole-map Hybrid view. Click a district, then **Inspect foreground setup** or **Inspect rear setup** for a closer view and the apparatus description. Press **P** to start its native clocks and material sources. This is a free-camera material exhibition with painting controls. It has no ordinary actor session, player-follow mode or F5 actor picker. The shared foreground circulation is real cleared native geometry: horizontal galleries and vertical shafts make 24 internal district connections. Camera movement and district selection preserve the entire map and all ongoing reactions. Reaction supplies are finite. To watch a selected setup from its original condition, choose the district or apparatus, press **R**, then **P**. **R resets all four worlds and all sixteen districts**, reinstalls the source programme, and pauses; it preserves the camera and selected district. It is not a local specimen refill. The resulting products remain in the world until further native interactions, painting or a whole-map reset changes them. ![Deepworks controls and district notes](../images/deepworks/deepworks-guide.png) Source: [`CyberDeepworks._ready()`, `reset_exhibition()`, `select_district()` and `focus_exhibit()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks.gd).
