Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > Four full-size worlds and independent clocks
Every plane owns a separate **1024 × 1024 native material world**. The displayed map remains 1024 × 1024 in total; the four overlapping planes do not form a 2048 × 2048 terrain or sixteen separately loaded scenes. | Internal plane | UI name | Running target | Authority and coverage | |---|---|---:|---| | `play` | Foreground | 30 Hz | Full map, cleared circulation and sixteen interactive foreground apparatuses. | | `scripted` | Rear reactions & machinery | 20 Hz | Full map, independent rear scenery and sixteen native apparatuses. | | `effects` | Atmosphere | 15 Hz | Authored atmospheric material and bounded local environmental sources across every district. | | `background` | Distant architecture | 0 Hz | Full authored distant map, never ticked; the first copied material publication is cached. | The **rear layer** is the interacting background set: it runs real native material drops, reactions and transport. The fourth plane, whose internal key is `background`, is deliberately frozen distant architecture. Its pixels are rendered through the same canonical material appearance system. Hiding a plane only changes visibility; it does not pause its native clock or source schedule. All districts run together, including those outside the camera. The host serializes adapter calls into its four isolated worlds. Rendering consumes copied RG8 packets, never mutable native storage. Failure of a native step or publication stops the exhibition and freezes presentation; it is not silently replaced with a successful frame. Layer visibility, parallax, relief, haze and liquid reflections do not transfer cells, charge, mass or collisions between worlds. The [depth contract](../systems/depth-layers-and-parallax.md) owns their rendering and publication rules. Source: [`CyberDeepworks.reset_exhibition()` and `_fault()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks.gd), [`CyberDeepworksRuntime`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_runtime.gd) and [`CyberDepthLayerRuntime`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_runtime.gd).

Section: Deepworks — the exhibition below > What is the map?
**Current source:** Deepworks is one **1024 × 1024 total map**, divided into a 4 × 4 grid of sixteen 256 × 256 districts. Every district has foreground architecture, an independent rear apparatus and service layer, local atmosphere, and a distant architectural scene. Its **32 exhibits** pair one foreground setup with one rear setup per district. The composition uses all **51 MAT-002 building materials, IDs 81–131**, including architectural specimens and material swatches; the [building catalogue](../systems/building-material-catalogue.md) owns their actual native rules and material identities. The map extends the layered presentation of [Strata Theatre](../systems/depth-layers-and-parallax.md), with the connected industrial composition and small architectural details of the earlier showcase maps. Numbered bays, valves, pipe clamps, specimen shelves, signal lamps, cargo, stained windows, domestic niches and distant machinery give each district a distinct setting. Foreground apertures deliberately expose the rear apparatus. Full coverage means all four planes are authored across all sixteen districts; open space remains part of the composition. Source: [`CyberDeepworksMap.build()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_map.gd), [`CyberDeepworksArchitecture`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_architecture.gd) and [`CyberDeepworksExhibits.build()`](../../godot/scripts/exhibition/deepworks_exhibits.gd). ![Deepworks atlas rendered from the four material planes](../images/deepworks/deepworks-atlas.png) The atlas is a 2048 × 2048 presentation capture of the 1024 × 1024 map. Image resolution does not enlarge the simulation. The sixteen retained 512 × 512 tile images are exact crops of this atlas.

results.query: Can a depth host use non-square or 1024 by 1024 material surfaces without changing Strata Theatre defaults, and what happens to its old world or pixels after an invalid resize or stale packet?
facts: Depth runtime reset accepts an authored size with each axis from 8 through 1024, including non-square worlds, and keeps 640 by 360 as the default. Compositor and surface configure methods use the same accepted ROI while retaining 1024 by 1024 native RG8 backing. Deepworks selects 1024 by 1024 for all four planes; no native ABI changes follow.

Reset validates the complete candidate before replacing worlds, dimensions, clocks, cached background, queued commands or generation. Invalid dimensions, geometry or reserved material ID 10 preserve the prior live state. Guard, weather and effects sinks follow the accepted extent.

Compositor set_view validates origin and extent, synchronizes uniforms/layout and clamps the camera; configured world dimensions cannot be changed in place. Surface packet validation stages all patches before the first blit and rejects older reset generations even when their serial is higher, preserving pixels, accepted serial, tick and generation.

Section: Depth layers and parallax prototypes > Four material planes
The prototype owns four separate CyberNativeCellWorld objects through CyberDepthLayerRuntime. Each world uses the existing native material IDs, rules and RG8 RenderBridge projection. Godot owns only authoring, presentation and explicit lab commands. | Plane | Strata default rate | Intended use | |---|---:|---| | play | 60 Hz | Active foreground/play material. | | scripted | 20 Hz | Rear set, destructible scenery and set-piece sequences that should not perturb foreground material. | | effects | 30 Hz | Rain, snow-like Dust, Steam fog, Spark energy and other environmental material effects. | | background | 0 Hz | Authored distant city. It is never ticked and its first copied RG8 publication is cached. | The rates are independent. Dynamic planes may be reduced or paused without changing the others. The background rejects non-zero rates. Deepworks selects 30/20/15/0 Hz for play/scripted/effects/background. Every Deepworks plane spans the full 1024 × 1024 authored map; the rear `scripted` world runs native reactions while the true `background` world remains frozen. Each plane has its own render canvas and a material surface covering the accepted authored ROI, defaulting to 640 × 360 in Strata Theatre. Frozen surfaces request a one-shot bake when a copied publication arrives or updates are paused, so pausing before the first draw still renders the admitted state. See [`CyberDepthLayerSurface.apply_packet()` and `set_render_enabled()`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_surface.gd). The current host uses one native adapter owner and serializes calls into its four worlds. Production adoption should integrate the play plane with the existing asynchronous owner rather than introduce another mutable owner.

Section: Depth layers and parallax prototypes > Parallax and authoring coordinates
**Strata Theatre defaults** to a 640 × 360 authored ROI over the existing 1024 × 1024 native backing. Its initial scale/parallax factors are: - play 1.00 / 1.00; - scripted 0.94 / 0.70; - effects 0.88 / 0.44; - background 0.78 / 0.18. **Current parameterized API:** [`CyberDepthLayerRuntime.reset(definitions, authored_size)`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_runtime.gd) accepts each authored axis from 8 through 1024, including non-square worlds. Omitting the size retains 640 × 360. It validates the whole candidate before replacement; rejected dimensions, geometry or material ID 10 leave the existing worlds, clocks, cached background, queued edits and reset generation intact. Guard cells, effects sinks, weather, authoring bounds and simulation interest all use the accepted `world_size`. [`CyberDepthCompositor.configure(authored_size)`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_compositor.gd) configures that size before the compositor enters the scene tree. `set_view(origin, extent)` synchronizes the view uniforms and layout, clamps the camera to the authored extent and refuses invalid/non-finite views before mutation. An already configured compositor cannot be resized to a different world. `CyberDepthLayerSurface.configure(id, frozen, authored_size)` likewise sets the complete material viewport ROI while retaining the 1024 × 1024 RG8 backing. Each plane has its own canvas and material surface. Deepworks sets all layer scales to 1, with closely spaced parallax factors so rear apparatus remains associated with its district at every corner of the map. The [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#depth-host-and-deepworks-configuration) owns exact dimensions, rate, event and presentation limits. `screen_to_layer()` is the exact inverse of the rendered layer transform. Painting therefore addresses the selected world's cell under the pointer.

Section: Depth layers and parallax prototypes > Material-surface rendering and bounds
Each world is rendered by CyberDepthLayerSurface through the existing material_palette.gdshader and CyberMaterialAppearanceLut. The private compositing palette only changes Empty alpha to zero; material IDs and the canonical appearance program remain unchanged. Copied native packets are validated before changing an Image: RG8 only, matching layer identity, nondecreasing reset generation and monotonic integer serial within a generation, at most 4096 patches and 2 MiB packet bytes, in-bounds rectangle/stride data, cumulative staged area no greater than one 1024x1024 backing, and exact full-refresh shape. Every patch Image is constructed before the first blit. A packet from an older reset generation is refused even if it has a higher serial. Rejection leaves pixels, accepted serial, tick and generation intact. This is enforced in [`CyberDepthLayerSurface._validate_packet()`](../../godot/scripts/depth/depth_layer_surface.gd). ImageTexture.update currently uploads the whole 1024x1024 RG8 image after an admitted changed packet: **2 MiB per changed layer upload**. Region texture uploads or a smaller presentation backing are the clearest follow-up optimizations.

The [Deepworks guide](deepworks-exhibition.md) owns the map and interactive controls; the [depth contract](../systems/depth-layers-and-parallax.md) owns parameterized surfaces, independent worlds and publication. results.query: Where can I play the stunt buggy, trials bike, momentum acrobat, arcade lander, Sand cloud, Water blob and jetpack barrel, and how do I switch or reset them?
facts: The feature launcher, --player-playground or res://player_playground.tscn opens the dedicated seven-preset course; --player=ID optionally chooses a starting preset.
1-7 and Tab/Shift+Tab select a fresh preset/course, R resets the selection, P/Escape pauses and F switches overview/follow. F2 closes the owner and returns to the launcher.

Five mechanical presets form F5 SetP, giving 46 physical actors across eight sets. The dry and liquid presets are dedicated-scene native material fields, not Rapier actors. Checkpoint routes exist, but complete-route and target-PC human feel acceptance require separate evidence.

Section: Player control playground > Keyboard controls for all seven presets
In `--player-playground` (optionally `--player=ID`), use 1–7 or Tab/Shift+Tab to select, R to restart, P/Escape to pause, F for overview/follow, and F2 for the launcher. These scene controls accompany the movement actions below. | Key / ID | Preset | Movement and actions | |---|---|---| | **1** / `stuntbuggy` | **Loose Cannon** — loose-jointed stunt buggy | W/S drive/reverse; A/D or Q/E lean and rotate in air; Space hops from support; Shift brakes; hold C for recovery assistance. Sprung wheels and a hinged rider carry the motion. | | **2** / `trialsbike` | **Trials Rat** — trials bike | W/S throttle/reverse; A/D or Q/E lean; hold Space while supported to preload, then release to hop; Shift brakes; hold C for recovery assistance. The rear wheel drives and the front wheel rolls freely until braking. | | **3** / `acrobat` | **Afterimage** — momentum acrobat | A/D run and steer in air; Space jumps, then double jumps; hold Shift or S to slide; tap Shift to roll; Shift+Space or S+Space bullet jumps; C cancels/brakes and, held in air, glides. Mouse position aims bullet jumps. | | **4** / `arcadelander` | **Vector Rush** — arcade lander | W or Space fires the body-axis main engine; A/D or Q/E rotates; S gives reverse thrust; Shift applies a strong airbrake; tap C toggles damped flight/coast. | | **5** / `dryswarm` | **Dust Devil** — Sand cloud | WASD guides actual Sand; Space surges in the movement direction, or upward from neutral; Shift spreads; C gathers. Neutral admitted input keeps the cohesion/loft field active. | | **6** / `liquidswarm` | **Undertow** — Water blob | WASD guides actual Water; Space surges; Shift squeezes transverse to travel into a stream; C gathers. Neutral admitted input keeps the cohesion/loft field active. | | **7** / `jetbarrel` | **Barrel Rocket** — barrel with jetpack | W or Space fires the body-axis jet; A/D or Q/E provides strong rotation; S gives reverse thrust; Shift brakes; hold C for upright assistance. | Arrow keys duplicate WASD in the dedicated scene. The lander and barrel thrust along their current orientation, so rotation changes the direction of the next burst. Damping and recovery are authored game assistance with bounded forces; contacts and rigid-body motion remain Rapier's responsibility. A cancelled bike preload is discarded without firing a hop.

results.query: How do I chain Afterimage slides, rolls, bullet jumps, double jumps and airglide, and can cancelling reload those airborne moves?
facts: A/D runs and steers, Space jumps/double jumps, holding Shift or S slides, tapping Shift rolls, and Shift/S plus Space requests an aimed bullet jump; actual joints tuck the physical body.

Space can jump-cancel a roll using available inventory; held crouch requests a bullet jump first. C cancels/brakes and held airborne C glides near the apex/fall with positive gravity and finite reserve. Releasing Space shortens an ordinary jump.

One extra jump, one bullet jump, one air roll and glide reserve recharge after confirmed landing. Cancelling, focus changes and authority transitions clear intent without replenishing spent airborne inventory or erasing velocity.

Section: Player control playground > Acrobat movement chains and cancels
Afterimage preserves momentum through a low-drag slide and uses actual folding hip/ankle joints for its tucked posture. Steering during slides and rolls is weaker than running; reversing input changes momentum gradually. A held crouch can keep the tuck during a brief loss of support. The controller does not teleport the body or replace its velocity with a character trajectory. - **Run → slide → bullet jump:** gain speed with A/D, hold Shift or S to tuck, aim with the mouse, then press Space. Grounded bullet jumps include an upward component; faster velocity already aligned with the launch is retained. - **Jump → double jump → roll → glide:** Space gives the ground jump and one airborne jump. Press Shift in air for the separate air roll. Hold C near the apex or while falling to reduce descent while steering with A/D. - **Roll → jump cancel:** press Space during a roll to leave it using an available jump. If Shift/S remains held, the same press requests a bullet jump first while that separate launch is available. Release crouch for an ordinary jump cancel. - **Slide/roll → brake cancel:** press C to end the slide or roll. On support, C brakes; slide stays suppressed until crouch is released. Releasing Space early shortens an ordinary jump. Q/E adds airborne attitude trim. The controller supplies a short coyote window and input buffer. One airborne jump, one bullet jump, one air roll and a finite glide reserve recharge after confirmed support, not after focus changes or cancellation. Glide retains positive gravity and has a finite duration; it is not hover. Exact timing and actuation limits belong to the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#player-playground-values). Sources: [acrobat controller](../../godot/scripts/player_acrobat_controller.gd) and [physical rig actuator](../../godot/scripts/physical_actor_rig.gd).

In Shared Workbench, open **Actor Composition…**, place or inspect an actor, then choose **Pilot inspected** for human control. The accepted composition contract admits at most eight actors, eight parts per actor and 64 body proxies overall. The [practical actor guide](../operations/workbench-actor-composition.md) and [composition contract](workbench-actor-composition.md) cover preparation, placement, producer ownership and capability refusals. Workbench equipment uses the [M / Alt controls](actor-usables.md#shared-workbench), leaving the paint pointer with PAINT. The following F5 route belongs to the ordinary sandbox and standalone scenes. F5 in the ordinary sandbox, Blacksite Nine and the four showcase districts selects a representation, set, actor and keyboard, scripted-demo or external policy producer. Its buggy/bike use vertical movement for throttle and horizontal movement for lean; the acrobat supplies slides, rolls, bullet/double jumps, cancels and glide. results.query: Do the dry cloud and liquid blob move real native material, and what prevents steering from repainting Water, moving it through walls or scanning the whole world?
facts: The dedicated exclusive owner applies a between-tick native field to local Sand or Water, then runs the normal native simulation. Complete stored cells and temperature move through existing relocation; partial Water quantity is exact within the call. No per-cell Rapier objects, erase/repaint or Water kernel rewrite is introduced.

The radius-32 selection scans at most 4225 candidate positions, snapshots at most 512 sources once and attempts at most four axis-adjacent moves each. Occupied cells, terrain, transient bodies, bounds and unavailable destination storage refuse moves; invalid commands refuse mutation.

The field selects matching material by location, so environmental material may join and material outside the circle is uncontrolled. Centre following uses the observed quantity-weighted centroid, not a remote cursor or hidden persistent parcel cohort.

Section: pressure_flow_v1 reference — corrected Water pressure family > Kernel (`update_water_pressure`)
Stages 1, 2, 4, 5 of the [material hooks](liquid-solver-family-policy.md#material-hooks-versus-motion-gate-c-correction-2026-10-23) are unchanged: pair chemistry runs before dispatch, the coherence countdown is kept and suppresses lateral motion, `mix_after_motion` receives the real moved quantity, body-mask contact uses `record_transient_contact`, and identity stays `Material::Water`. Stage 3 is replaced: 1. **Gravity:** down, then the two diagonals; into Water only to visible capacity (never overfill), otherwise `try_move` (whole tuple and sidecar). 2. **Overfill relief/relay:** overfill rises into unsaturated Water or creates Water in Empty above; a saturated column relays it whole (receiver not epoch-marked, so a bottom-up scan reaches the surface in one tick); under a lid it spreads sideways toward less overfill when the difference is ≥ 2. 3. **Adhesion film:** kept only for a **resting** thin cell (flow 0). 4. **Velocity:** `flow += gradient × kAccelNumerator / maximum` (deterministic dither), where `gradient = (h(x−2)+h(x−1)−h(x+1)−h(x+2))/2`. A sample at x±2 is used **only** if both faces toward it are open (Water or Empty); a wall, foreign liquid or body mask is a closed face that reflects the cell's own head. Overfill adds `kOverfillStiffnessRows × maximum` per unit (v1: 0). Start dead band 128/255 of a row (static friction above integer-gas gauge noise), moving band 10/255; `kRetain` 256/256 and `kFriction` 0 (momentum is lost only through mass-weighted merges and contacts). 5. **Surface skin:** a resting top-of-run cell relaxes sub-row steps with the FreeMass ¾ rule and `tolerance()`; saturated cells and overfill never move here. 6. **Flux:** `|flow| × quantity / kFlowScale` (dither) toward `sign(flow)`; Empty receives a new cell carrying this tick's **updated** velocity (front ≤ 1 cell/tick, receiver epoch-marked); Water receives visible then overfill capacity with a mass-weighted velocity merge whose truncation remainder is booked (`PressureFlowLedger.flow_remainder`). A source with Water directly above never empties laterally (no interior voids). A closed face zeroes flow and books `contact_loss`. Every direct authoritative write is witnessed like `transfer_water` (job effects or serial dirty/wake/discovery). Per-job ledgers merge after the phase barrier; there are no shared counters. Partial transfers propagate the maximum source/receiver coherence, capturing source coherence before an emptied tuple is retired. Every successful quantity transfer calls the unchanged material post-motion hook with its actual moved quantity, including surface skin and overfill relief/relay; the hook itself determines whether that motion qualifies for grain carrying. Reaction products start at family defaults even when a product retains Water identity. Same-material coherence countdowns retain family state. Repainting an identical visible tuple still publishes dirty/wake/discovery witnesses if its pressure state changed.

A whole cell caught in a gate (whole-cell Water, other declared liquids, powders) is moved exactly to the nearest free unmasked cell outside every gate (radius ≤ 4); in a flooded gate a liquid cell is instead passed up to its free surface, so the level rises by its volume. A partial Water cell (FreeMass/PressureFlow) cannot move without changing its quantity, so it is removed and booked as `trimmed_water`. With the pump on, drained Water enters the pipe instead of leaving the World, so native Water + pipe is constant: a closed circulation loop. A full pipe stops the drain (`pipe_full`); it never deletes the excess. Without the pump the drain is a sink and the supply is finite. | Inertial cellular flow, injected resting cells and ballistic parcels remain three distinct mechanisms; the receipt states the nozzle mode explicitly.

Section: Player control playground > Native Sand cloud and Water blob ownership
The [playground runtime](../../godot/scripts/player_playground_runtime.gd) exclusively owns one synchronous native World for a material preset. Setup seeds 256 Sand or Water cells. Each admitted step applies the native field before the ordinary material tick; normal kernels still own gravity, Water flow and reactions. Mechanical presets instead use the existing synchronous physical arena and its main-thread Rapier session. Neither lane borrows the asynchronous sandbox worker's World. `World::apply_player_material_field` moves complete stored cells through `relocate_stored_cell`, preserving compact state, temperature and exact partial Water quantity within that call. It does not erase/repaint the cloud, create per-cell physics bodies, or introduce a Water pressure/flow rule. The next normal tick can redistribute Water and apply ordinary interactions. A field therefore does not promise conservation across unrelated chemistry or authoring actions. Selection is **matching material within a local radius**, not a persistent collection of owned particles. Nearby environmental Sand/Water can join; material that leaves the field is no longer controlled. The field follows the returned quantity-weighted material centroid with a bounded centre adjustment. WASD moves material rather than a remote selection cursor. The visible ring shows this local selection boundary. The native call scans at most 4,225 candidate positions within a radius-32 selection, captures at most 512 source parcels once, and attempts at most four axis-adjacent moves per parcel. Stable ordering and phase-based scan rotation prevent repeated source processing. Occupied cells, hard terrain, transient bodies, world bounds and unavailable destination storage stop a step. No occupied cell is overwritten. Invalid commands and failed/in-tick Worlds are refused before mutation. Exact API, receipt and limits are in [interfaces](../reference/interfaces-and-message-contracts.md#player-material-field-control) and [configuration](../reference/configuration-reference.md#player-playground-values).

Section: Player control playground > Gamepad and quick scene controls
The dedicated scene samples the first connected standard gamepad. Its left stick supplies WASD, A supplies Space/primary, B supplies Shift/secondary, X supplies C/auxiliary, and the shoulder buttons supply Q/E trim. Start pauses. The stick has a radial deadzone and is combined with keyboard input before unit-length clamping. The mouse supplies aim while inside the play view; otherwise movement supplies aim, with a diagonal fallback at neutral. Gamepad mapping is implemented; physical controller qualification is separate. **Accepted PLAY-UI-004 shared-course event slice:** The normal desktop scene attaches a small main-thread [gamepad event bridge](../../godot/scripts/playable_course_gamepad_events.gd). When the existing course/human SetP capability gate is active, unhandled A/B/X press and release events from the first connected pad invoke the existing `publish_actor_keyboard_input` path immediately. This lets its existing bounded physical-session FIFO retain a short tap between physical callbacks, rather than relying only on the next polled state. Controls receive events first; other devices, unmapped buttons and non-course/specialist configurations are not intercepted. Focus, pause, reset, rearm, equipment and epoch authority stay in the original host; the bridge never steps or owns any simulation object. Analog stick/trim polling and standalone scene behavior are unchanged. The [focused fixture](../../godot/tests/test_play_ui004_gamepad_events.gd) uses genuine Viewport events and physical-session/Rapier steps, with a disclosed synthetic selected-device index and test host publisher. It verifies ordered button pairs and a matched no-event/poll-only negative control, not a physical controller, the complete desktop focus path or interactive feel. [PR #286](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/pull/286) merged as `e076819e086abb762796303b830314e330f87234`; its source-matched Windows/Linux fixture passed **32 assertions per OS**. The later combined #284 suite preserves that fixture. The [dated candidate audit](../audits/2026-10-28-play-ui004-gamepad-events.md) records the gap, test boundaries and integration obligations. | Control | Scene operation | |---|---| | 1–7 or preset buttons | Select a preset and construct a fresh course/session | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Select next / previous preset | | R or **Reset · R** | Reset the selected preset and course; keep this scene's best times | | P, Escape or gamepad Start | Pause/resume; pause revokes current input | | F or camera button | Toggle course overview and player-follow view | | F2 or Menu | Close the current owner and return to the feature launcher | Selection, restart, pause and focus changes require movement/action controls to be released before input rearms. Window focus loss, GUI focus or a mouse-button press cancels pending control. Focus loss alone does not pause the physics; uncontrolled material settles and mechanical momentum continues. Use pause to stop stepping. The scene begins running after successful setup, unlike the ordinary F5 map replacement, which begins paused. Source:

Section: Articulated Rapier actors and shared physical control > How do I select and control them?
In Shared Workbench, open **Actor Composition…**, place or inspect an actor, then choose **Pilot inspected** for human control. The accepted composition contract admits at most eight actors, eight parts per actor and 64 body proxies overall. The [practical actor guide](../operations/workbench-actor-composition.md) and [composition contract](workbench-actor-composition.md) cover preparation, placement, producer ownership and capability refusals. Workbench equipment uses the [M / Alt controls](actor-usables.md#shared-workbench), leaving the paint pointer with PAINT. The following F5 route belongs to the ordinary sandbox and standalone scenes. F5 in the ordinary sandbox, Blacksite Nine and the four showcase districts selects a representation, set, actor and keyboard, scripted-demo or external policy producer. Physical Rapier choices are the default actor route. Applying rebuilds the selected map at its initial spawn and starts paused. R retains the selection; changing district uses that district's spawn. Registered scientific fixtures and Benchmark mode retain their own actors. The new assembly remains suspended until its matching native reset and initial hard-terrain colliders are installed, including when Play is requested early. Physical wire controls are WASD movement, mouse aim, brackets for effort, Q/E trim, Z/X reel, Space primary, Shift secondary and C auxiliary. M uses the tool, N releases a held item and U requests nearby pickup. Left/right pointer buttons use equipment primary/alternate; its aim and power are independent of locomotion. F5 equipment selection changes a held chassis through the same admitted action. Exact ability meaning is displayed from the selected profile. These map to `tool`, `release_usable` and `attach_usable` in the shared API. These are bounded gameplay requests; no command writes a transform or assigns velocity as locomotion. Focus loss, pause, replacement and input cancellation revoke pending actions. SetP supplies five distinct human movement controllers through the same action path. Its buggy/bike use vertical movement for throttle and horizontal movement for lean; the acrobat supplies slides, rolls, bullet/double jumps, cancels and glide. Full controls and the separate seven-preset keyboard/gamepad course are in the [player control playground](player-control-playground.md). Its dry/liquid presets are native material fields and are not members of the Rapier roster. The retained single-body barrel/Ripper comparison is described separately in the [physical programme](../operations/physical-actor-programme.md). The current articulated Ripper is the five-part sprung crawler, not that historical hull arm. Desktop integration does not migrate the synchronous Web control owner.

Section: Interfaces and message contracts > What crosses the rigid-body bridge, and which limits apply?
**Current private adapter format:** `PackedFloat32Array`, not a versioned C ABI. Source: [rigid_body_coupling.gd](../../godot/scripts/rigid_body_coupling.gd), [native parser/results](../../godot/native_extension/cyber_native_cell_world.cpp). Offsets below are float indices within each record. | Input stride 11 | Field | Result stride 9 | Field | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | Body ID | 0 | Body ID | | 1–2 | Centre x/y | 1–2 | Central impulse x/y | | 3 | Rotation | 3–4 | Positional correction x/y | | 4–5 | Full rectangle size x/y | 5 | Contact count | | 6–7 | Linear velocity x/y | 6 | Displaced-cell count | | 8 | Angular velocity | 7 | Unresolved-cell count | | 9 | Mass | 8 | Sample serial | | 10 | Sample serial | — | — | Positions/sizes/corrections use pixels/cells, rotation radians, velocities pixels/second and radians/second. Mass/impulse use the Godot adapter's quantities; production physical-unit calibration remains unresolved. IDs/counts/serials travel as floats. ACT-004 parsing considers at most 64 complete records, accepts integer IDs 1–64 and integer sample serials 0–16,777,215, rejects any nonfinite field or nonpositive size/mass, ignores trailing partial records and retains the first duplicate. Accepted full sizes clamp to at least one cell and mass to 0.001. The same finite-record predicate is used by the fallback and bridge. The physical session rejects a complete assembly beyond capacity before spawning. SetP circular wheels supply their diameter as a circumscribed square in this unchanged rectangle layout. Rapier hard contact and graphics use circles; native masks and displacement retain the explicit conservative approximation. General contours and cellular torque feedback remain Planned; these private packed records are not an unrestricted public network protocol. Numerical response and sample-age policy belong in [coupling](../architecture/rigid-body-and-cellular-coupling.md).

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > Which values and units are preserved?
Every output has a declared type, cell-unit exponent, component bounds, natural sampling scale, identity and conservative work cost. Unit exponents range from −8 through 8. Coordinates and geometric distances have `cells^1`; gradients reduce the input exponent by one; products add exponents. Angles are radians with exponent zero. All numeric values are finite and bounded by the declared component range within ±`1e100`. | Type | Meaning | Conversion and comparison | |---|---|---| | `normalized` | Dimensionless scalar in `[0,1]` | May drive a material mask directly through a `spatial:<id>` reference | | `scalar` | General scalar, including signed values, with a declared unit exponent | No implicit clamping; `to_mask` explicitly maps its `low..high` interval into `[0,1]` | | `signed_distance` | Negative inside, zero at the boundary, positive outside, measured in cells | Only supported exact constructions retain this qualification; arbitrary arithmetic loses it | | `distance` | Nonnegative distance to a declared feature, with the operator's stated search scope | Bounded Poisson distance is a capped local search result; it is not an infinite-world nearest-seed guarantee | | `vector2` | Two continuous components sharing one unit exponent | Vector arithmetic, components, length, dot and normalization are explicit | | `category` | Exact tuple of signed integer x/y identity plus a 64-bit domain | Equality compares the full tuple; IDs are never numerically blended or converted to a mask | | `boolean` | Exact false/true, represented by zero/one | `equal`, `less` and local extrema produce it; explicit `to_mask` yields exact zero/one | Addition/subtraction and ordered scalar comparison require compatible units. Vector components require equal units. `equal` requires matching types and units, including exact categorical tuples. `select` consumes `[boolean, true_value, false_value]` with matching branch types/units. `mix` requires matching continuous inputs and a normalized weight. No categorical ordering or arithmetic is inferred from its payload. `category_is` compares a categorical input with an exact authored tuple. Its explicit literal domain zero selects the signed x/y ID within the input's own domain; a nonzero literal also requires exact domain equality. This supplies a declarative selector for generated district identities without requiring an author to reproduce the compiler's domain fingerprint. Ordinary `equal` still compares complete tuples. `constant` accepts normalized, general scalar, vector, category or boolean values. A constant with cell units is not automatically a distance to a shape. Distance types come from declared geometric operators. In JSON, categorical integers use exact text representations: signed decimal strings for x/y and exactly 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits for the unsigned domain. Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How are typed authoring controls and diagnostics used?
The standalone **World generation workbench — terrain authoring preview** launcher entry opens the generation editor. Its **Typed spatial graphs** page edits the `spatial` JSON section, inserts operator drafts from the native catalogue and selects complete executable examples. It shows accepted output type, units, scale, bounds, distance qualification, identity and work. `spatial:<expanded.id>` selects a copied typed diagnostic. The display may map a signed scalar or category to colour, while the inspector preserves the raw typed value. Presentation colour is never the stored categorical identity or a material mask. GEN-004 schema-3 recipes may populate selected `spatial` geometry inputs from [immutable semantic route/feature exports](procedural-hierarchical-generation.md). The planner resolves those names before the typed compiler runs. Each export is one actual polyline or feature boundary; separate routes are never joined by invented segments. Fields retain no dependency on grammar types, live World state or partially rasterized neighboring cells. GEN-004 also reuses this finite assignment solver for declared district themes. The Workbench writes JSON with full floating-point precision. External GDScript authors should use `JSON.stringify(recipe, " ", true, true)` so the `full_precision` argument preserves accepted double values and the compiled `spatial_fingerprint`; default JSON formatting can round them. Category strings remain exact independently of that numeric formatting. Reapplying an accepted recipe intentionally advances the adapter revision and recipe fingerprint; unchanged spatial content retains its separate graph fingerprint. Only `normalized` spatial outputs may feed existing application/exclusion, aggregate variation and parameter-mapping controls. Authors must add an explicit `to_mask` conversion for signed scalars or booleans. A category can first be compared with `equal`, then explicitly converted. The initial proposal context, modifier order, restored route skeleton and final hard-material authority remain owned by the retained [field/modifier contract](procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md). Executable profiles under [`examples/worldgen`](../../examples/worldgen) cover transformed industrial structure, vector-guided utilities, exact categorical districts, reusable decay masks and multiscale feature seeds. This is minimal authoring/inspection support for the native implementation. The accepted [GEN-007 editor and qualification workflow](../operations/procedural-qualification.md) adds graph-canvas, hierarchy, plane, provenance and comparison tools. These standalone generation controls remain separate from the Shared Workbench’s [Architectural Generator](architectural-generator.md). GEN-004 owns hierarchical places and GEN-005 finite semantic depth; persistent runtime streaming and edit reconciliation remain outside these contracts.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How do immutable routes and finite region assignments work?
Geometry inputs contain an ID, 1..256 finite points and a `closed` flag; a closed boundary requires at least three points. `geometry_distance` names one immutable input and returns Euclidean distance to its point, open polyline segments or closed boundary. Closed geometry measures the boundary; it does not silently become an inside/outside classifier. A single point and repeated points have bounded explicit segment handling. Geometry is copied/prepared before publication, and its actual coordinates enter the consuming node's identity. The accepted GEN-004 planner supplies routes and feature boundaries through this value interface: `Generator::compile` prepares exported geometry before compiling the spatial graph. The field implementation retains no dependency on grammar types or live World state. An assignment input declares a finite tile of at most 16×16 cells, up to 16 exact categories, four directional adjacency masks and optional per-cell domain masks. Opposite adjacency relations must be reciprocal. Deterministic propagation and bounded backtracking prepare the entire solution before a field can sample it. Unsatisfiable constraints and exhausted work are distinct explicit failures; neither exposes a partial assignment. `assigned_region` returns one exact category from the prepared tile. The tile repeats using floor addressing. `wrap_x`/`wrap_y` enable constraints across those tile edges; without a wrap constraint, adjacency is guaranteed only inside the finite tile. GEN-004 owns hierarchical layout use of this contract and should reuse this solver rather than introducing a conflicting field solver.

Section: Procedural world generation candidates > What is implemented?
**Current accepted source, beginning with GEN-001 / [#163](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/163) and GEN-002 / [#171](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/171):** three CPU procedural generators share one immutable recipe, theme hierarchy, spatial control stack and extensible native feature registry. They produce actual material IDs for signed-coordinate chunks. Generation is separate from simulation: it does not tick materials, query a mutable World, call Godot, request neighboring chunks or share a mutable random generator. The [public native API](../../native/include/cybersand/world_generation.hpp) and [implementation](../../native/src/world_generation.cpp) own these semantics. GEN-002 adds named structured-noise/finite-curve fields, scalar sidechains, masked context-aware guidance and sculpting, aggregate material recipes and paced diagnostic channels. The focused [fields and modifiers contract](procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md) owns those controls, immutable initial context and finite Hilbert/Morton scope. GEN-003 / [#190](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/190) adds explicit schema-2 [typed spatial functions](procedural-typed-spatial-fields.md): signed distance/vector/category values, transformed/derived geometry, reusable parameter subgraphs, structured seeds, finite adjacency assignments and world-aligned multiresolution sampling. The retained scalar graph remains separately defined; typed spatial functions have no per-cell initial-context input. Only explicit normalized `spatial:<id>` outputs may drive existing masks and mappings. GEN-004 / [#191](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/191) adds explicit schema-3 [hierarchical semantic plans](procedural-hierarchical-generation.md). Finite canonical regions own nested places and cross-chunk structures; stable rule/slot IDs, placement constraints, matched sockets, explicit loops/service trunks and final-raster route reports precede ordinary chunk publication. Selected immutable semantic geometries may feed the typed graph. The hierarchy does not add World streaming or replace final hard material authority. | Candidate | Generated structure | Suitable starting point | |---|---|---| | `strata` | Smoothly varying surface, domain-warped caves, strata, deposits and material-specific deep fill | Organic terrain, underground spaces and theme transitions | | `flow_network` | Strata plus a connected macrocell hub/port network, carved after structural modules | Interconnected passages, service routes and excavation networks | | `district_grammar` | Global room/floor lattice with repeated doors and accents, plus the same hub/port network | Dense urban interiors, industrial districts and structured construction | ![Actual native generation with the same authored controls across the three candidates](../figures/worldgen-candidates.png) Seed 314159; each panel covers 512 by 384 cells at origin `[-256,0]`. Reproduce the material pixels with `make worldgen-demo`. This is generation output, before simulation. Every candidate consumes the same brushes, paths, overrides and feature instances. A hard candidate override can choose another generator inside a rectangular zone. This is deliberately a set of provisional algorithms, not a selected production world style or a proof of useful player navigation. In particular, generator connectivity does not establish actor clearance, gravity traversal or fluid equilibrium; the existing material and actor owners retain those semantics. **Current authoring surface:** the separate [worldgen workbench](../../godot/worldgen_workbench.tscn) previews generated material pixels and performs bounded demand generation

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How are coordinate transforms composed?
`transform` samples its source in local coordinates. For local point `q`, world point `p`, origin `o`, translation `t`, rotation `R`, shear `H` and anisotropic scale `S`, the convention is: ```text p = o + t + R H S (q − o) q = o + (R H S)^−1 (p − o − t) H = [[1, shear_x], [shear_y, 1]] S = diag(sx, sy) ``` Positive angles use the ordinary coordinate rotation matrix. World y is the generator's downward-positive axis, so the on-screen visual interpretation follows that axis convention. Translation and origin are positions in cells; angles are radians. Nested transforms compose through explicit source inputs and are bounded by graph depth and recursive sampling work. `transform_vector` samples its vector source at the original point and applies the **forward linear part** `R H S`. It does not add translation or origin. Coordinate deformation of a vector field and transformation of its vector values are therefore separate operations an author may compose deliberately. The compiler rejects zero/tiny scales, singular shears, nonfinite parameters and excessive declared bounds. Translation, rotation/reflection and uniform scale preserve an exact SDF. A uniform scale multiplies the sampled distance by the absolute scale. Anisotropic scaling or shear preserves the zero set but changes the result to a general implicit scalar. Its reported minimum/maximum distance factors are the affine matrix's singular-value bounds: multiplying the absolute local distance by those factors bounds the world distance to the transformed boundary. General warps, polar maps and coarse interpolation discard an exact-distance claim. Do not use a warped scalar as an exact clearance radius. `repeat` subtracts its phase origin and maps each axis into local `[0,period)` using floor-equivalent remainder. `mirror` folds the phase-shifted, period-doubled axis into local `[0,period]`. Negative inputs and exact seams obey the same rules as positive inputs. These coordinate maps repeat a function; they do not imply that material routes connect across the repeated boundary. `polar` samples its source at `(radius/radial_scale, angle/angular_scale)`; `log_polar` replaces the first component with `log(max(radius,min_radius)/radial_scale)`. Both measure radius/angle relative to an explicit origin. Angle uses `atan2`, with angle zero at the origin; the negative-x, zero-y branch is positive pi. Radial/angular scales map physical radius/radians into the source's sampling coordinates. The logarithm's minimum-radius clamp and angle branch seam are explicit numerical conventions, independent of resident chunks. `warp` takes `[source, displacement_vector]`; the displacement is sampled at the original point and radially capped to `max_displacement` cells before resampling the source. Repeated composition is bounded; no neighbor-generation recursion is introduced. Public samples use integer world coordinates in `[-2^40,2^40)`. Internal transformed,

Section: Procedural world generation candidates > What is the control precedence?
The evaluation order is stable and independent of manifest array insertion order. IDs are required; duplicate IDs within a layer are rejected. For brushes, paths, modifiers and hard overrides, lower `priority` runs first, with lexical ID as the tie-break. Later values win. Moving an item in a JSON array is not a hidden priority control. | Order | Control | Meaning | |---|---|---| | 1 | Global parameters and resolved theme parameters | Establish the selected candidate's initial shape and palette distribution | | 2 | Broad polyline brushstrokes | Blend theme weights and selected shape parameters using radius, strength and falloff | | 3 | Hard parameter/candidate overrides | Assign exact values within a half-open world-space rectangle | | 4 | Initial raster and context | Capture the original proposed material, surface and route context before later changes | | 5 | Scalar fields and modifier influence | Evaluate the field DAG once and capture each modifier's application/exclusion/context/shape mask | | 6 | Masked theme and geometry guidance | Apply all theme blends; reblend theme/old brush parameters; apply direct edits and mappings; reapply hard geometry controls and rasterize | | 7 | Prepared feature modules | Add or carve structured zones in dependency order, clipped to bounds and optional field masks | | 8 | Masked material or aggregate modifiers | Use the original captured influence to select discrete existing material IDs | | 9 | Shared network and explicit guide paths | Reserve connective space after modules/modifiers; a guide may carve Empty or paint another material | | 10 | Hard material overrides | Force the final material, including intentionally blocking a route | Schema 3 inserts accepted semantic shell/interior/aggregate proposals between steps 6 and 7 and restores explicit semantic passages after step 9. Existing native modules and material modifiers can therefore contribute to semantic places, while final hard material overrides still win. The hierarchy's final-cell route report observes that complete stack and reports any blocked passage; it does not reinterpret a hard override as optional. Recipes without grammar retain the table's preceding behavior. The [field/modifier contract](procedural-generation-fields-and-modifiers.md) defines the two guidance stages, mapping endpoints and immutable context. No earlier modifier can change the context observed by a later modifier. Recipes without new controls retain their old material behavior; fixed legacy hashes cover all three candidates in four signed chunks. Brush points are world-space `[x,y]` pairs. A single point is a dab; multiple points form a polyline. Influence uses distance to the nearest segment, a smooth radial falloff raised

results.query: Which signs, spacing, units and edge behavior do procedural gradient, curl, ridge and level-set curvature use across chunk boundaries?
facts: Centered first derivatives use four axial immutable absolute-world samples with spacing 1..64 cells, not resident neighboring chunks.
Gradient reduces cell exponent by one; curl is dVy/dx-dVx/dy; slope is gradient magnitude and aspect uses signed atan2 radians.
Ridge/valley use positive negative/positive Laplacian; local extrema strictly compare four axial neighbors.
Curvature uses nine-point level-set derivatives, reciprocal-cell units and an explicit zero at zero gradient; nonlinear finite differences remain approximations.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > Which derivatives and geometric detectors are defined?
Spacing `h` is explicitly `1..64` cells. The first derivative uses centered differences, for example `(f(x+h,y)−f(x−h,y))/(2h)`. Second derivatives use the centered three-point form. The mixed derivative uses four diagonal samples. All positions are absolute-world coordinates of immutable functions. A chunk boundary is not a stencil boundary; it cannot substitute missing neighbor data or change the answer. | Operator | Numerical meaning | |---|---| | `gradient` | `(fx, fy)` with input unit exponent minus one | | `slope` | `hypot(fx,fy)`; nonnegative, same units as gradient | | `aspect` | `atan2(fy,fx)`, in signed radians; zero gradient has a finite zero convention | | `divergence` | `dVx/dx + dVy/dy` | | `curl` | Scalar `dVy/dx − dVx/dy`; positive sign is fixed by this formula | | `ridge`, `valley` | `max(0,−laplacian)` and `max(0,laplacian)`; input exponent minus two | | `local_minimum`, `local_maximum` | Strict comparison to the four axial samples, producing an exact boolean; a plateau is not a strict extremum | | `curvature` | Level-set curvature `(fxx*fy²−2*fxy*fx*fy+fyy*fx²)/hypot(fx,fy)^3`; zero at zero gradient, units `cells^-1` | Finite differences approximate nonlinear functions and discontinuities. The analytical regression uses quadratic scalar fields, radial circle distance and linear vector fields to establish values, signs and units independently. These operators detect properties of the authored function; they are not a fluid solver, a proof of physical traversability or exact geometry reconstruction.

Section: Procedural world generation candidates > Which fine parameters are available?
All positions, distances and widths below are measured in cells. Values must be finite. Out-of-range values are errors; the generator does not silently clamp the authored recipe. Spatial interpolation remains inside the endpoints' valid range. | JSON key | Default | Accepted range | Effect | |---|---:|---:|---| | `surface_y` | 96 | -1,000,000..1,000,000 | Mean Strata surface height, downward-positive | | `relief` | 48 | 0..4096 | Surface variation amplitude | | `feature_scale` | 96 | 8..4096 | Cave/terrain scale; global value also anchors palette patch scale | | `cave_threshold` | 0.60 | 0..1 | Higher values leave more solid terrain | | `strata_period` | 18 | 2..1024 | Spacing of potential deposit bands | | `warp` | 12 | 0..512 | Organic domain displacement amplitude | | `corridor_width` | 7 | 2..64 | Full width of shared connective routes | | `district_size` | 256 | Integer 64..2048 | Global macrocell topology size | | `room_size` | 48 | 12..256 | District room lattice spacing | | `wall_thickness` | 3 | 1..5 | District walls/floors | | `detail` | 0.32 | 0..1 | Accent/deposit preference | | `fluid_level` | 224 | -1,000,000..1,000,000 | Deep-cave fluid fill threshold | `district_size` is global-only. Theme, brush, modifier/mapping and hard spatial edits of it reject: varying a macrocell ownership grid across individual samples would break shared port ownership. Other hard controls can deliberately interrupt connectivity, so the resulting authored zone must be evaluated on its own terms. Integer room/wall rasterization has cell-sized steps even when the input editor accepts decimals. The default seed is 1 and chunk size is 128. Native seeds are unsigned 64-bit; Godot accepts nonnegative signed-64 values, while JSON numeric values are restricted to exactly representable integers through 2^53-1. Use modest numeric JSON seeds for portable profile roundtrips. `configure` owns its revision; `revision` is not an accepted user JSON field. Schema 1 retains generator algorithm 2 and its optional field/aggregate/modifier declarations. Schema 2 explicitly adds `spatial` and `spatial_limits`, using generator algorithm 3 and spatial algorithm 1. Legacy scalar semantics/material output remain independently tested; selecting schema 2 changes recipe/receipt identity deliberately.

Section: Procedural world generation candidates > How do chunks connect without generating neighbors?
Every field is sampled at global coordinates. Seeded lattice values depend on seed, coordinates and an algorithm lane, not a mutable PRNG sequence. Changing request order, slicing a job into different cell budgets, or partitioning the same region into different chunk sizes therefore leaves its material cells unchanged for the same effective recipe. Flow Network and District Grammar divide the plane into fixed macrocells. Each cell has a seeded interior hub. An edge's port is derived from a canonical edge coordinate and axis; its two owners independently obtain the same port. Each hub connects to all four edge ports. No recursive neighbor request, global graph construction, speculative edge negotiation or neighbor-residency check is needed. The shared skeleton is carved after feature modules and material modifiers so their ordinary walls do not seal it. An independent regression fills the region with solid Metal and requires a four-neighbor Empty component across a negative-coordinate 2x2 macrocell region to reach every outer side. The current guarantee is a deterministic raster connection in one unchanged recipe. It does not guarantee that independently edited recipes meet, that a large player fits every passage, or that a passage containing later simulation material remains traversable. Explicit hard material/candidate changes may alter connectivity by design. The workbench replaces its complete preview revision after an edit, avoiding a mixture of old and new generated chunks. Native World supports wider signed coordinates. This generator deliberately accepts only complete chunks inside `[-2^40,2^40)` cell coordinates: brush geometry uses doubles, and out-of-domain requests must refuse rather than alias distant positions. Negative coordinates use mathematical floor division. A job must fit the entire chunk in that domain before allocating its output.

results.query: Does the Peano spatial traversal make an infinite connected route, and how are Voronoi ties and Delaunay co-circular diagonals handled?
facts: Peano covers a finite 3^order square with order 1..12; its rank/inverse are bijective and successive ranks share an edge only inside that tile.
Repeated finite traversal does not imply connected physical routes between tiles.
Voronoi has one deterministically jittered seed per world lattice tile, a fixed 5x5 nearest search and lexicographic signed-coordinate ties.
Delaunay-derived adjacency is the positive-length Voronoi-face dual; zero-length co-circular diagonal edges are omitted.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > What do Peano, Voronoi, Delaunay and Poisson guarantee?
The Peano operator extends the retained finite Hilbert/Morton controls with a ternary square traversal. Side length is `3^order`, `order=1..12`; each local cell spans `cell_size=1..4096` world cells. Rank and inverse are bijections. Consecutive Peano ranks share an edge **inside one finite tile**. Signed tile addressing uses floor division. No infinite path or physical route is promised between independently repeated tiles; authored routes and the generator's shared-network controls retain that separate role. Voronoi seeds use one deterministically jittered point in each world-aligned lattice tile. `spacing` is `1..1,048,576` cells and `jitter` is `[0,1]`. A fixed 5×5 candidate search suffices for the nearest point because the containing tile always supplies a seed within `sqrt(2)*spacing`. Equal distances choose the lexicographically smaller signed seed coordinate. Region identity retains both seed coordinates and a stable graph domain; it does not pack an unbounded address into a floating-point number. `voronoi_distance` returns nearest-seed distance. `voronoi_boundary` measures distance to the nearest competing Voronoi boundary under its bounded 7×7 competitor search. `delaunay_degree` exposes the size of the positive-length Voronoi-face dual. The lower-level neighborhood API additionally returns incident neighbors/positions and distance to the owner's incident segments. Co-circular zero-length diagonal edges are deliberately omitted; a square lattice therefore has four face neighbors rather than an arbitrary triangulation diagonal. This is the documented Delaunay-derived structure. Poisson-style seeds use deterministic Matérn-II priority rejection. Each lattice tile owns one candidate. It survives only if no candidate within the authored radius has a lower `(priority, signed ID)` ordering. Rejected candidates still compete; acceptance never recursively asks whether a neighbor survived. Radius must be positive and no greater than twice the lattice spacing. Candidate ownership is half-open and independent of requested chunks. The query radius is `R=search_cells*spacing`, with `search_cells=1..4`. `poisson_found` reports whether an accepted seed lies strictly inside R. `poisson_distance` returns the nearest accepted distance capped at R. A `poisson_region` identity must be interpreted together with `poisson_found` when no candidate is found. This bounded selection gives hard minimum separation, not a guaranteed globally nearest seed, maximal packing or a measured blue-noise spectral guarantee.

The prototype supports square 256, 512 and 1024-cell compiler regions; ordinary Shared Workbench authoring uses 512 and 1024. Section: Hierarchical procedural places and structural routes > How are sockets, routes and finite curves used structurally?
A socket has an authored ID, route type, outward direction, integer edge offset, odd aperture width, required flag and attachment policy. Width and offset must fit the selected feature edge. Automatic attachment selects the nearest compatible predeclared regional route deterministically, checks passage width, creates an opposite-facing matching socket and an explicit connector that first exits along the authored normal. Shared boundary ports remain canonical records. Unsupported or unmatched required connections reject the plan. Hilbert, Morton and Peano are finite orderings of authored candidate addresses `order_x/order_y`. Their ranks affect candidate placement, progressive density and retained inspection/tour order. They can order declared district subdivisions or apparatus positions without array-order dependence. With `curve_services`, a bounded service tour visits finite curve sites in rank order and constructs explicit orthogonal material trunk edges between them, joined to the straight regional service. Hilbert/Morton use at most sixteen sites and Peano nine; a Morton jump is an authored L-shaped route, not an inferred adjacent step. Curve ranks never replace the explicit edge geometry used by hub arms, loops, utility trunks and socket connectors. Hilbert/Peano adjacency holds only inside their documented finite domains; Morton may jump. A sorted list of features alone is not a physical route.

results.query: How do Poisson-style procedural feature seeds stay deterministic across chunk edges without recursive neighbor generation, and what happens when no seed is found?
facts: One half-open lattice tile owns each candidate; deterministic Matern-II priority rejection compares all nearby candidates, including rejected candidates.
Acceptance uses bounded nonrecursive neighborhoods and radius greater than zero and no greater than twice spacing.
Query radius is search_cells*spacing with search_cells 1..4; found reports a seed strictly within that radius and distance is capped at the radius.
This does not promise maximal packing, a globally nearest seed outside the search radius or a measured blue-noise spectral property.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > What do Peano, Voronoi, Delaunay and Poisson guarantee?
The Peano operator extends the retained finite Hilbert/Morton controls with a ternary square traversal. Side length is `3^order`, `order=1..12`; each local cell spans `cell_size=1..4096` world cells. Rank and inverse are bijections. Consecutive Peano ranks share an edge **inside one finite tile**. Signed tile addressing uses floor division. No infinite path or physical route is promised between independently repeated tiles; authored routes and the generator's shared-network controls retain that separate role. Voronoi seeds use one deterministically jittered point in each world-aligned lattice tile. `spacing` is `1..1,048,576` cells and `jitter` is `[0,1]`. A fixed 5×5 candidate search suffices for the nearest point because the containing tile always supplies a seed within `sqrt(2)*spacing`. Equal distances choose the lexicographically smaller signed seed coordinate. Region identity retains both seed coordinates and a stable graph domain; it does not pack an unbounded address into a floating-point number. `voronoi_distance` returns nearest-seed distance. `voronoi_boundary` measures distance to the nearest competing Voronoi boundary under its bounded 7×7 competitor search. `delaunay_degree` exposes the size of the positive-length Voronoi-face dual. The lower-level neighborhood API additionally returns incident neighbors/positions and distance to the owner's incident segments. Co-circular zero-length diagonal edges are deliberately omitted; a square lattice therefore has four face neighbors rather than an arbitrary triangulation diagonal. This is the documented Delaunay-derived structure. Poisson-style seeds use deterministic Matérn-II priority rejection. Each lattice tile owns one candidate. It survives only if no candidate within the authored radius has a lower `(priority, signed ID)` ordering. Rejected candidates still compete; acceptance never recursively asks whether a neighbor survived. Radius must be positive and no greater than twice the lattice spacing. Candidate ownership is half-open and independent of requested chunks. The query radius is `R=search_cells*spacing`, with `search_cells=1..4`. `poisson_found` reports whether an accepted seed lies strictly inside R. `poisson_distance` returns the nearest accepted distance capped at R. A `poisson_region` identity must be interpreted together with `poisson_found` when no candidate is found. This bounded selection gives hard minimum separation, not a guaranteed globally nearest seed, maximal packing or a measured blue-noise spectral guarantee.

Section: Procedural world generation candidates > How do chunks connect without generating neighbors?
Every field is sampled at global coordinates. Seeded lattice values depend on seed, coordinates and an algorithm lane, not a mutable PRNG sequence. Changing request order, slicing a job into different cell budgets, or partitioning the same region into different chunk sizes therefore leaves its material cells unchanged for the same effective recipe. Flow Network and District Grammar divide the plane into fixed macrocells. Each cell has a seeded interior hub. An edge's port is derived from a canonical edge coordinate and axis; its two owners independently obtain the same port. Each hub connects to all four edge ports. No recursive neighbor request, global graph construction, speculative edge negotiation or neighbor-residency check is needed. The shared skeleton is carved after feature modules and material modifiers so their ordinary walls do not seal it. An independent regression fills the region with solid Metal and requires a four-neighbor Empty component across a negative-coordinate 2x2 macrocell region to reach every outer side. The current guarantee is a deterministic raster connection in one unchanged recipe. It does not guarantee that independently edited recipes meet, that a large player fits every passage, or that a passage containing later simulation material remains traversable. Explicit hard material/candidate changes may alter connectivity by design. The workbench replaces its complete preview revision after an edit, avoiding a mixture of old and new generated chunks. Native World supports wider signed coordinates. This generator deliberately accepts only complete chunks inside `[-2^40,2^40)` cell coordinates: brush geometry uses doubles, and out-of-domain requests must refuse rather than alias distant positions. Negative coordinates use mathematical floor division. A job must fit the entire chunk in that domain before allocating its output.

Derivative spacing is 1..64 cells and warp displacement 0..4096 cells. Exact category IDs retain integer components. Geometry has at most 256 points. Region assignment has at most 16×16 cells and 16 categories, a default 1,000,000-operation preparation budget, hard work ceiling 64,000,000 and fixed bounded solver scratch. Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How do multiresolution evaluation, caches and budgets behave?
Every node declares `sampling_scale` of 1, 4, 16 or 64 cells. The lattice is anchored at absolute world zero using mathematical floor, including negative positions. Continuous outputs use deterministic bilinear interpolation between the four coarse anchors. Categorical and boolean outputs select the nearest anchor exactly; an exact half tie selects the lower anchor on each axis. IDs and booleans are never numerically interpolated. Coarse distance interpolation loses exact-distance qualification. The caller-owned `SpatialScratch` contains 256 bounded cache entries. Keys bind the transitive node identity, exact double coordinate bits and sampling mode; the graph contains no mutable cache. Identity includes algorithm, operator, parameters, instance path/seed, inputs, referenced geometry/assignment and sampling scale. Warm, cold or evicted entries change work reuse, not results. Separate workers use separate scratch. In particular, no cache key needs a live World revision because the typed API has no World or per-cell context access. Numeric negative zero is canonicalized to positive zero in both identity and returned components, so sharing cached results between equivalent definitions cannot change their component bits. The numerical implementation uses ordinary C++ double arithmetic and standard transcendental functions. Exact equality is the supported deterministic guarantee for the same compiled numerical implementation under different request order, partitions, worker scratches, budget slices and cache states. Cross-platform bitwise equivalence of trigonometry/logarithms is not promised by this contract; Linux and Windows execution remain individually source-bound acceptance gates. The compiler accounts for recursive source sampling, derivative fan-out, coarse four-anchor sampling, every expanded declaration, seed neighborhoods, geometry segments and solver preparation. Declared work is conservative logical work, not wall-clock time or exact machine instructions; cache hits do not reduce the admission charge. Bounds and defaults are in the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#opt-in-procedural-generation-configuration). Successful evaluation uses fixed caller/stack scratch without per-cell heap growth. `evaluate` fills a private result before replacing the caller's output. Generation retains its private pending material/diagnostic arrays; cancellation or failure discards both payloads and their receipt hashes. A ready chunk is one complete result. Compilation, preparation and per-chunk rejection are not permission to expose a partially generated map.

results.query: Can a WFC-style finite region assignment guarantee adjacency between repeated tiles, and can an unsatisfiable or work-exhausted solver publish a partial layout?

Repeated tile seams have adjacency guarantees only on axes with explicit wrap constraints; GEN-004 reuses this field solver for hierarchical layout use.

Geometry inputs contain an ID, 1..256 finite points and a `closed` flag; a closed boundary requires at least three points. `geometry_distance` names one immutable input and returns Euclidean distance to its point, open polyline segments or closed boundary. Closed geometry measures the boundary; it does not silently become an inside/outside classifier. A single point and repeated points have bounded explicit segment handling. Geometry is copied/prepared before publication, and its actual coordinates enter the consuming node's identity. The accepted GEN-004 planner supplies routes and feature boundaries through this value interface: `Generator::compile` prepares exported geometry before compiling the spatial graph. The field implementation retains no dependency on grammar types or live World state. An assignment input declares a finite tile of at most 16×16 cells, up to 16 exact categories, four directional adjacency masks and optional per-cell domain masks. Opposite adjacency relations must be reciprocal. Deterministic propagation and bounded backtracking prepare the entire solution before a field can sample it. Unsatisfiable constraints and exhausted work are distinct explicit failures; neither exposes a partial assignment. `assigned_region` returns one exact category from the prepared tile. The tile repeats using floor addressing. `wrap_x`/`wrap_y` enable constraints across those tile edges; without a wrap constraint, adjacency is guaranteed only inside the finite tile. GEN-004 owns hierarchical layout use of this contract and should reuse this solver rather than introducing a conflicting field solver.

Section: ADR-013: Canonical semantic generation before rasterization > Decision
GEN-004 compiles immutable semantic plans in a finite, authored window of world-zero-anchored regions. A region owns its feature hierarchy; each feature's identity combines the authored world namespace, grid size, signed region address, parent path, rule ID and stable slot. Storage chunks only sample the plan. Shared boundary ports use canonical west/north ownership and keys independent of the compilation window. Neighbor generation and worker completion never negotiate which feature wins. Routine place construction is declarative. Bounded authored candidates and deterministic rule priority provide layout decisions, with explicit hard constraints, weighted preferences, rejection and authored omission receipts. GEN-003's finite assignment solver remains the single categorical adjacency solver. Trusted native modules remain an extension point within the established generation stack. The [hierarchy contract](../systems/procedural-hierarchical-generation.md) owns the executable vocabulary and precise scope. The planner supports region-contained buildings crossing storage chunks and explicit route/service structures crossing region boundaries. A `spatial` definition contains `nodes`, `subgraphs`, `instances`, `geometries` and `assignments`. A named subgraph declares typed parameters with optional defaults, local nodes, nested instances and named outputs. Instances supply typed literal `bindings`; nested instances may bind parameters from their enclosing subgraph. Numeric operator parameters can explicitly refer to a typed scalar parameter through `parameter_bindings`. The declared cell exponent must match the operator parameter: lengths, positions and sampling spacing use one; angles, affine scale factors, shears, jitter, salt and traversal order use zero. `to_mask` low/high bounds inherit the input field's exponent. Numeric bindings are not an escape from unit checking. A `parameter` node names its declaration with `reference` and may select a sampling scale; its type, units and value come from the declaration/binding, so ignored node-level overrides reject. Local IDs allow letters, digits, hyphen and underscore. Dot is reserved for expanded namespaces. An output named `mask` in instance `decay` is `decay.mask`; a nested instance adds another namespace component. The compiler rejects duplicate IDs, node/instance/output collisions, unknown bindings, missing required inputs, wrong types, dependency cycles and recursive expansion. Unused declarations are validated too. Root graph nodes may consume an expanded output by its full name. The definition admits at most 16 subgraphs, root instances, geometry inputs and assignments per family. Each subgraph admits at most 16 parameters, nested instances and named outputs; nesting depth is at most eight. Expansion shares a hard 1,024-instance-call ledger across actual and unused-template validation, so even a tree of empty subgraphs has bounded work. Every expansion call costs 512 preparation units and every expanded node costs 8,192, in addition to declaration validation and geometry/solver preparation. Stable instance paths derive deterministic seed domains from the recipe seed. Reordering declaration arrays does not alter meaning. A parameter edit changes the consuming node and its transitive consumers; unrelated instance/node identities remain reusable. Compiled inputs are immutable owned values, so editing the author's definition cannot mutate a retained graph or pending job.

Section: Typed spatial fields, transforms and reusable generation graphs > How do multiresolution evaluation, caches and budgets behave?
Every node declares `sampling_scale` of 1, 4, 16 or 64 cells. The lattice is anchored at absolute world zero using mathematical floor, including negative positions. Continuous outputs use deterministic bilinear interpolation between the four coarse anchors. Categorical and boolean outputs select the nearest anchor exactly; an exact half tie selects the lower anchor on each axis. IDs and booleans are never numerically interpolated. Coarse distance interpolation loses exact-distance qualification. The caller-owned `SpatialScratch` contains 256 bounded cache entries. Keys bind the transitive node identity, exact double coordinate bits and sampling mode; the graph contains no mutable cache. Identity includes algorithm, operator, parameters, instance path/seed, inputs, referenced geometry/assignment and sampling scale. Warm, cold or evicted entries change work reuse, not results. Separate workers use separate scratch. In particular, no cache key needs a live World revision because the typed API has no World or per-cell context access. Numeric negative zero is canonicalized to positive zero in both identity and returned components, so sharing cached results between equivalent definitions cannot change their component bits. The numerical implementation uses ordinary C++ double arithmetic and standard transcendental functions. Exact equality is the supported deterministic guarantee for the same compiled numerical implementation under different request order, partitions, worker scratches, budget slices and cache states. Cross-platform bitwise equivalence of trigonometry/logarithms is not promised by this contract; Linux and Windows execution remain individually source-bound acceptance gates. The compiler accounts for recursive source sampling, derivative fan-out, coarse four-anchor sampling, every expanded declaration, seed neighborhoods, geometry segments and solver preparation. Declared work is conservative logical work, not wall-clock time or exact machine instructions; cache hits do not reduce the admission charge. Bounds and defaults are in the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration-reference.md#opt-in-procedural-generation-configuration). Successful evaluation uses fixed caller/stack scratch without per-cell heap growth. `evaluate` fills a private result before replacing the caller's output. Generation retains its private pending material/diagnostic arrays; cancellation or failure discards both payloads and their receipt hashes. A ready chunk is one complete result. Compilation, preparation and per-chunk rejection are not permission to expose a partially generated map.
