Section: Atlas agent runner (MAP-AUTO-02, [#499](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/499)) > Security model
Enforced in code, not only in the prompt: - **Disposable workspace.** Only the approved read set is copied (the collection, the instruction files, the pinned support files its validators read). The source checkout is never written; changes leave as a patch. - **Path custody.** Model-supplied paths are normalised and rejected for traversal, absolute or drive paths, backslashes, NULs, ADS/reserved names, symlinks/junctions in any component, hard-linked write targets and a deny list; reads/writes must match explicit globs. Writable files are `pack.json` and `README.md` of the lane's own collection only; validators, render scripts and instructions are read-only. `preview.svg` changes only by the collection's own render script. - **No shell.** Processes run only through fixed argument vectors for three kinds (`validate`, `render_check`, `render_write`), with an allowlisted interpreter, a scrubbed environment (no API key), working-directory pinning, time limits with process-tree kill and output caps. A run that changes any unassigned file is a violation. - **Lane ownership.** Terrain Art = 001-005, Ruin Detail = 006-010, Art Curation = 011-015. A lane may write only its own collections; any other collection is read-only critique and the edit tool is not offered. - **Secrets.** Credentials never enter model context, tool output, logs or receipts (pattern and exact-value redaction; a receipt containing credential-shaped text is withheld). - **Source identity.** `expected_source_sha` must be a full SHA and equal HEAD; the source hashes and HEAD are re-checked after the run and a competing change blocks the patch. Receipts record the repository HEAD and the SHA-256 of every file read. - **Publication** is separate and off by default. `atlas_agent_runner.py publish` re-checks that upstream HEAD still equals the SHA the patch was made from, that only the lane's own files change and only as modifications, and that the branch name is a **new** `atlas-agent/*` name (local and remote); then it commits to that branch. It never changes the base branch or merges. An optional `--push` uses a create-only lease and refuses an existing remote branch. Publication is a separate operator-authorized action; the Actions workflow has no write access.

Every attempt (including each retry) first **reserves** a conservative worst case: the estimated input tokens (pessimistic bytes-per-token plus the published worst-case image tokens) at the uncached rate plus `max_output_tokens` at the output rate. The reservation must fit the per-call ceiling, the per-run ceiling and (live) the authorised ceiling. After the response the reported usage (including cached and reasoning tokens) is priced and reconciled; reported usage above the reservation stops the run. Timeouts, 5xx and dropped connections keep their reservation as **possibly charged**; 429s and rejected requests are released. A 429 that mentions quota, billing, credit or a hard spend limit is treated as exhausted credit and is not retried. The runner accounts for HTTP 429 rate-limit rejections separately: they do **not** consume `max_api_calls`; they are bounded by `max_retries` per call, `max_total_retries` per run (default 30) and the run time, and are reported separately as `usage.rate_limited_attempts` (`api_attempts` counts every request). Prompts above the runner's configured 272K-token short-context threshold are refused (`long_context_pricing_not_modelled`) because long-context rates are not modelled. Each `render_capture` writes a fresh bundle (`captures/after`, `after-2`, ...) and clears the previous comparison, so a model may refine and re-render several times; only a comparison of the latest render can support a cycle claim. One command (or one manual GitHub Actions run) starts a small robot that works on **one** Atlas collection. 1. Launch the desktop feature launcher and choose **Development workbench** (or use the launcher's `--workbench` argument). There is no new game scene. 2. Click **New from generator…**. Choose the native GEN-007 JSON profile (`gen007-deepworks` is initially selected), deterministic integer seed, global source X/Y and a finite 512², 1024² or, where the native recipe and capacity admit it, 2048² local canvas. 3. Click **Generate preview**. The dialog uses the native generator, not an image-to-rectangle rasterizer. The progress text identifies generated native cells, chunk count or semantic-plane work. Only the native final **play** material plane enters the simulation. The other semantic planes remain authoring-only; scripts/fixtures/effects are not activated. 4. Inspect the material preview; **Install into workbench** confirms replacement. The existing starting map is preserved if generation, source checking or native preparation refuses. Save any unsaved current work *before* confirming a replacement. Close the dialog to cancel its incremental generation. The first popup and saved-load popup are bounded to the embedded viewport or native screen usable area. On smaller windows the content scrolls; **Install** and **Keep current map** remain outside the scrolling content. 5. Use **Place model / Place at X/Y**, the existing **Pilot** selector, **Play / Pause**, **Step**, free/follow/overview camera, **Brush**, and left/right painting/erasure. A saved start records actor spawn and the authored ordered brush marks, not the live evolved native state. 6. In the painting row, enter a valid name and click **Save start [Ctrl+S]**. The existing `user://workbench/setup-<name>.json` is atomically replaced with the versioned generated-map manifest, only after the complete bounded JSON and material source have been checked. 7. Close Godot. Start it in a **new process**, select Shared Workbench, enter that name and click **Load start**. The same dialog re-generates the original native play-plane with the saved exact recipe, verifies all source identities and material SHA-256 before installing the stored actors, liquid settings, ordered manual erasures and overpainting. Section: Getting started with CyberSand > Your first screen
Choose **Development workbench — blank canvas, flyer fleet, materials and solver controls**. Other launcher entries open their own sessions. In the Workbench: | Control | Purpose | | --- | --- | | **Play / Pause [P]**, **Step [.]** | Run or pause; request one step while paused. | | **New blank** | Replace the authored scene with a blank starting canvas. Save first. | | **New from generator…** | Prepare a native preview; installation is a separate confirmation. | | **Free camera / Follow selected / Overview** | Select the view; wheel zooms and middle-drag pans. | | **Materials Lab…**, **Water Lab…**, **Art batches** | Open the corresponding authoring or inspection interface. | | **Save start [Ctrl+S] / Load start** | Save and reconstruct an authored start using the adjacent name field. | | **Menu [F2]** | Close this session and return to the launcher. | Text fields keep keyboard focus. Section: EXPLORE-001 — GEN-007 → Playable Workbench > Qualification commands (run against a **source-matched** native runtime)
Run from the selected current source with the exact pinned Godot, godot-cpp and Rapier identities and a source-matched materialized or rebuilt native extension. Follow [local validation](../operations/local-build-and-validation.md) for isolated profiles, import and provenance checks. An old candidate branch is not required to use the accepted feature. A library whose source-input hashes do not match cannot qualify these native interfaces. Use the same disposable profile for both processes of a save/reopen pair, separate from valued saves. Linux (in a suitable graphical environment): ```bash godot --path godot --script res://tests/test_explore001_generated_workbench.gd CYBERSAND_EXPLORE_REOPEN=1 godot --path godot --script res://tests/test_explore001_generated_workbench.gd godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_workbench_canvas.gd godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_worldgen_planes.gd ``` PowerShell (replace the executable with the pinned Godot 4.7 console binary): ```powershell $godot = 'C:\\path\\to\\Godot_v4.7-stable_win64_console.exe' & $godot --path .\\godot --script res://tests/test_explore001_generated_workbench.gd $env:CYBERSAND_EXPLORE_REOPEN='1' & $godot --path .\\godot --script res://tests/test_explore001_generated_workbench.gd Remove-Item Env:\\CYBERSAND_EXPLORE_REOPEN & $godot --path .\\godot -- --workbench ``` The first test process writes the named map to Godot's `user://` directory. The second checks reconstruction from the fresh process, after engine teardown. For original renderer frames, set `CYBERSAND_EXPLORE_CAPTURE` to an output directory. Keep that directory, native logs, runtime hashes and source commit with the PR evidence. The script performs direct play-plane readback, actual shared-owner installation, native ticks, a selected flyer, brush/erase, native failure refusals and save/reopen. A human desktop session must separately check movement feel, camera, collisions and physical traversal. The ordinary regression planner discovers the self-contained generated-map test; the source-built qualification workflows additionally execute its fresh-process phase using `CYBERSAND_EXPLORE_REOPEN=1`. Temporary admission/reopen diagnostics and old-artifact Windows replay have been retired; their source and first-failure logs remain historical evidence. The Windows source-built workflow retains a pristine desktop bundle with `Open Workbench.cmd` and a complete payload manifest. The six `test_explore001_dialog*_render.gd` cases are independent fresh-process graphical regressions for embedded/native first-open geometry, 1280×720 and 1920×1080 parent windows, first saved-load opening, resizing and content scrolling. They check both action buttons and retain original frames. Native windows use the real display's usable bounds; a smaller parent is not a simulated smaller physical monitor. These are geometry tests, not human camera/traversal acceptance.

hits.heading: Generated-map desktop playtest > Manual acceptance procedure
hits.text: Document: Generated-map desktop playtest Path: operations/explore001-desktop-playtest.md authority: current-documentation document-kind: guide status: Current scope: Accepted generated-map Workbench workflow and manual desktop validation, separate from hosted automation canonical-for: [explore001-desktop-playtest] last-reviewed: 2026-11-24 Section: Generated-map desktop playtest > Manual acceptance procedure 1. In Shared Workbench click **New from generator…**, select **gen007-deepworks**, seed **19337**, source origin **0,0**, size **1024**. Generate a preview, inspect its materials, and explicitly install it. On the very first opening, verify both bottom action buttons are on screen. Resize the window and scroll the contents; action buttons should stay visible. 2. Select an existing flyer such as **Midge**, place it in clear terrain, select it under **Pilot**, then press **Play**. Test the displayed movement controls (W/A/S/D for the flyer). Check contact with solid terrain and passage through open routes. Record any stuck actor, unexpected collision or movement issue. 3. Switch the existing free/follow/overview camera controls; pan and zoom. Check that input remains usable and the flyer stays observable. Hosted headless success does not establish camera or movement feel. 4. Pause and use the existing brush to add a solid wall and erase an opening. Resume and check the flyer contacts the new wall and passes through the erased opening. Paint Water; observe motion and flyer interaction without assuming pressure equivalence or a new Water law. 5. Preview another ordinary chunk profile twice, change size, and cancel a partial preview. Check that complete previews contain consistent terrain and cancellation keeps the installed map. Install a completed preview if desired. 6. In the painting row, enter a unique name and click **Save start [Ctrl+S]**. Record source/seed/region, spawn, selected flyer, paint marks and erased opening. Close Godot completely and relaunch through the same checked launcher. 7. Enter the same name and **Load start**. Let native regeneration finish; confirm authored terrain, ordered edits, actor spawn and selection, then continue painting and save again. Close/reopen once more if reporting a bug. 8. Repeat a bounded 512 test and, if resources permit, a 2048 test. Large preparation temporarily retains old and candidate Worlds plus copied grids; measure pauses/memory rather than inferring low cost from bounded size. Report candidate source commit, Windows/GPU, size/profile/seed/origin, exact steps, expected/observed behavior, saved start and original screenshot/log where useful. Report whether the steps were performed by a person, automation or source inspection. Accepted implementation and package qualification do not assert that a particular owner has performed this physical playtest. Original [8 November candidate evidence](../audits/2026-11-08-explore001-integration-qa.md) retains its dated source/runtime scope. The original launch heading remains a compatibility destination. Use the current procedure above; [baseline candidate text](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/00cdb02f103265b6dc5224c68283e9a0c8cb449f/docs/operations/explore001-desktop-playtest.md) preserves the earlier package-specific instructions.

Section: EXPLORE-001 — GEN-007 → Playable Workbench > Ordinary workbench workflow > Authoring and reopen
1. Launch the desktop feature launcher and choose **Development workbench** (or use the launcher's `--workbench` argument). There is no new game scene. 2. Click **New from generator…**. Choose the native GEN-007 JSON profile (`gen007-deepworks` is initially selected), deterministic integer seed, global source X/Y and a finite 512², 1024² or, where the native recipe and capacity admit it, 2048² local canvas. 3. Click **Generate preview**. The dialog uses the native generator, not an image-to-rectangle rasterizer. The progress text identifies generated native cells, chunk count or semantic-plane work. Only the native final **play** material plane enters the simulation. The other semantic planes remain authoring-only; scripts/fixtures/effects are not activated. 4. Inspect the material preview; **Install into workbench** confirms replacement. The existing starting map is preserved if generation, source checking or native preparation refuses. Save any unsaved current work *before* confirming a replacement. Close the dialog to cancel its incremental generation. The first popup and saved-load popup are bounded to the embedded viewport or native screen usable area. On smaller windows the content scrolls; **Install** and **Keep current map** remain outside the scrolling content. 5. Use **Place model / Place at X/Y**, the existing **Pilot** selector, **Play / Pause**, **Step**, free/follow/overview camera, **Brush**, and left/right painting/erasure. A saved start records actor spawn and the authored ordered brush marks, not the live evolved native state. 6. In the painting row, enter a valid name and click **Save start [Ctrl+S]**. The existing `user://workbench/setup-<name>.json` is atomically replaced with the versioned generated-map manifest, only after the complete bounded JSON and material source have been checked. 7. Close Godot. Start it in a **new process**, select Shared Workbench, enter that name and click **Load start**. The same dialog re-generates the original native play-plane with the saved exact recipe, verifies all source identities and material SHA-256 before installing the stored actors, liquid settings, ordered manual erasures and overpainting. It refuses incompatible revisions or different generated bytes **without altering the old World**.

hits.heading: EXPLORE-001 — GEN-007 → Playable Workbench > Ordinary workbench workflow > Explicit first-version limits
hits.text: Document: EXPLORE-001 generated playable starting maps Path: systems/explore001-generated-playable-maps.md authority: current-documentation document-kind: contract status: Current scope: GEN-007 final play plane to existing prepared finite shared-workbench World canonical-for: [generated-playable-map-admission, generated-playable-map-persistence] last-reviewed: 2026-11-24 Section: EXPLORE-001 — GEN-007 → Playable Workbench > Ordinary workbench workflow > Explicit first-version limits - Finite dimension 512, 1024 or 2048 on each side (square maps in the dialog); nonnegative destination coordinates, bounded global source range. - Current Workbench setup allows up to **32,768** ordered starting stamps or construction rectangles, subject to the 1 MiB envelope and native capability readback. The ordinary non-Workbench MicroScenario bound remains 4096. Generated baseline detail is **not** converted into those records. Native replay work is separately bounded to the smaller of 64×canvas cells and 32,000,000 attempted cells. Refusal preserves the prior document. [Flatten / Bake History](../operations/workbench-saving.md) can explicitly replace construction history with a stored material baseline; it is not automatic compaction or exact physical-state capture. - Source recipe document ≤1 MiB; saved manifest ≤1 MiB. Neither manifest includes the original million-cell material array. - Native semantic planes other than `play` do not become physical materials. Routine generator creation requires no editing JSON; custom files can be selected with **Choose profile file…**. - Setup-v2 names without generated manifest `format` retain their old reader. Material-baseline-v1 has its own reader. Old #402/#409 branch-format proposals are not additional current readers merely because the issue numbers appear in earlier integration notes. - A 2048² chunk profile requires up to 1024 receipts at aligned 64-cell chunks; region/profile capacity still applies. Deepworks' declared semantic plan is 1024², so a 2048² request is refused while preserving the installed map. Chunked previews now preflight the *exact* global source-chunk count, including unaligned origins, against the saved-map provenance limit of 1024 receipts. For example, a 512² request at eight-cell chunks needs 4096 receipts and is refused before allocating preview bytes or generating any source chunks; the installed native World remains unchanged. A 2048² aligned region at 64-cell chunks fits exactly 1024 receipts, but still needs its normal native, memory and source admission checks. Source material storage is one byte per cell (4 MiB at 2048²) and the preview is four bytes per cell (16 MiB); prepared/old Worlds and other staging memory coexist. Those buffer bounds are not a total-memory or responsiveness claim.

hits.heading: Procedural world generation candidates > How do chunks connect without generating neighbors?
hits.text:
Document: Procedural world generation candidates
Path: systems/procedural-world-generation.md
authority: current-documentation
document-kind: contract
status: Current
scope: Accepted native procedural proposals, schemas 1–4, theme and field guidance, trusted feature modules, bounded jobs, fresh chunk admission and isolated Godot preview
canonical-for: [procedural-chunk-generation, generation-theme-authoring, generation-module-contract]
last-reviewed: 2026-11-24
Section: Procedural world generation candidates > How do chunks connect without generating neighbors?
Every field is sampled at global coordinates. Seeded lattice values depend on seed, coordinates and an algorithm lane, not a mutable PRNG sequence. Changing request order, slicing a job into different cell budgets, or partitioning the same region into different chunk sizes therefore leaves its material cells unchanged for the same effective recipe. Flow Network and District Grammar divide the plane into fixed macrocells. Each cell has a seeded interior hub. An edge's port is derived from a canonical edge coordinate and axis; its two owners independently obtain the same port. Each hub connects to all four edge ports. No recursive neighbor request, global graph construction, speculative edge negotiation or neighbor-residency check is needed. The shared skeleton is carved after feature modules and material modifiers so their ordinary walls do not seal it. An independent regression fills the region with solid Metal and requires a four-neighbor Empty component across a negative-coordinate 2x2 macrocell region to reach every outer side. The current guarantee is a deterministic raster connection in one unchanged recipe. It does not guarantee that independently edited recipes meet, that a large player fits every passage, or that a passage containing later simulation material remains traversable. Explicit hard material/candidate changes may alter connectivity by design. The workbench replaces its complete preview revision after an edit, avoiding a mixture of old and new generated chunks. Native World supports wider signed coordinates. This generator deliberately accepts only complete chunks inside `[-2^40,2^40)` cell coordinates: brush geometry uses doubles, and out-of-domain requests must refuse rather than alias distant positions. Negative coordinates use mathematical floor division. A job must fit the entire chunk in that domain before allocating its output.

Section: Generation Workbench 2 inspection and transactional authoring > What is the current scope?
**Current implementation, GEN-007 / #193:** the opt-in [workbench](../../godot/scripts/worldgen_workbench.gd) edits the same native GEN-001/002/003/004/005 recipe consumed by production generation APIs. Its [tool controller](../../godot/scripts/worldgen_workbench_tools.gd) supplies the graph, hierarchy, replay inspector, plane/stage selection, seed cards and comparison. Its [preview](../../godot/scripts/worldgen_preview.gd) consumes copied native cells, typed diagnostics and semantic records. No second procedural algorithm, mutable World access or simulation tick is used to explain a preview. Choose **World generation workbench — terrain authoring preview** in the desktop feature launcher, or launch its scene directly from the repository root with the [pinned Godot runtime](../operations/getting-started.md): ```sh godot --path godot res://worldgen_workbench.tscn ``` This standalone editor owns a generation preview. To generate a playable layout in the ordinary Shared Workbench, use that host's **New from generator** and the [architectural authoring guide](../operations/architectural-generator-playtest.md). The preview's **Profile JSON… → Save accepted…** writes the accepted generation recipe, not a running World's material or physical state. **Load JSON…** reads a file into the editor; select **Apply JSON** to validate and accept it. Save the accepted recipe before **F2** closes this editor; its Undo/Redo history is session-local. The separate [procedural qualification scene](../operations/procedural-qualification.md) exercises a complete 1024 × 1024 four-plane place. The workbench itself uses a bounded movable viewport; it does not keep an unlimited world or trace history. Execution and visual acceptance are recorded in the [dated ledger](../audits/2026-10-21-gen007-workbench-qualification.md), separately from source feature availability. Runtime residency and persistence remain GEN-006.

Preview another ordinary chunk profile twice, change size, and cancel a partial preview. Check that complete previews contain consistent terrain and cancellation keeps the installed map. Install a completed preview if desired. 6. In the painting row, enter a unique name and click **Save start [Ctrl+S]**. Record source/seed/region, spawn, selected flyer, paint marks and erased opening. Close Godot completely and relaunch through the same checked launcher. 7. Enter the same name and **Load start**. Let native regeneration finish; confirm authored terrain, ordered edits, actor spawn and selection, then continue painting and save again. Close/reopen once more if reporting a bug. 8. Repeat a bounded 512 test and, if resources permit, a 2048 test. Large preparation temporarily retains old and candidate Worlds plus copied grids; measure pauses/memory rather than inferring low cost from bounded size. Report candidate source commit, Windows/GPU, size/profile/seed/origin, exact steps, expected/observed behavior, saved start and original screenshot/log where useful. Report whether the steps were performed by a person, automation or source inspection. Accepted implementation and package qualification do not assert that a particular owner has performed this physical playtest. Original [8 November candidate evidence](../audits/2026-11-08-explore001-integration-qa.md) retains its dated source/runtime scope. The original launch heading remains a compatibility destination. Use the current procedure above; [baseline candidate text](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/00cdb02f103265b6dc5224c68283e9a0c8cb449f/docs/operations/explore001-desktop-playtest.md) preserves the earlier package-specific instructions.

The ordinary regression planner discovers the self-contained generated-map test; the source-built qualification workflows additionally execute its fresh-process phase using `CYBERSAND_EXPLORE_REOPEN=1`. The Windows source-built workflow retains a pristine desktop bundle with `Open Workbench.cmd` and a complete payload manifest. The six `test_explore001_dialog*_render.gd` cases are independent fresh-process graphical regressions for embedded/native first-open geometry, 1280×720 and 1920×1080 parent windows, first saved-load opening, resizing and content scrolling. Section: GENTEK 80 — Windows evaluation > Test It
1. Generate **Suspended Deck**, seed 605, default geometry at 512². Inspect both hanger-to-carrier contacts. Reseed to 1701 and return to 605; the original output should return exactly. 2. Generate **Rib Vault**, then try bay 48 / floor 128 / wall 1. Inspect the steep ribs at close zoom. Restore default geometry before comparing another style. Also inspect **Scalloped Vault** at bay 48 / floor 64 / wall 2: each of its three small arches should have a continuous rib. **Ring Pier** should retain an empty diamond centre with stems touching both decks. **Tripod Frame** should connect successive tiers through its transfer decks, and **Cascade Terrace** should join its staggered platforms to a continuous rear core. With windows enabled, **Suspended Deck** and **Buttress Wall** should have framed panes without glass replacing the structural piers. 3. Generate **Interlaced Viaduct**, then **Rosework Gatehouse**, then one of the other advanced showcases at 1024². Compare silhouettes and intended voids; use the window/door switches individually to identify their actual effects. 4. Install a chosen map. Keep it paused, paint a visible Reinforced Concrete stroke and erase through another wall. Use **Step** or briefly **Play** to confirm the ordinary material World runs, then pause again. 5. Save a distinct named start. Exit Godot completely, relaunch the same source launcher or **Open Workbench.cmd**, and load that name. Confirm the same generated start and ordered paint/erase edits return. The save describes the authored start, not an arbitrary evolved simulation snapshot. 6. Open a new proposal with different settings, then **Stop preview**. The currently installed World must remain usable. Try an invalid share total or an impossible dimension; refusal must retain the existing World. 7. Try a five-style composition and a sparse selection using cards 1, 3 and 5. Check the per-style zone colours, names and shares, then save/reopen it. Record the package's source SHA, selected styles, seed, dimensions, Windows/display settings and any observed fault. Automated Windows graphical checks and PNGs do not replace the owner's physical NVIDIA/Firefox-machine assessment. No merge, Ready promotion or auto-merge is authorized by this guide.

results.query: How do desktop human agent and remote workbenches share authored baselines and edits, and how does Save differ from material-only Flatten?
facts: Approved convergence shares native authority, baseline reconstruction, acknowledged edits and persistence; interface permissions and budgets may differ.

Generated-start v1 reconstructs the authored start. GEN-008 captures current stored IDs into a uint16 little-endian standalone baseline, discards old reconstruction/history dependencies, preserves the same live World/tick/physics, and does not Save automatically.

Existing Setup-v2 and generated-start v1 remain supported. Standalone material-baseline v1 is bounded, integrity-checked and atomically saved; no physical checkpoint or Undo Flatten is promised. The earlier reset/respawn proposal was withdrawn on 11 November 2026.

The integration join verifies acknowledged human and agent edits after fresh-process load, stale proposal refusal after World replacement, and an independent authoring-generation fence when Flatten leaves native generation/revision/tick unchanged.

Section: Shared workbench authoring data and convergence > Flatten and storage compatibility > Recovery after a native owner fault
A failed native owner cannot be captured or edited. Its already acknowledged authored document remains independent of the quarantined live World. Explicit **Save start** may persist that retained document, including an unsaved flattened baseline and subsequent acknowledged edits, once all edit and replacement work has settled. Save does not read current native cells, attempt another Flatten, reset the World, clear the fault or create a simulation checkpoint. This recovery route bypasses only the general failed-owner admission refusal. Queued/executing edits, unconsumed native completion receipts, agent/manual queues, prepared replacements, pending Flatten and a partial-edit Save hold still refuse Save. The editor and worker fences are checked again after polling agent completions, so polling cannot admit new work through an earlier check. A refusal does not discard the retained baseline/history or change valid saves. After native failure, Save also conservatively refuses **any four-field legacy disc recipe** in `applied.edits`. Those intended brush instructions have no individual native acknowledgement, so their execution cannot be confirmed from the failed owner. The refusal preserves the complete authored document. A retained flattened baseline with acknowledged five-field PAINT/Art overlays remains eligible once the other guards settle. This restriction applies only after owner failure; healthy Save behavior and the Setup-v2/generated-start-v1 readers are unchanged. After a successful Save, completely exit the application, restart and **Load start** into a fresh native owner. Load reconstructs the saved material baseline, acknowledged overlays and supported actor/configuration state with normal initial physics. Runtime changes since Flatten remain outside that authored document. Failed-owner **Reset / R** and **Restore start** remain refused for generated or flattened starts because their legacy recipe-only recovery route cannot preserve those baselines; the refusal directs the user to Save, restart and Load. Recovery does not promise to turn unacknowledged or partial work into a saved edit.

Section: Flatten / Bake History evaluation > What Flatten does
**Flatten / Bake History…** makes the current native stored material layout the new authored baseline and retires earlier construction instructions and Undo/Redo history. The same live native World, tick, fluid quantities, temperatures, velocities and physical actors continue unchanged. Empty and every currently supported material ID use a complete row-major unsigned 16-bit little-endian plane. Flatten does not Save. New acknowledged paint and agent edits are recorded relative to that baseline. **Save start [Ctrl+S]** later saves the material baseline and those edits. Simulation after Flatten is excluded unless another explicit Flatten captures it. Reopening constructs ordinary initial material and actor state; the file is not a simulation checkpoint. For example, Plant reloads with ordinary initialized state; a captured Plant material ID does not preserve its previous energy or growth state. Existing Setup-v2 and generated-start-v1 files retain their original readers and meanings. The confirmation identifies the discarded history. While capture is pending, the same compact control offers **Cancel Flatten**. Pending human or agent work must finish or be stopped and acknowledged before Flatten. Refusal/cancellation leaves the prior authored start and existing saves intact. Retry after the reported owner operation settles; an incomplete capture never becomes the new baseline.

Section: Shared workbench authoring data and convergence > Common authored document semantics
The accepted [WB-ACTOR-COMPOSE-001 implementation](../systems/workbench-actor-composition.md#authored-data-options-and-compatibility) adds an optional versioned actor-control extension within existing Setup-v2, generated-start and material-baseline containers. Source, bounded cadence, starting equipment and compatible tuning are authored values. Live policy memory, leases, issued observations, resource consumption, momentum and evolved cells are not serialized by ordinary Save. Invalid definitions or controls refuse the complete preparation while retaining the previous applied map and session. **Approved requirements for convergence:** | Part | Meaning | |---|---| | Baseline | Starting terrain supplied by existing ordinary setup, verified procedural reconstruction, or a versioned standalone material baseline | | Authored changes | Ordered accepted edits after the baseline, including erase/replacement semantics; both human and agent changes must survive Save/reopen | | Actors and configuration | Supported authored spawns, selection and applicable response/liquid/material policy; view metadata is separate from material content | | Live session | Evolving native cells, tick, motion, active tasks and transient physics; not implicitly serialized by a starting-map Save | | Provenance | Reconstruction-critical identity where required; descriptive origin/history must be distinguishable from required inputs | These are semantic components, not mandated JSON keys or an unbounded operation journal. Existing bounds remain enforced. Exhaustion must be explicit and must not silently omit an accepted edit from the saved start. Ordinary Save persists the authored start; Restore reconstructs it. Neither implicitly captures evolved materials or promises deterministic coupled simulation replay. **Approved:** use shared reconstruction/validation, native preparation/adoption and authored-state recording services rather than interface-specific copies. Native C++ remains authoritative; the existing worker owns installed cells. Godot owns UI/input and main-thread scene/Rapier objects. Immutable copied snapshots retain their existing lifetime. Remote adapters do not simulate cells. An accepted queue entry is not proof of native application or durable recording; exact-cell authoring uses acknowledged application and explicit capacity/failure outcomes in the native PAINT/direct-Art paths. The live disc brush has its own bounded authored-stamp recording; it is not a paused before/after transaction and does not acquire paused Undo/Redo merely because its queue accepts a sample.
